## F225: gov/control_profiles.py shares one mutable evidence snapshot across all controls -- cross-control contamination (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-258 lane 4 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w258_redteam_probes.py` (probe `profiles/cross-control-snapshot-contamination`).

**Defect:** `run_profile()` deep-copies the evidence snapshot ONCE and passes the SAME object to every control's check. A check that mutates the snapshot (adds/removes keys) changes what subsequent controls evaluate: the battery probe shows check C0 writing `snap["poisoned"] = True` and check C1 observing it. The module's stated contract ("caller data is never mutated", F212 lesson) holds for the CALLER, but checks are not isolated from each other. Under check composition from multiple sources -- the InSpec pattern this module adapts explicitly supports vendored control packs -- one compromised or malicious check can poison the evidence view of every later control in the profile, flipping their verdicts, while the profile digest stays valid and the emitted compliance artifact looks legitimate. Per-control isolation is cheap: the module already deep-copies once.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. All checks are supplied by the profile author at runtime; with all-first-party checks there is no exposure (a malicious check author can already write a directly-lying check). The exposure appears only when a profile composes checks from an untrusted or compromised source alongside victim checks -- a real supply-chain shape for vendored control packs, but gated behind that composition choice. Scoped below MEDIUM because the attacker must already hold a check slot in the profile.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) each control's check evaluates against a pristine per-control deep copy of the snapshot (or the snapshot is frozen before evaluation), so a mutating check cannot affect later controls; (2) break-first battery: the contamination probe BREAKs (later check observes the mutation) on old code, HELDs (later check sees a pristine snapshot) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_control_profiles, w257 profiles battery).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-259 lane A).** Close-when evidence: (1) `run_profile()` now builds `view = copy.deepcopy(pristine)` at the top of each control's iteration, so every check receives its own pristine per-control copy; the up-front `copy.deepcopy` of the caller snapshot (and its fail-closed `control-profile-evidence-malformed` refusal) is unchanged. Copy bound documented at the code site and in the docstrings: `copy.deepcopy`, unbounded depth, cycle-safe via its memo dict; an environmental copy fault inside the loop records an ERROR result for that control, never a crash. (2) Break-first battery `evals/w259_f225_probes.py`: 4 BREAK on the pre-fix tree (verdict-flip, nested-mutation, cycle-marker, cross-run leakage; exit 1), 6/6 HELD on the fixed module in staging AND `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (exit 0 both). The wave-258 red-team standing pin (`profiles/cross-control-snapshot-contamination`) flipped BREAK -> HELD. (3) Adjacent suites green: tests.test_control_profiles 23/23 (incl. new `test_per_control_snapshot_isolation` regression test at the run_profile seam), w257_profiles_probes.py 13/13 HELD. Full canonical suite not run: ~1.7 GB available memory, below the ~2 GB standing threshold (F186 lesson); the 2 ERRORs in w258_redteam_probes.py are the pre-existing F226 defect, identical on the pristine base, out of this lane's scope. Taxonomy pin unchanged: 1064.

## F227: gov/control_profiles.py emit_profile_results escapes raw KeyError on malformed caller-built result records (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-259 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w259_redteam_probes.py` (probes `profiles/malformed-results-missing-control-id-keyerror`, `profiles/malformed-results-missing-reason-keyerror`).

**Defect:** `emit_profile_results()` claims the caller-supplied `profile_results` shape is "re-validated fail-closed here", but the validation checks only five top-level keys (`profile_id`, `profile_title`, `profile_digest`, `success`, `results`). Per-result record keys are trusted: `_finding_ref()` and the findings-mapping loop index `r["control_id"]`, `r["status"]`, `r["reason"]`, `r["impact"]`, `r["severity"]`, `r["digest"]` directly. A caller-built record with a fail/error entry missing any of these escapes raw `KeyError` from the public seam instead of `ControlProfileError(control-profile-malformed)`. Verified on base: missing `control_id` -> `KeyError('control_id')`; missing `reason` -> `KeyError('reason')`; missing `status` -> `KeyError('status')`. Same defect class as F226 (wrong error type at a public seam; a caller catching only `ControlProfileError` misses the refusal entirely).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed (the exception aborts before the emitter runs -- no artifact is emitted), no integrity property weakened, no silent pass. The caller is the trusted deployment, and well-formed fabricated results still emit per the documented trust boundary (pinned HELD). Exposure is the same envelope break as F226: error-type confusion for a caller that catches only `ControlProfileError`.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `emit_profile_results()` validates per-result record keys and refuses malformed caller-built records with `ControlProfileError` carrying a `control-profile-*` machine code -- no raw `KeyError` escapes on any missing per-result key; (2) break-first battery: the two malformed-results probes BREAK (raw `KeyError`) on old code, HELD (machine-coded refusal) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_control_profiles, w257 profiles battery).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-260 lane A).** Close-when evidence: (1) `emit_profile_results()` now re-validates every per-result record BEFORE the first per-result key is indexed: `results` must be a list and each record a dict carrying `control_id`, `status`, `reason`, `impact`, `severity`, `digest` (new module-level `_RESULT_KEYS`, matching the exact keys the seam indexes). A malformed caller-built record is refused via `_refuse(MALFORMED, ...)` -- `ControlProfileError(control-profile-malformed)`, the EXISTING code (verified in `gov/decision_codes.py`, domain `control-profile`); no new taxonomy code, pin unchanged at 1080. The validation is status-agnostic (it runs before the pass/fail split) so the pass-mapping path, the findings-mapping loop, and `_default_findings_index()` all see only validated records; module + `emit_profile_results` docstrings now state the F227 seam contract. (2) Break-first battery `evals/w260_f227_probes.py`: 8 BREAK on the pre-fix tree (raw `KeyError` for each of the six missing keys, raw `TypeError` for a non-dict record and non-list `results`; exit 1), 11/11 HELD on the fixed code in staging AND `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (exit 0 both). The wave-259 red-team standing pins `profiles/malformed-results-missing-control-id-keyerror` and `profiles/malformed-results-missing-reason-keyerror` flipped BREAK -> HELD (machine-coded refusal: `control-profile-malformed`). (3) Adjacent suites green in both modes: tests.test_control_profiles 29/29 (incl. 4 new F227 regression tests: per-key refusal, non-dict record, non-list results, pass-record status-agnostic refusal), w257_profiles_probes, w258_f222_probes, w259_f226_probes (via the battery's depth-1 green check honoring GOV_SKIP_GREEN). Taxonomy pin unchanged: 1080.

## F228: gov/short_lived_credentials.py verify() validates `now` only on the good-secret path (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-259 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w259_redteam_probes.py` (probe `credentials/now-validation-path-dependent`).

**Defect:** F224's close-when criterion (1) requires that a non-numeric `now` "is refused with a `short-lived-credential-malformed` machine code on both `verify()` and `expire_due()`". The closure added `_validate_now()`, but in `verify()` it runs AFTER the unknown-id, secret-mismatch, revoked, expired, and scope checks. Verified on base: `verify(unknown_id, secret, now="yesterday")` -> `short-lived-credential-unknown`; `verify(cid, wrong_secret, now="yesterday")` -> `short-lived-credential-unknown`; only `verify(cid, correct_secret, now="yesterday")` -> `short-lived-credential-malformed`. `expire_due()` validates first and is consistent. So whether a non-numeric `now` is reported as malformed depends on id/secret correctness -- the F224 machine-code contract is path-dependent. Same defect class as F224 (machine-code contract at a public seam).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed and machine-coded on every path: no raw exception escapes, no verification is bypassed, and no attacker advantage follows (the refusal codes reveal nothing beyond the API-level claim). The gap is contract inconsistency -- F224's close-when (1) is not satisfied on the letter ("refused ... on verify()") for the two refusal paths.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `_validate_now()` runs before any refusal decision in `verify()` (equivalently: on all paths including unknown-id and secret-mismatch), so a non-numeric/bool/NaN/inf `now` is refused with `short-lived-credential-malformed` regardless of id/secret correctness; the past-numeric test hook keeps working; the F223 timing symmetry is preserved (validation work identical on both refusal paths); (2) break-first battery: the now-validation probe BREAKs (`short-lived-credential-unknown` instead of malformed on the refusal paths) on old code, HELDs on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_short_lived_credentials, w256 credentials battery).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-260 lane B).** Close-when evidence: (1) `at = _validate_now(now)` moved to the first line of `verify()` in gov/short_lived_credentials.py, before the id lookup, the F223 dummy-HMAC unknown-id refusal, the secret-mismatch check, and the revoked/expired/scope checks -- non-numeric/bool/NaN/inf `now` is now refused with `short-lived-credential-malformed` on unknown-id, secret-mismatch, and good-secret paths alike; the past-numeric `now` test hook keeps working (pinned by control probe); the validation work is identical on every path (all refusal paths pass through the same call before branching), so no new id-existence timing delta: the F223 timing battery re-measured at **306 ns** (median-of-medians, bar 1000 ns), unchanged within noise vs the pre-fix tree. No new taxonomy code (pin stays 1080). (2) Break-first battery `evals/w260_f228_probes.py`: 3 BREAK on the pre-fix tree (unknown-id + `now="yesterday"` -> `short-lived-credential-unknown`, mismatch + `now="yesterday"` -> `short-lived-credential-unknown`, the same for bool/list/NaN/inf shapes) in BOTH staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; 8/8 HELD on the fixed tree in both modes. The wave-259 red-team standing pin `credentials/now-validation-path-dependent` flipped BREAK -> HELD. (3) Adjacent suites green: tests.test_short_lived_credentials rc=0, evals/w258_f223f224_probes.py 6/6 HELD (timing 306 ns), evals/w259_redteam_probes.py 13 HELD / 4 BREAK (all 4 are the F227/F229 open-finding probes from other lanes, unrelated to this change).

## F229: gov/evidence_quality.py _safe_deepcopy maps only four exception types -- a hostile __deepcopy__ raising anything else escapes raw (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-259 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w259_redteam_probes.py` (probes `evidence/hostile-deepcopy-runtimeerror-raw-escape`, `evidence/hostile-deepcopy-meta-runtimeerror-raw-escape`).

**Defect:** The F220 closure guards every deepcopy site with `_safe_deepcopy()`, which maps `RecursionError` and `(TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError, copy.Error)` to the evidence/malformed machine codes. A deepcopy-hostile caller object whose `__deepcopy__` raises anything outside that tuple -- e.g. `RuntimeError`, `KeyError`, `OSError`, a custom `Exception` subclass -- escapes RAW from the public `evaluate()` / `validate_expectation()` seams. Verified on base: an object raising `RuntimeError("boom-from-deepcopy")` in `__deepcopy__` escapes raw `RuntimeError` from `evaluate()` (evidence deepcopy) and from `validate_expectation()` (meta deepcopy). Same defect class as F220 (raw hostile exception at a public seam; the machine-code contract is "never a raw escape", F218 class). Fail-closed in effect (the exception aborts before any result), wrong error type.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Same scoping as F220/F224/F226: fail-closed, no integrity property weakened, no attacker advantage beyond a loud refusal of the wrong type.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `_safe_deepcopy()` maps ALL exceptions raised by hostile caller objects to the machine codes (e.g. a broad `except Exception` arm alongside the `RecursionError` arm), so no raw exception from `__deepcopy__` escapes `evaluate()` / `validate_expectation()`; (2) break-first battery: the two hostile-deepcopy probes BREAK (raw `RuntimeError`) on old code, HELD (machine-coded refusal) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_evidence_quality, w256 evidence-quality battery).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-260 lane C).** Close-when evidence: trailing `except Exception` arm added to `_safe_deepcopy()` alongside the `RecursionError` arm, mapping every remaining hostile exception to the caller's EXISTING evidence/malformed machine code (no new codes; F220 mapping convention). `except Exception` does not catch `BaseException`, so `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit` propagate raw (verified directly). Red-first: `evals/w260_f229_probes.py` (hostile `__deepcopy__` raising `RuntimeError`, `KeyError`, `OSError`, and a custom `Exception` subclass across the evidence/meta/artifact seams) BREAKs 4/4 raw-escape on base, HELDs 5/5 on fixed code x2 (staging + `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`); the wave-259 red-team F229 probes now HELD. Adjacent suites green: tests.test_evidence_quality, w256 evidence-quality battery, w258_f220f221 7/7, w258_f222 11/11.



## F230: gov/transparency_log.py verify_log cannot see tail truncation -- the last append(s) can be silently deleted (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-260 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w260_redteam_probes.py` (probe `transparency/tail-truncation-invisible-to-verify-log`).

**Defect:** `verify_log()` recomputes roots, signatures, and contiguity from `leaves.jsonl`/`heads.jsonl`, and `detect_equivocation()` only fires on same-size conflicting roots. Neither sees the log *shrink*: an attacker with write access to the log directory (no signing key needed) who deletes the last line of both files leaves a fully self-consistent shorter log. Verified on base: 5 appends, delete the tail line of both files, re-open in auditor mode -- `verify_log()` returns `(True, "ok: 4 leaves, 4 heads verify")` and `detect_equivocation()` returns `[]`. The module's headline claim is an append-only tamper-evident log ("consistency proofs for the append-only guarantee", verify_log catching "history was rewritten"); tail deletion is history rewriting that the module's own audit reports as OK.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Exploitation needs write access to the operator's log storage (a strong position -- compromised storage or a keyless insider); only the most recent tail is deletable, never rewritten or forged; auditors retaining newer signed tree heads out-of-band can notice the shrink, though no in-repo API expresses the comparison (verify_consistency refuses old_size > new_size, so a witnessed head at size n cannot be checked against a truncated log at size n-1). Scoped below MEDIUM because the position is privileged and the damage is deletion-only.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) there is an in-repo, keyless way to detect that the log shrank below a previously witnessed state -- e.g. `verify_log()`/`compare()` accepts a witnessed head (or witnessed tree size) and refuses when the current log is shorter, or a monotonic append counter is anchored in the signed heads -- so the truncation probe is detectable without the signing key; (2) break-first battery: the tail-truncation probe BREAKs (verify_log=True after truncation) on old code, HELDs (truncation detected) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_transparency_log, w259 transparency battery).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-261 lane A).** Witnessed-state comparison landed: `TransparencyLog.verify_log(expected_size=None, expected_head=None)` -- keyless (the witnessed head's STH signature is re-verified under the log's own key, so auditor mode needs no signing key). Returns `(False, reason)` when the current log is shorter than the witnessed state, when the witnessed head does not verify, or when the witnessed head's root disagrees with the current log's prefix at that size (history rewritten or forked view). Evidence: `evals/w261_transparency2_probes.py` f230/* probes BREAK pre-fix (no witnessed-state API; truncation invisible) and HELD post-fix, in staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; the w260 pin probe `transparency/tail-truncation-invisible-to-verify-log` was updated to witness the head pre-truncation and now HELDs; adjacent suites green (`tests.test_transparency_log` 32/32, `evals/w259_transparency_probes.py` 19/19, both modes). Honest residual (documented in the module docstring): with no witnessed state, `verify_log()` remains a self-consistency check -- a truncated-but-internally-consistent log verifies True.

## F231: gov/transparency_log.py detect_equivocation counts unsigned/forged heads as conflicts (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-260 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w260_redteam_probes.py` (probe `transparency/equivocation-unsigned-head-counts-as-conflict`).

**Defect:** `detect_equivocation()` groups heads by `(tree_size, root_hash)` and reports >1 distinct root per size as a conflict -- "durable evidence of operator misbehavior" -- but never verifies a signature. Verified on base: one genuine signed head at tree_size 1 plus a forged head (same size, different root, 64 zero bytes as the "signature"; `verify_tree_head` returns False) yields a conflict dict claiming "equivocation: 2 distinct roots signed for tree size 1". Anyone who can hand the detector a JSON object -- no log key required -- can manufacture durable-looking evidence of operator misbehavior: a false-accusation / alarm-fatigue vector against the very witnesses the design relies on.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. False positive, not false negative: no integrity property is weakened, no forged record verifies. Exposure is reputational/operational (a witness acting on an unsigned conflict), and the docstring does say "signed heads", so a careful caller pre-verifies -- but the function itself does not, and its output is presented as evidence.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `detect_equivocation()` verifies each head's STH signature (and log_id binding) before grouping, so only genuinely-signed conflicting heads produce conflicts; unsigned/unverifiable heads are ignored or reported separately, never as equivocation evidence; (2) break-first battery: the unsigned-head probe BREAKs (conflict from an unsigned head) on old code, HELDs on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_transparency_log, w259 transparency battery).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-261 lane A).** `TransparencyLog.detect_equivocation(heads=None, strict=False)` now gates every head through `verify_tree_head` under the log's key (signature + log_id binding) before conflict grouping: unsigned/forged/foreign-key/malformed heads are skipped by default and can never become operator-misbehavior evidence; `strict=True` refuses to adjudicate, raising `TransparencyLogError` that names them as invalid input. Evidence: `evals/w261_transparency2_probes.py` f231/* probes BREAK pre-fix (unsigned-head conflict, no invalid-input reporting) and all 5 HELD post-fix x2 modes, with the genuine-equivocation guard probe still detecting real split-views; the w260 pin probe `transparency/equivocation-unsigned-head-counts-as-conflict` HELDs; adjacent suites green (32/32, 19/19, both modes).

**Cells:** wave-260 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w260_redteam_probes.py` (probe `transparency/operator-path-raw-oserror-escapes`).

**Defect:** The module's contract is that failures raise `TransparencyLogError` with plain human messages (it adds no taxonomy codes). `verify_log()` honors this (it catches `OSError`), but the operator path does not. **Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-261 lane A).** All operator-path I/O now raises `TransparencyLogError` with plain human messages: `__init__` log-directory creation, LOG_ID write, and leaves/heads reads (plus an explicit "exists but is not a regular file: storage is corrupt" refusal instead of silently treating it as absent), and `append()` leaf/head writes. No new taxonomy codes (module contract; pin stays 1092). Evidence: `evals/w261_transparency2_probes.py` f232/* probes BREAK pre-fix (raw `FileExistsError`/`IsADirectoryError` escape) and all 6 HELD post-fix x2 modes; the w260 pin probe `transparency/operator-path-raw-oserror-escapes` HELDs; adjacent suites green (32/32, 19/19, both modes).

## F233: gov/svid_issuer.py SVID usage field is signed but never enforced by SvidVerifier or MeshControl (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-260 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w260_redteam_probes.py` (probe `svid/usage-never-enforced-by-verifier-or-mesh`).

**Defect:** Issuance profiles bind usages (`workload` -> `("workload-auth",)`, `mesh-control` -> `("mesh-control",)`), the TTL half of the profile is enforced at issuance (`svid-ttl-stretched`), and the usage list is signed into the SVID body -- but nothing ever checks it. Neither `SvidVerifier.verify()` nor `MeshControl.admit()` takes an expected usage; the signed `usage` field is returned in the claims dict and constrains nothing. Verified on base: a `mesh-control`-profile SVID for `spiffe://example.org/workload/agent1` is admitted by a `MeshControl` whose allowlist is `spiffe://example.org/workload`. The profiles-as-data story (cfssl ADAPT: "per-profile max TTL and usages") is half-enforced: TTL is a real bound, usage is claims-only.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Exploitation needs a valid issuer-signed SVID for the trust domain (issuer compromise, or legitimate issuance under a second profile -- the realistic shape is a workload that legitimately holds a mesh-control SVID using it where only workload-auth was intended). The trust-domain, signature, expiry, and ACL checks all hold; this is a missing least-privilege layer, not a bypass of any enforced check.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `SvidVerifier.verify()` and/or `MeshControl.admit()` accept an expected-usage parameter and refuse with a machine code when the SVID's signed usage does not cover it -- a new code only if none of the existing ten covers the refusal (`svid-acl-denied` fits the admit seam; the verifier seam likely needs its own); (2) break-first battery: the usage probe BREAKs (mesh-control SVID admitted to a workload ACL) on old code, HELDs (refused) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_svid_issuer, w259 identity battery).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-261 lane B).** Close-when evidence: (1) `SvidVerifier.verify()` now takes `expected_usage`: after signature verification, the SVID's SIGNED usage list must cover it, else the new machine code `svid-usage-mismatch` (registered in `gov/decision_codes.py`, domain `svid`, severity medium; usage is checked only over the signed body, so a tampered usage still dies at `svid-signature-invalid`). `MeshControl` policy gains an optional `"usages"` key binding allowed usages per route -- a verified SVID outside it is refused with the EXISTING `svid-acl-denied` at the admit seam -- and `admit()` takes a per-call `expected_usage` threaded through to the verifier seam. A malformed `expected_usage` (non-str/empty) is caller error -> `svid-malformed`. Omitted `expected_usage` and policies without `"usages"` keep the old behavior (backward compatible). (2) Break-first battery `evals/w261_svid2_probes.py`: 5 BREAK on the pre-fix tree (verify/admit take no `expected_usage` -> TypeError; policy `"usages"` silently ignored -> mesh-control SVID admitted to a workload-usage route) in BOTH staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; 7/7 HELD on the fixed tree in both modes (exit 0, pin OK). The wave-260 red-team standing pin `svid/usage-never-enforced-by-verifier-or-mesh` flipped BREAK -> HELD (probe updated to pin the closure at both seams: verifier `svid-usage-mismatch`, admit `svid-acl-denied`, admit passthrough). (3) Adjacent suites green: tests.test_svid_issuer + tests.test_mesh_admission + tests.test_svid_enrollment 80/80 (incl. 9 new regression tests: usage enforcement, tamper-before-usage, policy binding, bad-usages policy, admit passthrough), tests.test_decision_codes 19/19, w259_identity_probes 18/18 HELD, w260_identity2_probes 18/18 HELD, w260_redteam_probes 8 HELD / 3 BREAK / 3 BASELINE (the 3 BREAKs are the F230/F231/F232 open-finding probes, other lanes' scope). Taxonomy pin: 1092 -> 1093 (+1 `svid-usage-mismatch`); all pin assignments/assertions repointed value-token-only.

## F234: gov/svid_issuer.py `now` validation is path-dependent in SvidVerifier.verify and TestSvidIssuer.issue (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-260 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w260_redteam_probes.py` (probe `svid/now-validation-path-dependent`).

Whether a non-numeric `now` is reported as malformed depends on SVID validity -- the documented machine-code contract is path-dependent.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed and machine-coded on every path: no raw exception escapes, no verification is bypassed, no attacker advantage follows. The gap is contract inconsistency against the module's own documented `_validate_now` refusal.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `_validate_now()` runs before any refusal decision in `SvidVerifier.verify()`, `TestSvidIssuer.issue()` (and `MeshControl.admit()` via verify), so a non-numeric/bool/NaN/inf `now` is refused with `svid-malformed` regardless of SVID validity or field errors -- no new code needed, `svid-malformed` already covers the refusal; (2) break-first battery: the now-validation probe BREAKs (refusal codes instead of malformed on the refusal paths) on old code, HELDs on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_svid_issuer, w259 identity battery).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-261 lane B).** Close-when evidence: (1) `_validate_now(now)` moved to the FIRST line of `SvidVerifier.verify()` and `TestSvidIssuer.issue()` -- the F228 fix pattern, mirrored from `gov/short_lived_credentials.py` -- so a non-numeric/bool/NaN/inf `now` refuses `svid-malformed` before ANY refusal decision (presence, structure, trust-domain, issuer, signature in verify; identity/profile/TTL in issue); `MeshControl.admit()` is covered via `verify()`. No new code: the existing `svid-malformed` covers the refusal. The past-numeric `now` test hook keeps working (pinned by a control probe on issue/verify/admit). (2) Break-first battery `evals/w261_svid2_probes.py`: the three now probes BREAK on the pre-fix tree (bad-sig + `now="yesterday"` -> `svid-signature-invalid`, missing -> `svid-missing`, issue refusal-path -> `svid-identity-malformed`; admit -> `svid-signature-invalid`) in BOTH staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; 7/7 HELD on the fixed tree in both modes (exit 0). The wave-260 red-team standing pin `svid/now-validation-path-dependent` flipped BREAK -> HELD with no probe change (it already expected `svid-malformed` on every path). (3) Adjacent suites green: same scope as the F233 closure above -- 80/80 unit tests (incl. 3 new now-first regression tests), 19/19 decision-codes, 18/18 + 18/18 identity batteries, w260_redteam 8 HELD / 3 BREAK (F230/F231/F232, other lanes) / 3 BASELINE. No taxonomy change for F234.


## F235: gov/policy_distribution.py Subscriber.apply raises RecursionError on hostile deeply-nested input -- the "never raises" contract is violated (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-261 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w261_redteam_probes.py` (probe `poldist/recursion-error-on-hostile-unsigned-input`).

**Defect:** `Subscriber.apply()` documents "Never raises on hostile input; every refusal is machine-coded." The `apply` catch covers only `UnicodeDecodeError` and `ValueError`, but `json.loads()` on deeply nested hostile JSON raises `RecursionError` (a `RuntimeError` subclass), which escapes `apply()`. Verified on base: hand-crafted unsigned bundles nested 2000/5000 deep are refused as `poldist-signature-mismatch` (the JSON parses), but a 20000-deep unsigned bundle raises `RecursionError` out of `Subscriber.apply()` instead of being machine-coded. The input is unsigned and unauthenticated -- anyone positioned at the transport seam (the module's threat model: bytes arrive over "any channel", e.g. a file drop, queue, or websocket) can kill the subscriber's apply loop with a single hostile bundle. A long-lived subscriber (the designed deployment) dies on the first hostile input.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Availability-only: no policy is bypassed, no hostile bundle is applied, no data is corrupted. The defect is the contract violation itself -- the module's headline promise ("Never raises on hostile input") is false at the exact seam it defends.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `Subscriber.apply()` refuses hostile deeply-nested (and other recursion-hostile) input with a machine code (e.g. `poldist-bundle-malformed` or a new bounded-nesting code) instead of raising -- e.g. bound the parser's nesting depth or catch `RecursionError` alongside the existing catches; (2) break-first battery: the recursion probe BREAKs (RecursionError escapes `apply()`) on old code, HELDs (machine-coded refusal) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_policy_distribution, w260 redteam battery poldist probes).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-262 lane A).** Close-when evidence: (1) `except RecursionError` added at the unsigned-input parse boundary in `Subscriber.apply()` -- `json.loads` raises `RecursionError` (a `RuntimeError` subclass, not `ValueError`) on nesting beyond the interpreter's budget, and it used to escape `apply()`. The branch refuses with the existing `poldist-bundle-malformed` code (no new code; no hard depth bound, so legitimate depth is untouched). Post-fix depth sweep of unsigned hostile bundles at depths 100--100000: no raise anywhere, machine-coded refusal everywhere (under-budget -> `poldist-signature-mismatch` on the signature seam, over-budget -> `poldist-bundle-malformed`), worst apply time 2ms -- the "never raises on hostile input" contract holds at every nesting depth. (2) Break-first battery `evals/w262_poldist2_probes.py`: the red-team's verbatim probe `poldist/recursion-error-on-hostile-unsigned-input` BREAKs (RecursionError escapes) on the pre-fix tree and HELDs (refused as `poldist-bundle-malformed`) on the fixed tree, in BOTH staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; new probes: just-under-boundary (900-deep) unsigned refused `poldist-signature-mismatch`, just-over-boundary (30000-deep) refused `poldist-bundle-malformed`, signed 800-deep bundle still verifies/applies (legitimate depth preserved), 100000-deep hostile input refused in ~1ms. Pre-fix battery: 3 BREAK / 2 HELD (the two boundary/signed controls hold pre-fix too); post-fix: 5/5 HELD in both modes (exit 0). No in-repo git subprocesses; depth-1 green checks honoring `GOV_SKIP_GREEN=1`. (3) Adjacent suites green: `tests.test_policy_distribution` 16/16 (incl. 2 new F235 regression tests: recursion-hostile refused machine-coded, signed-deep still applies), `evals/w260_poldist_probes.py` 10/10 via the green check, `evals/w261_redteam_probes.py` F235 probe flipped BREAK -> HELD while the F236 probes remain BREAK (other lane's scope). No taxonomy change (pin 1106 held). Residual noted for a future lane: `Publisher.sign_bundle` with a recursion-hostile payload raises raw `RecursionError` out of `canonical_payload` instead of `PublisherError` (trusted operator surface, not the refusing seam; not part of F235).

## F236: gov/svid_enrollment.py EnrollmentAuthority key table has no concurrency control -- concurrent redeem double-issues SVIDs from one key; live_keys raises under concurrent issue (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-261 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w261_redteam_probes.py` (probes `enrollment/concurrent-redeem-double-issues-single-key`, `enrollment/live-keys-raises-under-concurrent-issue`).

**Defect:** `EnrollmentAuthority` holds its key table in a plain dict with no lock anywhere in the module. (a) `redeem()` performs a check-then-set on `record["used"]`: it reads `used`, and only later writes `used=True` after issuing. Two threads redeeming the SAME key concurrently can both observe `used=False` before either writes, so both proceed to `issuer.issue()` -- one enrollment key yields two (or more) SVIDs, breaking the module's headline "single-use" / "exactly one SVID per key" / "burned on redemption" contract. Verified on base: 64 threads racing one key across 150 trials repeatedly double-issued (1-7 double-issuing trials per 150-trial run across repeated runs). (b) `live_keys()` iterates `self._records.values()` while `issue_key()` mutates the same dict, raising `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` -- verified on base: 8 reader threads crashed within 3s against 4 writer threads. The module documents cross-INSTANCE burn atomicity as deployment-owned, which implies in-process atomicity is the module's own job; the in-process table is unprotected. Exploitation needs possession of a valid enrollment key plus concurrent redemption against the same in-process authority -- a stolen/shared key enrolls two workloads instead of one.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires a valid enrollment key (no authentication bypass, no bypass of the signature/binding checks); each extra SVID is still bound to the key's spiffe-id; the `live_keys` crash is on an observability/test path. The gap is the broken single-use accounting invariant under ordinary threaded use, not a verification bypass.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `redeem()` burns the key atomically under concurrency (e.g. a lock around the check-then-set, or an atomic state transition) so N concurrent redemptions of one key yield exactly one SVID; `live_keys()` (and `issue_key()`) are safe under concurrent mutation; (2) break-first battery: both concurrency probes BREAK on old code, HELD on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (post-fix the probes are deterministic: double-issue is impossible under a lock); (3) adjacent suites green (tests.test_svid_enrollment, w259/w260 identity batteries).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-262 lane B).** Close-when evidence: (1) `redeem()` now performs the whole find-check-burn sequence as one atomic step under a new `threading.Lock` (`self._lock`, created in `__init__`); the lock is released BEFORE `issuer.issue()` is called, so the recorded burn already guarantees exactly-once while issuance itself is not serialized across distinct keys and an issuer exception cannot wedge the table (`with` releases on error; no locked method calls another). `issue_key()` performs its collision-check/insert under the same lock; `live_keys()` iterates a snapshot taken under the lock, so concurrent `issue_key()` inserts can no longer raise "dictionary changed size during iteration". No new machine codes: the existing burn/refusal codes cover every path, so the taxonomy pin stays 1106. (2) Break-first battery `evals/w262_enrollment2_probes.py`: both concurrency probes BREAK on the pre-fix tree (3/150 trials double-issued at 64 threads; `live_keys()` raised `RuntimeError` with 8/8 readers crashing) and HELD on the fixed tree in BOTH staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (exit 0), deterministically post-fix since the lock makes the double-issue interleaving impossible. Three guard probes also HELD in both modes: 64 distinct keys redeemed concurrently all succeed (no false serialization), sequential redeem-after-redeem still refused with `svid-enrollment-key-replayed`, and an exception in the issue path keeps the key burned, releases the lock, and never deadlocks (16 threads). The red-team standing pins in `evals/w261_redteam_probes.py` flipped BREAK -> HELD with no probe change. (3) Adjacent suites green: tests.test_svid_enrollment 26/26 (incl. 4 new concurrency regression tests), tests.test_mesh_admission 24/24, evals/w260_identity2_probes.py 18/18 HELD, evals/w261_redteam_probes.py 22 HELD / 1 BREAK (F235, other lane's scope) / 2 BASELINE (F230/F233, other lanes). No taxonomy change for F236.

## F237: gov/ballot_governance.py resolve() re-runs vote hooks without the vote()-time bool coercion -- non-bool truthy/falsy hook returns corrupt the tally (veto evasion -> wrongful adoption) (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-262 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w262_redteam_probes.py` (probes `ballot/resolve-drops-nonbool-hook-returns-veto-evaded`, `ballot/resolve-drops-nonbool-hook-returns-yes-lost`).

**Defect:** `BallotBox.vote()` bool-coerces the vote-hook return (`effective = bool(effective)`) and journals the coerced value, but `resolve()` tallies `_effective_votes()`, which stores the RAW hook return with no coercion. The shipped sample resolvers then use identity checks (`v is False` for veto, `v is True` for yes). A deployment-authored `vote_fn` returning idiomatic truthy/falsy values (e.g. `1`/`0`, or `True`/`0`) silently corrupts governance: verified on base, a `True`/`0` hook lets a ballot ADOPT despite a member voting `False` (the journaled `effective=False` veto is missed because `0 is not False` -- note `majority`), and a `1`/`0` hook drops every yes-vote (`1 is not True`) so a unanimous ballot dies as `rejected/ballot-quorum-not-reached`. The journaled effective values and the resolve-time tally disagree -- the ledger says veto, the resolver adopts. The `BallotType` docstring contracts `vote_fn -> bool`, but the module enforces it at only one of its two call sites.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The hook is deployment-authored and trusted (a hostile hook is outside the threat model); the defect is the module's own inconsistency between its two hook call sites, turning an idiomatic non-bool return into silent governance corruption. Wrongful adoption is integrity-relevant, but exploitation requires the deployment to write a non-bool hook.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) the resolve path bool-coerces vote-hook outputs exactly as `vote()` does (e.g. in `_effective_votes()`), so journaled effective values and the resolve-time tally always agree; (2) break-first battery: both w262 probes BREAK on old code (veto evaded -> adopted; unanimous yes -> quorum-not-reached), HELD on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w261_ballot_probes.py, evals/w262_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-263).** Fix: `_effective_votes()` bool-coerces the vote-hook return (`bool(btype.vote_fn(...))`), exactly as `vote()` does, so the resolve-time tally always agrees with the journaled effective values. Evidence: `evals/w263_closures_probes.py` 11/11 HELD in staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (both w262 pin probes BREAK pre-fix, HELD post-fix); `evals/w262_redteam_probes.py` 35 HELD / 0 BREAK / 2 BASELINE (documented trust boundaries) / 0 ERROR x2 modes; `evals/w261_ballot_probes.py` 12/12 x2; `tests/test_decision_codes.py` 19 OK x2. Taxonomy pin unchanged (1129).

## F238: gov/failure_actions.py filter no-bypass sweep never visits dict keys -- exact offending bytes surviving as a key are missed and filter returns "continued" on a tainted value (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-262 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w262_redteam_probes.py` (probe `failaction/filter-offending-bytes-as-dict-key-not-swept`).

**Defect:** The filter action documents a byte-level no-bypass guarantee: after redacting the named field, "the whole copy is swept; if those bytes survive at any other path (aliasing the caller did not name), the filter refuses instead of returning a tainted value." The sweep (`_iter_subvalues`) extends its stack with dict VALUES only -- keys are never yielded and never digested. Verified on base: `{"note": "SECRET", "SECRET": "innocent"}` filtered at `field_path="note"` returns disposition `"continued"` with `{"SECRET": "innocent", ...}` -- the exact offending bytes survive at another path and the sweep misses them. The aliased-value control (same object at an unnamed VALUE path) correctly refuses, so the mechanism's intent is subvalue-identity and keys are simply an unswept position. Substring containment (`"xxSECRETxx"`) is accepted as subvalue-granularity by design (probed, HELD -- the "(aliasing the caller did not name)" parenthetical scopes the threat to aliased copies, and refusing on every superstring would make filter unusable).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires the offending bytes to also appear as a dict key in the filtered value -- an unusual shape -- and the failure direction is a "continued" disposition the caller must interpret, not a silent allow. The gap is the documented guarantee being false at one class of paths.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) the no-bypass sweep visits dict keys (and any other byte-carrying positions of the value graph) so exact offending bytes surviving as a key are refused with the FailResult's own code; (2) break-first battery: the key probe BREAKs on old code, HELDs on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; the aliased-value control still refuses; (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w261_failaction_probes.py, evals/w262_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-263).** Fix: `_iter_subvalues()` now extends the sweep stack with dict keys as well as values, so exact offending bytes surviving as a key trip the no-bypass sweep and the filter refuses with the FailResult's own code (`FailureActionError("pii-leak")`). Evidence: `evals/w263_closures_probes.py` 11/11 HELD in staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (key probe BREAKs pre-fix, HELDs post-fix; nested-key variant and clean-value control HELD); the w262 pin probe was adapted to the refusal idiom (same attack, same input -- the mandated refusal raises, so the break-first fall-through is unreachable post-fix; mirrors the file's own aliased-value control); aliased-value control still refuses (w262 HELD); `evals/w261_failaction_probes.py` 12/12 x2. Taxonomy pin unchanged (1129).

## F239: gov/detectors.py per-engine provenance stamp is exfiltratable through data-defined detector field paths -- the "stripped before events are returned to callers" claim is false (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-262 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w262_redteam_probes.py` (probe `detectors/stamp-exfiltrated-via-from-field`).

**Defect:** The trust boundary documents that subscription edges carry only engine-issued produced events "recognized by a per-engine secret stamp that is stripped before events are returned to callers." But chained detectors evaluate predicates and extract `produces.fields` from the INTERNAL event with `_engine_stamp` still present, and `_check_path` allows the single-underscore key (the dunder/proto guard refuses `__` segments only). Verified on base: a data-defined chained detector with predicate `{"field": "_engine_stamp", "op": "exists"}` and `produces.fields = {"leaked_stamp": {"from_field": "_engine_stamp"}}` emits the live engine secret into a produced event returned to the caller. The structural defense (chained levels only ever see engine-produced internals, never caller input) still holds -- forged produced events cannot traverse subscription edges today -- so the stamp is currently defense-in-depth; but the documented stripping property is factually false, the secret reaches detector-definition authors/callers, and any current or future stamp-checking path is defeated by construction. Detector definitions are DATA (JSON-serializable, crossing trust boundaries -- the `__` refusal shows hostile definitions are in the threat model), so a definition-level read of engine internals is in-scope.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Secret exposure with limited immediate exploitability: the structural pending-list defense (not the stamp) is what actually blocks forged traversal today. The defect is the exfiltration path plus the false documented claim; it also lets definitions branch on internal-vs-raw event identity.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) detector field paths cannot observe engine-internal keys: `_check_path` refuses `_engine_stamp` (extend the dunder-style guard to the engine's own reserved key) and/or predicate evaluation and field extraction run against the stamp-stripped event; (2) break-first battery: the stamp probe BREAKs on old code (secret in produced fields), HELDs on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; the sample chain still fires end-to-end and forged events still cannot traverse edges; (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w261_detector_probes.py, evals/w262_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-263).** Fix: `DetectorEngine._run_detector()` evaluates selectors, predicates, exception fields, and `from_field` extraction against the stamp-stripped event (the "and/or" second option -- chosen because a registration refusal would turn the w262 pin probe's `register_all` into a harness ERROR instead of the required HELD flip). The structural provenance check in `process()` stays on the internal event (not data-defined); the alert sink already received the stripped event via `on_match`. Evidence: `evals/w263_closures_probes.py` 11/11 HELD in staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (stamp probe BREAKs pre-fix with the live secret in produced fields, HELDs post-fix; legitimate producer->consumer chain still fires; `from_field: "_engine_stamp"` resolves to None; predicate on the reserved key never matches while registration still succeeds); w262 `detectors/sample-chain-fires-end-to-end` and `detectors/forged-produced-event-no-subscription-traversal` HELD; `evals/w261_detector_probes.py` 19/19 x2; `evals/w262_alert_probes.py` 14/14 x2. Taxonomy pin unchanged (1129).

## F240: gov/scoped_tool_listing.py seals a subject binding into scope tickets but never verifies the presenter -- tickets are usable by any holder (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-263 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w263_redteam_probes.py` (probe `scopelist/cross-subject-ticket-bearer`).

**Defect:** `ScopeTicketIssuer.seal(subject_digest, scopes)` binds the caller's subject digest into the HMAC'd ticket (module docstring, "Identity binding: scopes are sealed into an HMAC ticket bound to the caller's SUBJECT DIGEST"). But `ToolRegistry._ticket_scopes` discards the bound subject (`_, scopes = self._issuer.verify(sealed_ticket)`), and neither `invoke` nor `list_tools` accepts a presenter identity -- there is no parameter, on any registry method, to assert who is presenting the ticket. Verified on base: a ticket sealed for `alice-subject-digest` authorizes `invoke`/`list_tools` for any holder; `inspect` of both signatures shows no subject/presenter parameter. The module's honest residual delegates subject enforcement to `gov.mcp_invocation_authz`'s trust-anchored subject -- but that layer never sees the ticket's `sub` claim, and the module's own documented composition ("deployments using transactional tokens run `check_scope` first, then this registry's `invoke`") never compares the ticket's bound subject against anything. The w244 layer binds its grant to the exact token (`token_digest`); this layer binds its ticket to a subject no seam ever checks. The "bound to the caller's SUBJECT DIGEST" claim is therefore unenforced at every seam: the binding's purpose -- making a stolen/exfiltrated ticket useless to another subject -- is defeated, and cross-subject replay passes both composed layers (each verifies only its own credential).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Exploitation requires obtaining another subject's ticket (exfiltration); scope coverage is still enforced per ticket, and no denied capability is granted beyond the ticket's own scopes. The defect is the false binding claim at the module's documented choke point.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `ToolRegistry.invoke`/`list_tools` verify the presenter against the ticket's bound subject (e.g. an expected-subject parameter, or the registry bound to a subject when the issuer is attached) and refuse a presenter mismatch with a machine code; OR the "bound" claim is removed and replaced with documented holder-usable semantics plus the required deployment composition (the deployment compares `issuer.verify(ticket).sub` against the trust-anchored subject before calling `invoke`); (2) break-first battery: the w263 probe `scopelist/cross-subject-ticket-bearer` BREAKs (cross-subject use succeeds, no presenter seam) on old code, HELDs (refused, or claim removed and documented) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w262_scopelist_probes.py, evals/w263_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-264 lane A, TDD, red-first).** `ToolRegistry.invoke`/`list_tools` take an optional keyword-only `expected_subject`; when given it MUST equal the ticket's bound subject (constant-time `hmac.compare_digest`) or the use refuses the new machine code `scope-listing-subject-mismatch` (taxonomy 1151 -> 1152, additive, alphabetical). Without an asserted presenter the ticket keeps documented holder-usable semantics. Verified: `evals/w264_f240f241f242_probes.py` `f240/cross-subject-invoke-bearer` and `f240/cross-subject-listing-bearer` BREAK on base / HELD on fix x2 modes, `f240/holder-semantics-preserved` HELD (no false positives); w263 `scopelist/cross-subject-ticket-bearer` flips to HELD; adjacent suites green (w262 7/7, w263 no new breaks). Two-axis review: Standards PASS, Spec PASS (all three close-when criteria met verbatim).

## F241: gov/scoped_tool_listing.py has no domain separation between scope tickets and consent tokens -- a consent token verifies as a scope ticket under a shared deployment key (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-263 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w263_redteam_probes.py` (probe `scopelist/consent-token-verifies-as-scope-ticket`).

**Defect:** `_seal`/`_open` use a single MAC construction (`hmac.new(key, canonical_json)`) for both sealed-token protocols with no type tag and no domain separation. Both issuers take "the deployment key", so a deployment naturally shares one key. Verified on base: with a shared key, `ScopeTicketIssuer.verify()` accepts a `ConsentIssuer.mint_consent_url()` token, returning `(sub='human-sub', scopes={'net:fetch'})` -- every consent token doubles as a holder-usable scope ticket for its scopes until its `exp`. Consent tokens are minted into human-facing URLs (out-of-band by design: logged, shoulder-surfable, proxied), so a consent-token leak upgrades into scope-ticket use on any tool the token's scopes cover. The reverse direction (ticket presented to `confirm_consent`) refuses, but only as `scope-consent-expired` -- the missing `exp` defaults to 0 -- i.e. refused for the wrong reason, confirming the format carries no type information. The house standard exists in the same tree: w244's `gov/token_scope_enforcement.py` separates its grant and policy MACs with `_GRANT_DOMAIN`/`_POLICY_DOMAIN`.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Blast radius is bounded by the token's own scopes and the consent TTL (300s default); no scope is exceeded beyond what the token already carried. The defect is the defeated protocol separation: a token minted for one (approval, tool) confirmation is silently valid as a general scope ticket.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) sealed payloads carry a verified type tag (or per-protocol domain separation in the MAC input, as w244 does) so a cross-presented token refuses machine-coded at open -- in both directions, with a correct code; (2) break-first battery: the w263 probe `scopelist/consent-token-verifies-as-scope-ticket` BREAKs (consent token verifies as a scope ticket) on old code, HELDs (refused machine-coded) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; genuine consent confirmations still verify and genuine scope tickets still verify (no cross-breakage); (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w262_scopelist_probes.py, evals/w263_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-264 lane A, TDD, red-first).** `_seal`/`_open` now take a per-protocol MAC domain (w244 house pattern): `scope-ticket.v1` vs `consent-token.v1`, domain-prefixed into the HMAC input. A consent token presented as a scope ticket refuses `scope-grant-tampered` (MAC domain mismatch) under a shared key; a scope ticket presented to `confirm_consent` refuses `scope-consent-forged` (the correct code — previously the wrong-reason `scope-consent-expired`). Verified: `evals/w264_f240f241f242_probes.py` `f241/consent-token-verifies-as-scope-ticket` and `f241/scope-ticket-presented-to-consent` BREAK on base / HELD on fix x2 modes, `f241/genuine-tokens-still-verify` HELD (genuine consent confirms, genuine ticket verifies); w263 `scopelist/consent-token-verifies-as-scope-ticket` flips to HELD; adjacent green. Honest migration note: sealed values minted before this change refuse fail-closed (no silent downgrade); documented in the module docstring. Two-axis review: Standards PASS, Spec PASS.

## F242: gov/scoped_tool_listing.py ToolRegistry.invoke checks tool existence before ticket verification -- unauthenticated existence oracle beyond the documented residual (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-263 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w263_redteam_probes.py` (probe `scopelist/pre-auth-invoke-existence-oracle`).

**Defect:** `ToolRegistry.invoke` does `spec = self._tools.get(tool_name)` (refusing `scope-listing-not-registered` for unknown names) BEFORE `self._ticket_scopes(sealed_ticket)` verifies the ticket. Verified on base: `invoke(None, "ghost_tool")` -> `scope-listing-not-registered` vs `invoke(None, "read_file")` -> `scope-listing-denied`; `invoke("AAAA.BBBB", "ghost_tool")` -> `scope-listing-not-registered` vs `invoke("AAAA.BBBB", "read_file")` -> `scope-grant-tampered`. A caller with NO ticket -- or a forged one -- distinguishes absent names from present-but-scoped names: an unauthenticated existence oracle over the tool registry. The module documents a DELIBERATE residual ("the two codes are distinguishable") for the invoke path, but that residual presumes a ticket-holding caller; the pre-auth oracle needs no credential at all and defeats the listing seam's headline property ("an unpermitted tool's existence is never confirmed") for anyone who can reach `invoke` and guess deployment-chosen names. The listing seam itself stays silent (probed, HELD) -- the oracle is purely the invoke order-of-checks.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Names only (no scopes, descriptions, or schemas leak); exploitation needs guessing deployment-chosen tool names; it cannot escalate to invocation. The defect is the order-of-checks defeating the silence property pre-auth.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `invoke()` verifies the sealed ticket before consulting the tool registry: a forged/malformed ticket refuses `scope-grant-tampered` for every tool name (no existence signal), and a missing ticket refuses identically (`scope-listing-denied`) for every non-public name while zero-scope (public) tools remain invokable -- consistent with `list_tools(None)`; (2) the deliberate post-auth distinguishability (valid ticket: `scope-listing-not-registered` vs `scope-listing-denied`) is preserved; (3) break-first battery: the w263 probe `scopelist/pre-auth-invoke-existence-oracle` BREAKs on old code, HELDs on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`, and `scopelist/post-auth-distinguishability-residual` stays HELD; (4) adjacent suites green (evals/w262_scopelist_probes.py, evals/w263_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-264 lane A, TDD, red-first).** `ToolRegistry.invoke` now verifies the sealed ticket BEFORE consulting the tool registry: forged/malformed ticket -> `scope-grant-tampered` for EVERY tool name (no existence signal); missing ticket -> `scope-listing-denied` for every non-public name (a missing ticket with an unknown name refuses `scope-listing-denied`, not `scope-listing-not-registered`); zero-scope (public) tools stay invokable with no ticket, consistent with `list_tools(None)`. The deliberate post-auth distinguishability (valid ticket: `scope-listing-not-registered` vs `scope-listing-denied`) is preserved. Verified: `evals/w264_f240f241f242_probes.py` `f242/pre-auth-existence-oracle` BREAKs on base (none: ghost=scope-listing-not-registered vs real=scope-listing-denied; forged: ghost=not-registered vs real=scope-grant-tampered) / HELDs on fix x2 modes (none: denied/denied; forged: tampered/tampered), `f242/post-auth-distinguishability-residual` and `f242/public-tool-no-ticket` HELD; w263 `scopelist/pre-auth-invoke-existence-oracle` flips to HELD and `scopelist/post-auth-distinguishability-residual` stays HELD; adjacent green. Two-axis review: Standards PASS, Spec PASS.

## F243: gov/detectors.py deployment-policy values-overrides are invisible in alert records -- a widening override silently re-arms the rule (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-263 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w263_redteam_probes.py` (probe `detectors/policy-values-override-invisible-in-record`).

**Defect:** `AlertSink._record` journals `exception_decision` = {evaluated, matched, disabled_but_matched, suppressing_exception, decision} -- but not the EFFECTIVE exception values after the deployment policy override is applied (`_effective_block` substitutes `policy["exceptions"][det][exc]["values"]` invisibly). Verified on base: a detector with exception block (host `startswith` ["ci.internal.example"]) plus a policy overriding that block's values to [[""]] (matches every string host -- total re-arm) produces `suppressed` records naming the exception, with nothing in the record attributing the suppression to the policy. The module's alert discipline promises "never silent": suppressions are journaled, and disabling an exception journals the re-arming in `disabled_but_matched` (probed, HELD). The values-override path -- which can widen an exception to match-everything -- leaves no trace: an auditor holding the record, the event, and the registered definition sees a suppression the definition cannot explain and cannot distinguish a policy override from an engine defect. `set_policy` itself is never journaled either, so the override's existence is undiscoverable from the alert journal.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The policy is deployment-owned (a hostile deployment is outside the threat model); the realistic harm is a misconfigured/widening policy silently reducing alert coverage in exactly the way the module promises typo'd policies never do silently ("A typo'd policy must never silently do nothing"). No alert is fabricated and detection (produced events) flows on regardless.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) alert records carry the effective exception values (or a digest of the effective block plus the policy revision in force) so a widening override is attributable from the record alone; (2) break-first battery: the w263 probe `detectors/policy-values-override-invisible-in-record` BREAKs (override invisible) on old code, HELDs (override visible in the record) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; the disable path still journals `disabled_but_matched`; (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w262_alert_probes.py, evals/w263_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-264 lane B, TDD, red-first).** `AlertSink._evaluate_exceptions` now journals `effective_values` (per exception block: the effective `values` actually evaluated plus `policy_overridden`) and `policy_revision` (the sink's deployment-policy revision, bumped on every `set_policy`) in every record's `exception_decision`. A widening values-override is attributable from the record alone: the suppressed record names the exception AND shows the widened values with `policy_overridden: True` and the revision in force; a `set_policy` is discoverable from the journal via the revision step. Break-first battery `evals/w264_f243f244_probes.py` (6 probes): 5 BREAK + control HELD on pristine base in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; 6/6 HELD post-fix ×2. The disable path still journals `disabled_but_matched` and fails closed to alert (control HELD on both). Adjacent suites green: `evals/w262_alert_probes.py` PASS (record-shape schema repointed to the F243-extended shape); `evals/w263_redteam_probes.py` F243 probe now HELD (the 3 remaining BREAKs are the still-OPEN F240/F241/F242 scopelist pins); `evals/f143mem_break.py` 0 BREAK / 11 HELD / 0 ERROR (F175 regression pin). Two-axis review: Standards PASS (1 unused import + 2 nits fixed), Spec PASS (empirically break-first verified via stash against pre-fix code). Taxonomy pin: 1151 (no new decision codes).

## F244: gov/detectors.py DetectorEngine.detectors returns live definition dicts -- runtime mutation bypasses every load-time refusal with no journal (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-263 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w263_redteam_probes.py` (probe `detectors/detectors-accessor-runtime-mutation`).

**Defect:** `DetectorEngine.detectors` returns `dict(self._detectors)` -- a shallow copy whose VALUES are the live validated definition dicts. Verified on base: `eng.detectors["d"]["maturity"] = "experimental"` flips `AlertSink.may_gate_enforcement("d")` from True to False and turns subsequent matches into `observation` records instead of alerts; rewriting `["exceptions"]` changes suppression behavior with no validation. Every load-time LOUD refusal (`detector-unknown-priority`, `detector-unknown-maturity`, `detector-deprecated`, `detector-exception-malformed`) is bypassable post-load -- including `maturity: "deprecated"`, which refuses to load but, set at runtime, is silently treated as a non-experimental tier (the deprecated refusal is load-time only). Nothing is journaled. The registration path deep-copies (`_validate_definition` returns `copy.deepcopy`), so the property accessor is the only mutation leak; and the sink itself re-resolves definitions from `engine.detectors` on every evaluation, so the mutation takes effect immediately in the trusted path.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires engine access (deployment-held); no forged detection is possible, only re-tiering/suppression of the deployment's own detectors. The defect is the validation boundary being registration-time-only while the accessor defeats it silently at runtime.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `DetectorEngine.detectors` returns deep copies (or immutable views) so mutating the returned structure cannot change engine/sink behavior; (2) break-first battery: the w263 probe `detectors/detectors-accessor-runtime-mutation` BREAKs (runtime mutation changes behavior) on old code, HELDs (no effect) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w262_alert_probes.py, evals/w263_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-264 lane B, TDD, red-first).** `DetectorEngine.detectors` now returns `copy.deepcopy(self._detectors)` -- a fresh deep copy per access -- so mutating the returned structure at any depth (top-level keys, nested predicates, exception lists) cannot change engine or sink behavior; `register_all` is the only mutation path and sink paths (`evaluate`, `may_gate_enforcement`) re-resolve via the property. The w263 red-team probe `detectors/detectors-accessor-runtime-mutation` was made fix-aware and is now the standing regression pin: it BREAKs (via the genuine defect mechanics) if the live definition ever leaks through again, HELDs on the fixed code. Break-first battery `evals/w264_f243f244_probes.py` f244 probes (maturity flip, exception rewrite, deep nested predicate mutation): all BREAK on pristine base, all HELD post-fix in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`. Adjacent suites green: `evals/w262_alert_probes.py` PASS; `evals/w263_redteam_probes.py` F244 probe HELD (3 remaining BREAKs are the still-OPEN F240/F241/F242 scopelist pins); `evals/f143mem_break.py` 0/11/0. Two-axis review: Standards PASS, Spec PASS. Taxonomy pin: 1151 (no new decision codes).

## F245: gov/provenance_policy.py hostile input shapes escape as raw exceptions instead of machine-coded refusals (LOW)

**Defect:** the module promises machine-coded refusals on every failure path ("Fail-closed rules (all machine-coded)"; `verify_statement` "raises provenance-statement-unverified on ANY failure (malformed statement, unknown key id, bad signature)"). Three hostile input shapes escape as raw exceptions instead, all fail-closed but contract-breaking. Verified on base, deterministic in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`: (1) `verify_statement` with a signature entry whose `key_id` is unhashable (dict) raises raw `TypeError` from `signers.get(key_id)` -- the lookup is unguarded; (2) `admit_vsa` with a truthy non-dict `verifier` field raises raw `AttributeError` from `verifier.get("id")` -- no type check before the attribute access (the `or {}` only covers falsy); (3) `admit_vsa` with a non-numeric `now` (e.g. a str) raises raw `TypeError` at `issued_at <= now` -- the module never validates `now`, unlike `gov/mesh_auth.py`'s F228-shaped `_validate_now` which refuses non-finite/bool/non-numeric clocks machine-coded before any refusal decision. (The `signature`-entry path is already guarded: a non-dict `sig_entry.get` `AttributeError` is caught alongside `ValueError`/`TypeError`.) Stated honestly: every escape is fail-closed (admission is refused, nothing verifies that should not); the defect is the broken machine-code contract at the admission seam, which downstream policy engines cannot match on.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed in every case; no forgery, no silent admission. The harm is contract-level: callers matching on the closed `provenance-*` vocabulary miss these paths, and a raw-exception crash is not the module's documented refusal shape.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) all three shapes refuse machine-coded (`provenance-statement-unverified` for the key_id shape; `provenance-vsa-refused` for the verifier/now shapes) -- no raw `TypeError`/`AttributeError` escapes `verify_statement`/`admit_vsa`/`evaluate` on hostile input; (2) break-first battery: the three w264 probes BREAK (raw exception) on old code, HELDs (machine-coded) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; genuine statements/VSAs still verify and admit (no cross-breakage); (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w263_provenance_probes.py, evals/w263_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-265 lane F245/F246/F247, TDD, red-first).** `gov/provenance_policy.py`: (1) `verify_statement` skips a non-string (unhashable) signature `key_id` as an unmatchable signer, so the entry falls through to the final machine-coded `provenance-statement-unverified`; (2) `admit_vsa` treats a truthy non-dict `verifier` field as unpinned -> `provenance-vsa-refused`; (3) new module-level `_validate_now` (the F228 clock contract) refuses a bool/non-numeric/non-finite `now` with `provenance-vsa-refused` before any validity decision. The two-axis Spec review caught three sibling hostile shapes on the same seam, fixed in this closure: an unhashable verifier `id` is treated as unpinned (`provenance-vsa-refused`); a truthy non-dict VSA `subject`/`digest` carries no digest (`provenance-subject-refused`); a non-string `verified_level` has no rank (`provenance-vsa-refused`). Break-first battery `evals/w265_f245f246f247_probes.py` (12 F245 probes): all 8 attack shapes BREAK with raw `TypeError`/`AttributeError` on the pristine base (verified via stash against pre-fix `gov/provenance_policy.py`), all 12 HELD machine-coded post-fix in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; genuine statements/VSAs still verify and admit (controls HELD on both). Adjacent suites green: `evals/w263_provenance_probes.py` PASS (depth-1 green check), `tests.test_provenance_policy` 37 OK. Two-axis review: Standards PASS, Spec PASS after the sibling-shape fixes (re-verified break-first).

**Cells:** wave-264 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w264_redteam_probes.py` (probe `meshauth/task-call-drops-subject-binding`).

**Defect:** the module's honest boundary documents the subject-binding composition: "Deployments needing subject binding pass `subject=` (the verified spiffe_id); mismatch refuses `mesh-auth-subject-mismatch`." `MeshTaskAuth.resume()` accepts `subject=` for exactly this ("the paired SVID identity for subject-bound schemes (the scope-ticket case)"). But `MeshTaskAuth.call()` -- the per-call seam every task uses after resume -- has no `subject` parameter at all (`(self, task_id, card, envelope, required_scopes, now)` vs resume's `(self, task_id, card, envelope, subject, now)`). Verified on base by signature inspection, deterministic in both envs. Consequence: a deployment that performs a subject-bound resume gets exactly one bound call; every subsequent `call()` on the task evaluates scope-ticket credentials as Bearer <redacted> (`"ticket:<digest>"`, subject unproven) with no way to opt back into binding. The downgrade is silent -- no code, no journal entry, and nothing in the auth record distinguishes the bound resume from the unbound calls. Stated honestly: the Bearer <redacted> semantics are the module's documented residual, so no denied capability is granted beyond the ticket's own scopes; the defect is the asymmetric seam -- the composition the module promises (`subject=`) is unavailable on the path tasks actually use.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Exploitation needs a stolen/exfiltrated scope ticket (the F240-adjacent shape); scope coverage is still enforced per ticket. The defect is the silent, unavoidable downgrade from subject-bound to Bearer <redacted> on the task call path.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `MeshTaskAuth.call` accepts `subject=` and threads it into `authorize_call` (or the task records the resume-time subject and enforces it on subsequent calls, refusing `mesh-auth-subject-mismatch` on mismatch); (2) break-first battery: the w264 probe BREAKs (call has no subject param) on old code, HELDs (subject honored end-to-end on the task path) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w263_meshauth_probes.py, evals/w263_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-265 lane F245/F246/F247, TDD, red-first).** `MeshTaskAuth.call` now accepts `subject=None` (appended after `now`, backward compatible) and threads it into `authorize_call`, so the subject-binding composition `resume()` already supports is available on the per-call path tasks actually use; a mismatched subject refuses `mesh-auth-subject-mismatch`, and omitting `subject=` keeps the documented Bearer <redacted> semantics (`ticket:<digest>`) unchanged. Break-first battery `evals/w265_f245f246f247_probes.py` (4 F246 probes): the signature probe and the end-to-end probes BREAK on the pristine base (`call` has no `subject` param / `TypeError`), all 4 HELD post-fix in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; the Bearer <redacted> control HELDs on both. Adjacent suites green: `evals/w263_meshauth_probes.py` PASS, `evals/w264_redteam_probes.py` PASS (the `meshauth/task-call-drops-subject-binding` signature probe now HELDs). Two-axis review: Standards PASS, Spec PASS.

**Cells:** wave-264 red-team, 2026-10-01. Standing regression pin: `evals/w264_redteam_probes.py` (probe `meshauth/unauthenticated-task-transitions`).

**Defect:** the task state machine has no caller-authentication concept. `escalate(task_id, required_scheme, reason)` and `abandon(task_id)` take no credential, no envelope, no proof of task ownership -- only the task_id. Verified on base, deterministic in both envs: a party holding no credential at all called `escalate("victim-task", "svid", ...)` and the task transitioned to AUTH_REQUIRED (paused; every further `call` refuses `mesh-auth-task-paused`), and called `abandon("victim-task-2")` and the task transitioned terminally to ABANDONED ("the task will never resume"). The module documents task_ids nowhere as capabilities and states no authorization rule for these transitions; its fail-closed philosophy ("nothing proceeds on a partial verification") stops at the call seam and does not extend to its own state machine. Stated honestly: impact is availability only (pause / terminal kill), not authentication bypass or data disclosure; exploitation needs the task_id, whose secrecy is undeocumented. The `call`-refused path additionally appends to the task's `history` on every refused call, so a task_id holder can also grow another task's history unboundedly -- noted, not separately filed.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. No credential is forged and no data crosses a boundary; the harm is denial of service against another member's task (abandon is irreversible). The defect is the missing authorization on state transitions in a module whose entire purpose is authentication.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `escalate`/`abandon` (and the task registry generally) bind transitions to an authenticated caller -- e.g. the task records its owner's verified subject at `begin` and `escalate`/`abandon` require a credential proving that subject, refusing machine-coded otherwise -- or task_ids are documented and enforced as unguessable capabilities with the transitions rate-bounded; (2) break-first battery: the w264 probe BREAKs (unauthenticated transitions mutate state) on old code, HELDs (refused without the owner's credential) on fixed code, in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; the owner can still escalate/resume/abandon their own task end-to-end; (3) adjacent suites green (evals/w263_meshauth_probes.py, evals/w263_redteam_probes.py).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-01 (wave-265 lane F245/F246/F247, TDD, red-first).** `MeshTaskAuth.begin(task_id, owner=None)` records the task owner's subject (signature backward compatible); `escalate`/`resume`/`abandon` require the matching `subject=` via the new `_require_owner` (constant-time `hmac.compare_digest`) and refuse the new machine-coded code `mesh-auth-not-owner` on a missing/mismatched subject; a task begun WITHOUT an owner has no authorization anchor and refuses every transition (fail-closed). The honest trust model is documented in the module docstring and `begin`: the deployment authenticates the network caller through `authorize_call`/`MeshControl` and threads the verified subject in; this layer compares, it does not mint identities (the F240 `expected_subject` pattern). New taxonomy code `mesh-auth-not-owner` (domain mesh-auth, severity high); pin 1177 -> 1178. Break-first battery `evals/w265_f245f246f247_probes.py` (6 F247 probes): unauthenticated escalate/abandon BREAK on the pristine base (paused/killed another's task), the attacker-resume probe BREAKs (resumed with their own credential); all 6 HELD (`mesh-auth-not-owner`) post-fix in both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; the owner end-to-end control (escalate/resume/abandon) HELDs on both. Adjacent suites green: `tests.test_mesh_auth` updated to the owner-bound API (+3 new refusal tests) OK, `evals/w263_meshauth_probes.py` PASS, `evals/w264_redteam_probes.py` PASS (the F247 probe was made fix-aware and now HELDs). Two-axis review: Standards PASS, Spec PASS.
