## F302: seal_evidence imposes no content contract on the artifact body -- a cert-holder can seal contract-empty evidence and the signature attests compliance it never checked (MEDIUM)

**Cells:** wave-279 sealer-as-authority lane (Chainloop PR #3465 steal), 2026-10-02. Standing regression pin: `evals/w279_sealer_probes.py` (probes `sc01`-`sc07`).

**Defect:** `gov/evidence_bundle_v2.py::seal_evidence` verified the producer's signature (chain-then-binding) but imposed ZERO content requirements on `artifact_body`: any JSON dict signed by a valid cert-holder sealed into an `evidence-bundle.v2` record. The Chainloop PR #3465 root cause, verbatim: "Because the bundle is signed by the same client that decides whether to run that check, a valid signature says nothing about contract compliance." Demonstrated on the wave-278 base: a body `{"invocation_class": "tool_execution"}` with no approval receipt, no digests, and no decision sealed successfully; an unknown invocation class sealed; malformed digest shapes and out-of-vocabulary decisions sealed (battery probes sc01/sc02/sc05/sc06 BREAK on base). There was also no assembler-side pre-check at all, so any future one could have drifted from the sealer (the #3465 drift class).

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): `seal_evidence` never inspects `artifact_body` beyond JSON-serializability -- confirmed by source (the function's only body checks are the signature-shape check and `build_artifact`) and by the battery (contract-empty body seals on base); falsifiable: adding a seal-time contract check flips sc01 to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): contract compliance is enforced elsewhere in the submission path -- falsified: `submit_evidence` / `submit_evidence_with_producer_claim` add the issuance join, producer authorization, and transparency submission, none of which inspects body content. H3 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the transparency log's producer-auth verifier rejects contract-empty bodies -- falsified: `default_producer_auth_verifier` checks the key<->producer binding only.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. A valid evidence certificate is still required (the signature ceremony is intact), so this is not an unauthenticated forgery; but any authorized producer could mint signed bundles attesting compliance with a contract that was never checked -- the signature attests integrity AND implied compliance, and the compliance half was vacuous. "Sell evidence, not the engine" makes this load-bearing: an auditor receiving a sealed bundle cannot tell a contract-complete bundle from a contract-empty one by the signature.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) a body declaring a known invocation class with missing/malformed materials is refused at seal time with the coded verdict `evbundle-contract-refused`, fail-closed; (2) unknown invocation classes are refused; (3) the assembler pre-check and the sealer evaluate the same contract via one shared validator (probe sc04: identical verdicts on N crafted bodies); (4) fully compliant bodies still seal (no regression); (5) adjacent suites stay green (`tests/test_evbundle.py`, `tests/test_decision_codes.py`).

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-279 lane 2; closed 2026-10-02, wave-279 lane 2). Fix: new `gov/evidence_contract.py` (the shared validator: `validate_artifact` / `precheck_artifact` / `validate_or_raise` / `load_contract`, one implementation for both sides) + `gov/evidence_contracts/*.yaml` (tool_execution, approval_decision, redteam_probe: required materials, verdict vocabularies, digest64 chain-integrity shapes); `seal_evidence` validates the contract seal-side BEFORE signature verification (coded refusal), with `invocation_class` pass-through on both submission paths; bodies declaring no class take the documented legacy path; one new decision code `evbundle-contract-refused` (taxonomy 1493 -> 1494). Verification: `evals/w279_sealer_probes.py` 7/7 HELD (5 BREAK on the wave-278 base); `tests/test_evidence_contract.py` 25/25 OK; `tests/test_evbundle.py` green via the battery depth-1 green-check; `tests/test_decision_codes.py` 19/19 OK.

 TripFatigueTracker.note_trip raises TypeError on mixed `now` types at eviction -- the "Total on hostile input" contract is violated (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-279 red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pin: `evals/w279_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f299-eviction-mixed-types`).

**Defect:** `note_trip` documents "Total on hostile input" and `_window_of` never raises, but the bounded-store eviction path compares raw `now` values with `min()` (`oldest = min(self._store.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1][2])[0]` while `rec[2] = now` stores the raw value). A store holding mixed `now` types (e.g. `None` and `int` -- both blessed by the F299 contract as fresh-window-per-call) raises `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'` once the store reaches `max_keys`. Demonstrated: a 4-key store with `now` values `1000`, `None`, `"later"`, `2000.5`; the 5th `note_trip` raises.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): eviction orders by raw `now` -- confirmed by code read and the probe; falsifiable: ordering eviction by insertion sequence instead of raw `now` flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): `_window_of` is the total path -- falsified: `_window_of` is total; the raise is in the eviction comparator, a different line.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The helper has zero product callers (only tests/evals reference `TripFatigueTracker`); this is a contract violation in a defensive accounting helper, not an authorization bypass. Reaching it requires a full store (1024 distinct keys by default) holding mixed `now` types.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) probe `f299-eviction-mixed-types` flips to HELD (eviction never raises on mixed `now` types); (2) the F299 `_window_of` contract probes stay HELD; (3) `tests/test_decoy_grants.py` and `evals/w278_f299_probes.py` stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-279 red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-280 lane 1). Fix: `TripFatigueTracker` eviction no longer orders by the raw `now` value (which has no total ordering across hostile types). The record's third slot now holds a monotonic per-call touch sequence (`self._touch_seq`); eviction picks the least-recently-touched entry by that sequence, which is always total. "Oldest-touched" keeps its call-order meaning; `_window_of`'s F299 contract is untouched. Verification: `evals/w280_f304_probes.py` 8/8 HELD in staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (was 2 BREAK on base: red-team repro + all-hostile eviction); probe `f299-eviction-mixed-types` flips to HELD (w279_redteam 31 HELD / 1 BREAK (F305 expected-open) / 6 RESIDUAL); `tests/test_decoy_grants` 32/32 OK; `evals/w278_f299_probes.py` 9/9 HELD. Two-axis code review (parallel): Standards PASS, no blockers; Spec PASS, no blockers -- close-when criteria met by construction and probe. ## F305:

**RENUMBER MAP (wave-279 merge):** this finding was filed as F303 by the wave-279 red-team lane (completed 2026-10-02 02:34:31 UTC); renumbered because the sealer lane's F302 claims F303 as its next-free number. Body text carried verbatim.

 concurrent decide()/elicit_decision calls double-decide -- check-then-act TOCTOU, nondeterministic terminal status (MEDIUM)

**Cells:** wave-279 red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pin: `evals/w279_redteam_probes.py` (probe `elic-concurrent-burn-no-double-decision`).

**Defect:** `ApprovalQueue.decide()` reads the record (`self.all()`), checks `target["status"] != "pending"`, and much later persists via `self._rewrite(...)` -- with no lock serializing check vs write. Two barrier-synchronized `elicit_decision("decline")` calls both see "pending" and both write a terminal decision: the audit log records TWO `approval_decision` events for one approval (demonstrated deterministically 4/4 with a write-gated interleaving, and reproduced ungated). Worse, a concurrent accept+decline pair yields a nondeterministic terminal status -- observed 4x `approved` / 3x `rejected` over 10 ungated trials, both decisions audit-logged. `elicit_decision` inherits the race: its budget burn is read-then-write and its terminal disposition delegates to `decide()`.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): decide() check-then-act races -- confirmed by the gated-interleaving probe (both threads pass the pending check before either writes); falsifiable: serializing check+write (a queue mutex held across the decision) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the race is in the elicitation budget burn only -- falsified: concurrent bare `decide()` calls (no elicitation) double-decide identically (6/6 trials, 2 decision events each); the elicitation lane merely inherits it.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. The approval decision is the authorization trust boundary: a concurrent accept can silently override a legitimate decline (or vice versa) with last-writer-wins, and the losing decision is audit-visible but not state-reflected. Requires concurrent callers within one process (threads); cross-process callers serialize only through the queue file, which carries no locking either.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) concurrent `decide()`/`elicit_decision` calls serialize -- at most one terminal decision per approval, the loser raises `ValueError`; (2) probe `elic-concurrent-burn-no-double-decision` flips to HELD, and a concurrent accept+decline probe shows exactly one decision event with deterministic loser-refusal; (3) adjacent batteries (`evals/w278_approvalv2_probes.py`, approval-queue unit tests) stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (closed 2026-10-02, wave-280 lane 2).

**Closure evidence:** Per-record decision serialization landed in `gov/approvals.py`. `ApprovalQueue` now keeps a refcounted registry of per-approval `threading.RLock`s (`_decision_locks` + `_decision_locks_guard`; entries evicted at zero waiters so the registry cannot grow; the guard is never acquired while a per-record lock is held, so the two cannot deadlock). `decide()` is a thin wrapper holding the record's lock across `_decide_locked` (the former body, unchanged); `elicit_decision`'s cancel section (7a) and its burn+delegate section (7b) each hold the same lock across a re-read of the record from disk -- the loser finds the record non-pending and is refused via `_refuse` (audit-logged `elicitation_refused`, `ElicitationError`) instead of writing. The 7b coverage was load-bearing: the first fix attempt locked only `decide()`/7a and the close-when probe still broke under a clean env -- file-hash tracing showed the unlocked 7b burn's stale-base splice clobbering a landed cancel back to `pending` (lost update), after which `decide()` read `pending` under its lock and emitted a second terminal decision; holding the 7b lock across re-read+burn+decide closed it. Red-first battery `evals/w280_f305_probes.py` (8 probes): **6 BREAK / 2 HELD on the pristine wave-279 base** (`7849c86`), **8/8 HELD after the fix** -- in staging, 3x under `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`, plus 24 extra gated cancel-vs-decide trials, 0 breaks. Red-team pin `elic-concurrent-burn-no-double-decision` repointed BREAK→HELD (verified HELD on the fixed tree). Adjacent green: `evals/w278_approvalv2_probes.py`, `evals/w279_remediation_probes.py`, `evals/w279_triad_probes.py` all GREEN (depth-1); unit suites `test_decision_codes`/`test_elicitation_contract`/`test_remediation` (86 tests) and approval suites (`test_approvals_d1`, `test_approval_policy`, `test_approval_abuse`, `test_approval_ceremony`, `test_durable_approval` -- 136 tests) all OK. Taxonomy pin unchanged at 1495 (no new decision codes) (lane-time pin; wave-280 merge pin 1541/1541/0 sorted, no new codes from this fix). Residual (documented, out of close-when scope): cross-process callers (web UI + CLI as separate processes) still serialize only through the queue file, which carries no locking -- same as the rest of the queue's writers; the finding's reproducer and close-when are in-process.


## F306: tool_guardrail_run audit records echo credential-shaped guard messages before the elicitation secret ban runs (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-280 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pin: `evals/w280_redteam_probes.py` (probe `triad-secret-msg`).

**Defect:** `ApprovalQueue.elicit_decision(..., guardrails=[...])` evaluates the wave-279 guardrail triad as step 3b and emits each guard run into the HMAC-chained audit log via `self._log` (`gov/tool_guardrails.py::_run_guards` -> `_record_for`, whose reject_content note is `"rejection: %s" % result.message` verbatim). The elicitation secret ban (step 5) fires AFTER the emit: `gov/elicitation_contract.py::credential_material_present` refuses the elicitation with `elicitation_secret_detected`, the record stays pending, and the refusal is loud -- but the `tool_guardrail_run` audit record already carries the credential-shaped message. Demonstrated on the wave-279 push: a guard returning `reject_content("blocking: saw password= hunter2-hunter2-x9 in the request")` is refused by the secret ban, yet `read_log()` shows the `tool_guardrail_run` entry with the secret in its `output_info`. The elicitation contract promises "the secret itself is NEVER echoed into the log" (`credential_material_present` docstring); the new triad seam breaks that promise on the guard-run record. This is a wave-279-introduced regression-class gap: before wave-279 there were no `tool_guardrail_run` records at all, and the triad lane's own report claimed reject messages are "validated by the rationale schema + secret ban" -- true for the elicitation decision, false for the audit evidence emitted one step earlier.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): the step-3b emit precedes the step-5 ban -- confirmed by source (approvals.py:4714-4727 emit; 4779-4795 ban) and by the battery (refused elicitation + secret-bearing audit record); falsifiable: moving the ban before the emit (or sanitizing the record) flips `triad-secret-msg` to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the secret ban also scans guard records -- falsified: it only scans the rendered rationale. H3 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the message is redacted by `_evidence_string` -- falsified: that only truncates.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Exploitation needs a guard whose message echoes attacker-influenced text (e.g. a DLP-style guard quoting the offending argument); guard authors are deployment-trusted, so this is not a remote primitive. The elicitation itself refuses fail-closed, so no unauthorized decision is made; the leak is confined to the operator-visible audit log (which already carries other credential-adjacent records under the DLP strict rules). It matters because the "never echo secrets" promise is load-bearing for the sell-evidence story: an auditor-visible log must not contain the very material the product promises to withhold.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) guard evidence is sanitized before emit -- `credential_material_present` applied to the message/output_info, on hit the record carries a redacted placeholder (never the secret) and the elicitation refuses before any emit; (2) probe `triad-secret-msg` flips to HELD and a sanitize-unit probe shows the placeholder shape; (3) adjacent batteries (`evals/w279_triad_probes.py`, `tests/test_tool_guardrails.py`, approval suites) stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-280 red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-281 lane 1). Closure evidence: `gov/tool_guardrails.py::_sanitize_note` applied at the `_record_for` emit funnel -- credential-shaped guard messages, output_info, and crash notes are replaced with kind-preserving `[credential material withheld]` placeholders before any emit; the crash-tripwire exception now carries only the sanitized note, so the step-3b tripwire refusal reason in `approvals.py` cannot echo a secret either (spec-review catch, probed). Battery `evals/w281_f306_probes.py`: 7/7 probes HELD (reject-content, allow-output-info, crash-note, crash-through-elicitation, verdict-preserved, clean-message-verbatim) in staging and clean env; red-team pin `triad-secret-msg` HELD; adjacent `w279_triad_probes.py` and `tests/test_tool_guardrails.py` green.

## F307: instruction-provenance routing is defeasible by the governed agent itself via plan-trace omission (MEDIUM)

**Cells:** wave-280 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pin: `evals/w280_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f300-omission`).

**Defect:** the F300 closure routes consequential actions through `instruction_provenance.grant_check` inside `ToolExecutor.call()` -- but the driver set comes from the agent-supplied framing kwarg `provenance_driving_units` (`gov/executor.py:9564`, `_provenance_grant_decision`). In the toxic-flow threat model the AGENT is the threat actor (a compromised plan under injection influence), and the agent chooses which content-unit ids drove its action. Demonstrated on the wave-279 push: with provenance context installed (a USER_DIRECT user instruction + a RETRIEVED_UNTRUSTED injection unit), the honest driver set routes (`provlabel-approval-required`, routed=True), but a plan trace that lists ONLY the user unit id -- omitting the injected unit -- returns `allowed=True, routed_to_approval=False, code=None`: the toxic shape executes silently at the provenance seam. The executor's own comment admits "Framing kwargs are agent-supplied metadata, never trusted inputs," yet the routing decision -- the F300 closure's core guarantee that "the toxic-agent-flow shape is never silently executed" -- is computed from exactly such an untrusted input. The F300 close-when criterion (a product authorization path routes through grant_check) is honestly met for honest plan traces, so this is a NEW finding, not an F300 overstatement; but the closure's guarantee does not bind the attacker it was built for. Related documented residual: the seam is opt-in (`set_instruction_provenance` has zero product callers; the operator must arm it) -- this finding is the orthogonal axis: even when armed, a hostile agent evades.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): the driver set is agent-chosen -- confirmed by source (kwarg popped from agent framing at executor.py:9557-9564; grant_check reads req.driving_units verbatim) and by the battery (omission allows silently, honest set routes); falsifiable: server-side driver derivation flips `f300-omission` to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the queue re-derives drivers from the transcript -- falsified: `queue()` receives only the early grant decision. H3 (alternative, FALSIFIED): omitting a unit triggers unresolvable-driver routing -- falsified: unresolvable routing only fires for UNKNOWN ids; omitting an id entirely is invisible.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. This does not bypass policy or approval -- it bypasses the provenance routing that was built to catch the exact attack shape (injection riding user authority). Any action the policy would allow without approval executes silently when the agent omits the injected driver; the approver-facing provenance section never renders because nothing routes. The precondition (a compromised agent that also lies about its plan trace) is precisely the F294 toxic-flow scenario, so the seam's value is limited to honest-mistake cases, not the adversarial case. No data is forged and the audit trail stays intact, which keeps it below HIGH.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) driving units are derived server-side instead of trusted from the agent kwarg -- e.g. the executor matches the action against the operator-installed transcript units (all instruction-shaped units installed this turn are the candidate driver set; the agent's kwarg may only NARROW with a logged, auditable justification, and an installed injection-shaped unit can never be narrowed away silently); or an explicit honest-agent-only contract documented in the F300 entry with the adversarial gap closed; (2) probe `f300-omission` flips to HELD (omission routes) while an honest narrow-down still works; (3) adjacent batteries (`evals/w279_f300_probes.py`, `evals/w278_redteam_probes.py`, executor suites) stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-280 red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-281 lane 2).

## F308:

**RENUMBER MAP (wave-280 merge):** this finding was filed as F306 by the wave-280 FGA lane (committed 2026-10-02 03:16:30 UTC), but the wave-280 red-team lane filed F306 first (committed 2026-10-02 03:08:56 UTC) and keeps the number per the wave-272 earliest-filed rule. Body text carried verbatim.

Single-use ephemeral-grant lease: cross-process replay is a STATED BOUNDARY, not a defect (LOW, informational)

**Cells:** wave-280 lane 3 (ephemeral grants / OpenFGA steal), 2026-10-02. Standing regression pin: `evals/w280_fga_probes.py` (probes `p_single_use_spent`, `p_single_use_requires_registry`).

**Boundary:** `gov/ephemeral_grants.py` `SpentLeaseRegistry` is in-process. Within one process, a single-use lease (`claims["lease"] == "single-use"`) is enforced fail-closed: the lease requires contextual tuples at the check seam, requires a registry (`spent_ledger=`; refused coded `delegation-ephemeral-grant-refused` without one — the revocation-seam precedent: no trustworthy answer, no authorization), and second presentation of the same lease ref is refused coded. Across processes (restart, second executor), the spent set does not persist: a replayed single-use lease with valid tuples would be accepted again. This is the same class as the revocation seam's stated boundary (`gov/delegation_tokens.py` docstring: cross-process revocation propagation needs an external store).

**Why accepted:** the lane's contract is the per-invocation mechanism with fail-closed in-process enforcement; a persistent/cross-process spent-lease store is explicitly out of scope (SPEC.md "Out of scope"). The boundary is documented in three places, not hidden: `gov/ephemeral_grants.py` module docstring + `SpentLeaseRegistry` header, `gov/delegation_tokens.py` docstring, and `~/workspace/teams/wave280-fga/SPEC.md`. A future cross-process store (same shape as a future persistent revocation store) would close it without changing the check semantics.

**Severity rationale:** LOW/informational. The residual is real but bounded: replay requires a second process presenting the same signed lease token with valid contextual tuples — the lease token itself is still human-signed and session-bound, so this is not an unauthenticated bypass; it is a double-spend of an already-authorized grant across a process boundary.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) in-process single-use enforcement holds break-first (probes above HELD); (2) the boundary is documented in the module, the seam docstring, and the lane spec; (3) no code change needed.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed as F306 and closed 2026-10-02, wave-280 lane 3 — accepted stated boundary, documented; renumbered to F308 at the wave-280 merge per the wave-272 earliest-filed rule).

- transform path (`GuardChain.run_hook`): the `guardrail-run` record's rationale is `"transform: <detail>"` verbatim AND the distinct `guard-plugin-transform` record carries `"detail": outcome.detail` verbatim (2 records per transform);
- deny path (`GuardChain._run_one`): the `guardrail-run` record's rationale is `outcome.detail` verbatim (returned-deny);
- raised `PluginDeny`: rationale `"PluginDeny: <exc>"` verbatim (exception text);
- allow path: rationale `outcome.detail or "plugin passed"` verbatim (code-read; same funnel).
Demonstrated on the wave-281 push: a plugin whose transform detail quotes a credential-shaped span (`redacted password= hunter2-hunter2-x9 from args`) lands the credential in both records; a deny detail (`refusing: saw password= hunter2-hunter2-x9 in args`) lands it in the intentional_block rationale; a raised `PluginDeny("blocked: password= hunter2-hunter2-x9 present")` likewise. Same defect class as F306/F310, different emission site: F306's close-when (sanitize the triad `_record_for` funnel) covers only the `as_tool_input_guardrail` adapter path; F310's close-when (sanitize the shield `_run_shields` funnel) covers only shield runs; neither covers `GuardChain._run_one` / `run_hook`.

H3 (alternative, FALSIFIED): `_capped` (2000 chars) redacts -- falsified: it is a length cap on exception text only, on the technical_failure path.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. **Close-when criteria:** (1) GuardChain evidence sanitized before emit -- `credential_material_present` applied to the plugin detail/exception text at the `GuardrailEvidenceWriter.record` calls in `_run_one` and to the `guard-plugin-transform` record's `detail` in `run_hook`; on hit the record carries a redacted placeholder (kind-preserving, matching the F306 convention) and the transform/deny verdict still enforces; (2) probes `f311-transform-detail-echo` and `f311-deny-detail-echo` flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries (lane batteries, guard-plugin suites) stay green. ## F312: Forged `_atomic_normalized` marker skips atomic schema validation; bare KeyError escapes (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-283 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w283_redteam_probes.py` (probe `atomic-forged-marker`).

**Defect:** `gov/battery_lang.py::_ensure_atomic_spec` trusts a spec dict as already-normalized iff it carries `_atomic_normalized: True`. The marker is a plain public dict key -- any caller can set `spec["_atomic_normalized"] = True` on a raw unvalidated dict, skipping `validate_atomic_spec` entirely. The code comment claims "a caller can forge the marker, but only by reaching into this module's privates" -- factually false: no privates are involved, it is one dict assignment. `run_atomic({"name": "x", "_atomic_normalized": True}, {})` then dies with a bare uncoded `KeyError: 'input_arguments'` instead of the coded `AtomicError("atomic-spec-invalid")` the module's contract promises. This is the exact bug class the lane fixed for the `"guid"` key (their own probe `p_raw_guid_dict_not_trusted`) -- the fix reintroduces it one key over.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): forged marker bypasses validation and escapes uncoded -- confirmed by source (`_ensure_atomic_spec` lines 754-757) and by the battery (bare `KeyError`, not `AtomicError`); falsifiable: removing the marker-trust (or validating marker-carrying dicts) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the marker is a deliberate trust boundary -- falsified: the comment itself says "Guard against programmer error, not a trust boundary". H3 (alternative, FALSIFIED): `validate_atomic_args` catches it coded -- falsified: it is the site that raises the bare KeyError.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. No privilege boundary is crossed (same-process caller) and no unauthorized decision is made; the failure is still a loud crash. It matters because the atomic layer's contract is coded, auditable refusals -- an uncoded KeyError from a malformed spec is the loudness gap the lane already judged in-scope for the `guid` key, and the comment's false "privates" claim will mislead future callers into trusting the marker.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `_ensure_atomic_spec` no longer trusts the public marker alone -- either validate every dict through `validate_atomic_spec` (marker deleted after normalization) or scope the marker so a forged one cannot skip the gate; (2) probe `atomic-forged-marker` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries (`evals/w280_batterylang_probes.py`, atomic suites) stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-284 lane 1). **Closure record:** forged `_atomic_normalized` marker now refused LOUD with coded `atomic-spec-invalid` (module-private identity sentinel; `w284_f312_315_probes.py` f312-forged-marker HELD, f312-valid-spec-runs HELD; `w283_redteam` atomic-forged-marker re-verified HELD)

## F313: Failing audit emit silently drops drift events (audit gap) (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-283 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w283_redteam_probes.py` (probe `discovery-emit-failure-drops-event`).

**Defect:** `gov/discovery_scan.py::ToolDefinitionRegistry._record_event` appends to the in-memory `_drift_events` list, then tries the deployment's `emit` sink inside `except Exception: pass` ("emit must never break scan"). With a failing sink, a drift still quarantines (enforcement holds -- `run_rescan` reports `drifted` and `held()` is True) but the `definition_drift` event never reaches the audit log: zero events in the sink, the only copy in-memory and lost on restart. The lane's REPORT claims drift events are "chained into the HMAC log" (executor wiring); the failure path silently drops them with no fallback marker, no loud failure, and no recovery -- a silent audit gap on the highest-severity discovery code (`discovery-definition-drift`).

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): emit failure drops the event silently -- confirmed by the battery (quarantine applied, `drift_events` non-empty, sink empty); falsifiable: a fallback (buffer-to-disk, loud once, or a persistent pending-events queue) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the in-memory list is sufficient -- falsified: it is not persisted by `save()` and is lost on restart while the hold survives, so the post-restart audit trail cannot explain the hold. H3 (alternative, FALSIFIED): emit failure also breaks enforcement -- falsified: quarantine is applied before/around the emit; enforcement held in the battery.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Enforcement is intact (the drifted tool stays held); the gap is audit completeness: the governed re-pin decision later cannot be reconstructed from the chain, and a restart erases the evidence that a drift ever occurred. Matters for the sell-evidence posture: an auditor-visible log must explain every hold.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) a failing emit on a drift/unregistered/re-pin event is never silent -- either the event is durably queued (survives restart) for retry, or the failure is loud (coded refusal/marker) rather than `pass`; (2) probe `discovery-emit-failure-drops-event` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries (`evals/w282_agentscan_probes.py`) stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-284 lane 1). **Closure record:** dead audit sink now fails LOUD with coded `discovery-emit-failed` after one bounded retry (new decision code, taxonomy pin 1587 -> 1588); event kept in the in-memory drift list; `w284_f312_315_probes.py` f313 probes HELD; `w283_redteam` discovery-emit-failure-drops-event re-verified HELD

## F314: Untrusted `|` in a tool name permanently bricks the pin store (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-283 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w283_redteam_probes.py` (probe `discovery-pipe-in-name-bricks-store`).

**Defect:** the observation source is UNTRUSTED by design (`gov/discovery_scan.py` line 23), but `_require_shape` accepts tool names containing `|`. `RegistryStore.save()` serializes key tuples with `"|".join(k)`; `load()` splits on `|` and raises `RegistryStoreError` ("malformed pin entry") on any key that does not split into exactly 4 parts. One hostile (or merely odd) tool name `a|b` therefore writes a 5-part key, after which EVERY subsequent `load()` raises -- the deployment can never restart with its pins again: a persistent self-DoS of pin persistence from untrusted input, with no recovery path short of hand-editing the store.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): `|` in a name bricks load -- confirmed by the battery (`RegistryStoreError` on every load after save); falsifiable: rejecting/escaping `|` in names at `_require_shape`, or length-prefixing the serialization, flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): load's loudness is the designed behavior -- falsified: loud-once is the design; loud-forever-from-untrusted-input is a DoS, and the observation source is untrusted by the module's own contract. H3 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the deployment can sanitize names -- falsified: the module owns the `|`-join serialization format, so it owns the injection.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Loud, not silent: the failure is visible (though only at restart, which delays detection). No unauthorized decision is made and in-memory enforcement still holds; the damage is availability of pin persistence across restarts. A single untrusted observation name should never be able to brick the store.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) tool/agent_host/component names containing `|` are refused (or escaped) at the observation boundary, or the store serialization is injection-proof; (2) probe `discovery-pipe-in-name-bricks-store` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-284 lane 1). **Closure record:** `|` in observed definition names refused LOUD at the observation trust boundary (`_require_shape`), and tool-key parts validated in `check_at_use`/`request_repin`/`approve_repin`; the pin store can no longer be bricked by hostile input; probes HELD; `w283_redteam` discovery-pipe-in-name-bricks-store re-verified HELD

## F315: Re-pin binds to the fresh observation by tool NAME only; a same-name shadow lifts the wrong hold (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-283 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w283_redteam_probes.py` (probe `discovery-repin-binds-by-name-only`).

**Defect:** `approve_repin` (and `check_at_use`) re-observe via `observe_one(tool_key[3])` -- the tool NAME only -- discarding the 4-part `(scope, agent_host, component_id, name)` identity the registry itself uses everywhere else. The discovery domain explicitly models same-name tools across scopes/components (4-scope coverage matrix; 4-part tool keys). With a same-name shadow (component A drifted/quarantined in user scope, component B clean in system scope) and a name-keyed deployment observer resolving to B, `approve_repin(A_key, digest_of_B)` SUCCEEDS: A's drift hold lifts, A's pin is set to B's digest, while component A still serves drifted bytes. Thereafter `check_at_use(A_key, ...)` diffs against B's definition too, so A's drift stays invisible at use time. The bait-and-switch protection's threat model -- "what is served at approval time differs from what was approved" -- is realized through the product's own name-keyed seam, using identity information the product had and discarded.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): cross-component re-pin binds and lifts the hold -- confirmed by the battery (hold lifted, pin == B's digest, A still serves drifted bytes); falsifiable: re-observing by full tool key (or refusing when the name resolves ambiguously) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, PARTIALLY TRUE): name resolution is deployment-owned -- the `observe_one(tool_name)` contract is documented as deployment-supplied. Accepted as a mitigating caveat, but the product chose the name-only call at both call sites when the full key was available, and the shadowing case is in the product's own domain model. H3 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the digest match is sufficient protection -- falsified: the digest matched (B's), and the wrong hold lifted.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires a same-name shadow across components plus a name-ambiguous deployment observer -- not a remote primitive; the deployment's observer implementation is a mitigating factor (caveat H2). Filed because the seam is the product's choice (it discards available identity at the exact point the bait-and-switch protection is supposed to bind), the consequence is enforcement-visible (a drifted tool un-held while still drifted), and the lane's own domain model anticipates shadowing.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) the re-observation binds to the full tool identity -- `observe_one` receives the 4-part key (or the name plus component attribution), or `approve_repin` refuses when the fresh observation's provenance is ambiguous; (2) probe `discovery-repin-binds-by-name-only` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-284 lane 1). **Closure record:** `observe_one` now receives the FULL 4-part tool key (contract change, in-repo call sites updated); observed-definition name must match the pinned identity (identity-mismatch refuses LOUD); probes HELD; `w283_redteam` discovery-repin-binds-by-name-only re-verified HELD

## F316: close_old_findings treats a scan entry missing `reproduced` as closure -- fail-open mitigation with fabricated evidence (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-284 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` (probe `fl-close-old-missing-reproduced`).

**Defect:** `FindingRegistry.close_old_findings` (`gov/finding_lifecycle.py:378`) reads `result.get("reproduced")`; a scan entry that omits the `reproduced` key (or sets it falsy) falls through to the mitigate path, transitioning an OPEN finding to `mitigated`. The recorded evidence note literally asserts "break-first probe no longer reproduces" with `reproduced: None` -- fabricated closure evidence from malformed input. `_require_closure_evidence` only checks key presence of `battery`/`commit`, so values may be `None`. A buggy or hostile scan feed can silently close real findings (SLA clock stops, metrics drop the finding).

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): missing `reproduced` -> mitigated, confirmed by the battery (OPEN HIGH -> mitigated with the fabricated note); falsifiable: malformed scan entries raising `FindingLifecycleError` (loud) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): absence is a valid "no longer reproduces" signal -- falsified: the lane's own docstring frames the sweep as break-first evidence; an absent verdict is not evidence of anything.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. In-process library; the scan feed is deployment-supplied, so exploitation needs feed influence. Filed because closure is the most consequential transition in the state machine and it happens on malformed input with fabricated evidence.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) a scan entry without an explicit boolean `reproduced` is refused loudly (or recorded as a note, never a closure); (2) probe `fl-close-old-missing-reproduced` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-285 lane 2). **Closure record:** `close_old_findings` now requires `reproduced` to be an explicit bool and raises `FindingLifecycleError` LOUD on any malformed entry (missing/None/truthy-string); `_require_closure_evidence` additionally refuses None/empty `battery`/`commit` values; `w285_f324_f316_probes.py` f316 probes 7/7 HELD; `w284_redteam` fl-close-old-missing-reproduced re-verified HELD

## F317: Decode-layer detection evasion -- triple-nested base64 and binary-padded single base64 defeat credential_material_present (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-284 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` (probes `sc-decode-depth-evasion`, `sc-decode-printability-evasion`).

**Defect:** the `secret_canonicalizer` decode contract (the F306 family's detection seam) has two attacker-controllable evasions. (a) `_decode_layers` caps at `MAX_DECODE_DEPTH = 2` (`gov/secret_canonicalizer.py:455,78`): a triple-base64-nested credential shape returns `False` from `credential_material_present` while trivially decoding to a live key. (b) `_try_b64` abandons any candidate whose decode is not >=0.6 printable (`_is_mostly_printable`, line 448): a single-base64-encoded credential padded with binary bytes returns `False`. Both were verified red with the literal key bytes absent from every encoding layer (no vacuous pass). The lane's own battery pins only single-layer decode detection; neither bound is pinned as documented behavior. Defeating detection means credential-shaped bytes cross the F306-family emission funnels undetected.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): triple-b64 of a live key shape evades detection, confirmed by the battery; falsifiable: raising the depth bound or recursing until no more layers flips the probe to HELD. H2 (confirmed): binary-padded single-b64 evades the printability gate, confirmed by the battery; falsifiable: scanning the printable remainder of an abandoned decode flips the probe to HELD. H3 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the depth bound is a documented contract -- falsified: the module docstring presents decode layers as an evasion-semantics feature, and no probe documents the depth-2 bound as intended.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The evasion needs an attacker who can shape the emitted bytes; the fix is defense-in-depth on the detection seam. Filed because the F306 family funnels route through this seam, so detection evasion is emission-funnel evasion.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) triple-nested and binary-padded encodings of credential shapes are detected (or the bounds are pinned as documented contract with a fail-closed rationale); (2) probes `sc-decode-depth-evasion`, `sc-decode-printability-evasion` flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-284 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-285 lane 3).

**Closure record:** (1) `gov/secret_canonicalizer.py` now unwraps decode layers recursively until no more layers decode, bounded by `MAX_DECODE_DEPTH = 10`; a span still decodeable AT the bound yields a fail-closed `SecretFinding` (`detector="decode-depth-bound"`, `kind="over-deep-encoding"`, digest-only, outermost span redacted via `[REDACTED:over-deep-encoding]`) instead of being silently trusted -- so triple-nested, quad-nested, and arbitrarily-nested base64 are detected; non-printable decodes are no longer abandoned (`_printable_runs` scans maximal printable runs >= 16 chars inside the raw bytes) -- so binary-padded single base64 is detected. (2) `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py`: `sc-decode-depth-evasion` HELD (triple-nested b64 detected; 15-deep nesting fails CLOSED via the depth-bound finding), `sc-decode-printability-evasion` HELD (binary-padded b64 detected; the extracted run carries no raw bytes, redacted at sanitize); lane battery `evals/w285_f317_f319_probes.py` 0 BREAK / 16 HELD. (3) Adjacent green: `tests.test_secret_canonicalizer` + `tests.test_campaign` + `tests.test_decision_codes` 78/78 OK; `w283_gitleaks_probes` 0 BREAK / 16 HELD; `w283_caldera_probes` 0 BREAK / 18 HELD; `w284_f312_315_probes` 0 BREAK / 10 HELD; `w283_f311_probes` 0 BREAK / 13 HELD; `w283_redteam_probes` 0 BREAK / 27 HELD; `w284_redteam_probes` 7 BREAK (F316, F318, F320-F324 expected-open; F317/F319 probes now HELD) / 32 HELD. Existing regression `test_non_printable_decode_skipped` stays green (extracted run has no rule keywords). Residual (not filed): a credential split across multiple printable runs by single binary bytes is not gap-joined (would need gap-tolerant matching; outside the finding's close-when).

## F318: replay_campaign executes unverified evidence -- manual_approve downgraded to always-approve, elevation bit taken from the file (MEDIUM)

**Cells:** wave-284 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` (probe `cp-replay-unverified-evidence`).

**Defect:** `replay_campaign` (`gov/campaign.py:741`) re-executes a campaign from an evidence file without ever calling `verify_campaign_records` -- the chain that exists precisely to detect tampering is ignored. A forged JSONL containing only a `campaign-start` line (no valid chain; `verify_campaign_records` returns False on it) was replayed and the step EXECUTED (battery: 1 step ran). Worse, the replay hardcodes `manual_approve=False, approve_fn=lambda name: True` even when the start record says `manual_approve: true` -- the human-approval gate is silently downgraded, leaving only an advisory `replay-note` diff emitted after execution. And `elevation_granted=start.get("elevation_granted", False)` takes the privilege bit from the unverified file. The combination -- unverified chain, approval downgrade, file-controlled elevation -- is a privileged re-execution path with none of the original run's gates.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): forged evidence replays and executes, confirmed by the battery (step ran, elevation bit honored, approval downgraded); falsifiable: verifying the chain before execution and refusing unverified files flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, PARTIALLY TRUE): replay needs the registry, so the caller is already privileged -- accepted as a mitigating caveat: a caller that can invoke replay can also call `run()` directly with elevation. Filed anyway because the replay API is presented as the verification path ("deterministic re-run ... and diffs"), its contract is evidence-integrity, and the silent approval downgrade plus file-controlled elevation are exactly the defects a chain-verifying replay should not have.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. The blast radius is bounded by caller privilege (the registry is caller-supplied), but the defect class -- a verification path that does not verify -- undermines the evidence story the campaign layer sells, and the always-approve downgrade is silent except for an after-the-fact note.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `replay_campaign` verifies the evidence chain (via `verify_campaign_records`) and refuses unverified files loudly; (2) a `manual_approve: true` start record is never replayed with always-approve (refuse, or re-prompt through a caller-supplied approval); (3) probe `cp-replay-unverified-evidence` flips to HELD; (4) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-285 lane 1). **Closure record:** `replay_campaign` now verifies the evidence chain via `verify_campaign_records` BEFORE anything executes and refuses unverified files LOUD (`CampaignError`, no replay evidence produced); a `manual_approve: true` start record is never replayed with always-approve (refused LOUD without a caller-supplied `approve_fn`; with one, the human is re-prompted through it and denials stop the replay as `approval-denied`); the elevation bit comes from the caller (`elevation_granted` kwarg, default False), never from the file (disagreement noted in the diffs, not honored). Red-first battery `evals/w285_f318_probes.py`: 5 BREAK on base -> 0 BREAK / 6 HELD / 0 ERROR; `w284_redteam` probe `cp-replay-unverified-evidence` repointed to the fixed contract and HELD; `tests.test_campaign` 23/23 OK; `w283_caldera` 0 BREAK; `w283_redteam` 0 BREAK / 27 HELD.

## F319: Campaign evidence is an un-sanitized emission site -- raw credential-shaped args/executor notes land in the campaign JSONL (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-284 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` (probe `cp-evidence-emission-echo`).

**Defect:** same defect class as F306 (triad), F310 (shields), F311 (GuardChain) -- a new emission site echoing credential-shaped data with no secret scan on the path. `CampaignWriter` writes attacker-influenced free text with no `secret_canonicalizer` call anywhere in `gov/campaign.py`: the campaign-start record carries the FULL `args_map` in plaintext (while steps deliberately use `arg_digest`), the step record carries `executor_note` (raw executor output, `[:400]`), and `parser_note` embeds raw exception text. Battery: after a campaign whose args and executor note contained a synthetic key shape, the evidence file contained the raw bytes twice (the canonicalizer itself flags 1 finding on the file -- the raw bytes are present). The wave-283 merge composed the canonicalizer into every other emission funnel; the campaign evidence path was not wired.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): raw key bytes in the campaign JSONL, confirmed by the battery (bytes present in start + step records); falsifiable: routing start/step records through `sanitize()` (the `guard_plugins.py:439` precedent) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): campaign evidence is not an audit log -- falsified: it is hash-chained, presented as evidence ("genesis-chained JSONL evidence"), and the F306 family promise is that secret bytes do not reach evidence records.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Same as F311: the exposure is log-shaped credential material, not a decision bypass. The executor/args are deployment-supplied, so the leak needs attacker-influenced tool output or args.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) campaign-start/step records route attacker-influenced free text (`args_map`, `executor_note`, `parser_note`) through the `secret_canonicalizer` seam before writing; (2) probe `cp-evidence-emission-echo` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-284 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-285 lane 3).

**Closure record:** (1) `gov/campaign.py` now routes all three named fields through the `secret_canonicalizer` seam before the evidence write (the F306/F310/F311 composition: span-level redaction with kind-preserving `[REDACTED:<kind>]` placeholders). `_sanitize_args_map` recursively sanitizes string VALUES of the mapping (keys and non-strings pass through untouched; tuples keep their type), the start record stores the redacted `args_map` plus an `args_map_digest` binding the ORIGINAL args for tamper evidence; execution still uses the original args. `_run_one` sanitizes `executor_note` (full text, then `[:400]`) and `parser_note` before the step write. Scope kept to the three fields named in the finding: `seed_facts` (stored as normalized typed tuples, not free text) is unchanged. Honest caveat documented in `run()`/`replay_campaign()` docstrings: replay re-executes with the redacted args as recorded, so a redacted campaign may show verdict-drift on replay -- the expected signal of differing inputs. (2) `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py`: `cp-evidence-emission-echo` HELD (synthetic key in args_map + executor_note: evidence file carries `[REDACTED:...]` placeholders, zero raw bytes; `args_map_digest` present and binding); lane battery `evals/w285_f317_f319_probes.py` 0 BREAK / 16 HELD. (3) Adjacent green: same unit/battery set as the F317 closure record above. Note for the wave-285 merge coordinator: the wave-284 red-team's `cp-evidence-emission-echo` probe never genuinely exercised `executor_note` on the base tree -- its `args_map={"probe": {"target": SECRET}}` was refused at `validate_atomic_args` (the leak_spec declares `input_arguments: {}`), so the executor never ran; the SECRET reached the JSONL only via the campaign-start record. The lane battery ships a fixed probe (`_leak_spec_with_args`, declares `input_arguments.target`) plus a vacuity guard erroring if the executor never ran. Test hygiene gap in `w284_redteam_probes.py`, not a filed finding.

## F320: run_query_pack emits duplicate report entries per query -- second lacks `released`, withdrawals double-counted (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-284 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` (probe `iq-pack-report-duplication`).

**Defect:** `QueryRegistry.run_query_pack` (`gov/inventory_query.py:589`) appends the per-query report block twice: the first append (lines 659-669) carries `released`; then the withdrawn loop repeats (lines 671-675, double-appending every withdrawal) and a second `qreps.append` (lines 676-687) omits `released`. Battery: one query yields `len(report["queries"]) == 2`; after a withdrawal, entry 1's `withdrawn` contains the identity twice and `released` is `None`. Any scheduler/consumer indexing reports positionally or reading `qrep["released"]` sees corrupt data (releases look still-held on the duplicate entry, withdrawals inflated). Enforcement (hold placement) is unaffected -- this is report integrity, the thing the deployment's scheduler consumes.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): duplicate entries with doubled withdrawals and missing `released`, confirmed by the battery; falsifiable: one entry per query, each carrying `released`, flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): consumers can dedupe -- falsified: the dedupe burden is not in any contract, and doubled withdrawals change consumer semantics.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Report corruption only; holds are placed correctly. Filed because the pack report is the scheduled audit's output surface and silent double-counting corrupts downstream automation.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `report["queries"]` has exactly one entry per pack query, each carrying `released`, no duplicated withdrawals; (2) probe `iq-pack-report-duplication` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-285 lane 4). **Closure record:** the duplicated withdrawn loop and second `qreps.append` (which omitted `released` and doubled withdrawals) were deleted from `run_query_pack` (`gov/inventory_query.py`); `report["queries"]` now carries exactly one entry per pack query, each with `released`, and withdrawals counted once; `evals/w285_f320_f323_probes.py` f320-pack-report-integrity HELD; `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` iq-pack-report-duplication now HELD

## F321: Duplicate identity rows silently shadow in register_table_rows/_extension_rows -- a degenerate provider hides rows (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-284 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` (probe `iq-identity-collision-shadowing`).

**Defect:** both `register_table_rows` (`gov/inventory_query.py:392`, line ~410) and `_extension_rows` (line 479) key rows by identity with plain dict assignment -- last-write-wins, no error. Battery: seeding `agents` with two rows sharing `agent_id` "a1" keeps only the second, silently. A compromised or degenerate extension provider can hide rows from every query and pack by declaring coarse `identity_columns` (e.g. `("scope",)`) so all rows collapse onto one identity; the pin then binds the attacker-chosen survivor and the dropped rows are invisible to the drift audit. `row_digest`'s pre-seed stripping is correctly closed; identity collision is the remaining shadowing primitive.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): duplicate identities silently collapse, confirmed by the battery (one row visible, no error); falsifiable: duplicate identities raising `InventoryError` (loud) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): seeding is operator action, so collisions are the operator's bug -- falsified: the extension-provider path takes rows from provider code (a plug-in boundary), and fail-closed is the module's own contract for provider misbehavior.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Needs provider-side control (plug-in boundary) or operator error; the pack audit then binds the wrong survivor. Filed because silent row-shadowing is exactly the shape a supply-chain inventory must refuse.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) duplicate identities within one seed/fetch raise `InventoryError` loudly (or the pack refuses to pin over them); (2) probe `iq-identity-collision-shadowing` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-285 lane 4). **Closure record:** `register_table_rows` and `_extension_rows` (`gov/inventory_query.py`) now refuse LOUD with coded `inventory-identity-collision` (new decision code, taxonomy pin 1621 -> 1622) on duplicate identity keys within one seed/fetch -- no more silent last-write-wins shadowing; `evals/w285_f320_f323_probes.py` f321-identity-collision-loud HELD (seed and provider-fetch paths); `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` iq-identity-collision-shadowing now HELD

## F322: Severity-blind identity dedup -- a HIGH filing dedups onto a pre-seeded LOW canonical and inherits the 3-wave SLA (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-284 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` (probe `fl-severity-blind-dedup`).

**Defect:** `FindingRegistry.file_finding` (`gov/finding_lifecycle.py:263`) dedups on identity-hash alone and ignores severity: the duplicate branch appends to `filings` and returns the canonical number without comparing severity. Battery: pre-file a LOW with a given (seam, attack_shape, close_when); a later HIGH filing with the same shape returns `kind="duplicate"` on the LOW's number, severity stays `low` -- the HIGH gets a 3-wave SLA instead of 1 and never appears in metrics as high. This is a pre-emption attack on the SLA clock (plant a LOW, downgrade the real HIGH) and also the benign unlucky-parallel-lane case.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): HIGH dedups onto LOW with no severity handling, confirmed by the battery; falsifiable: escalating the canonical severity (or filing separately / raising) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): dedup is about shape, severity is triage's job -- falsified: the registry itself drives the SLA clock from severity, so the registry cannot be severity-blind at the same time.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Needs a pre-seeded colliding LOW (attacker with registry access or an unlucky parallel lane); the consequence is SLA dilution, not silent closure.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) a filing whose severity differs from the canonical identity escalates the canonical severity, files separately, or raises -- never silently inherits the weaker SLA; (2) probe `fl-severity-blind-dedup` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-285 lane 4). **Closure record:** `FindingRegistry.file_finding` (`gov/finding_lifecycle.py`) is now severity-aware at dedup: a duplicate filing whose severity outranks the canonical severity ESCALATES the canonical record (audit-noted in `scan_notes`; downgrades never applied, so the canonical always keeps its tightest SLA); severity is also validated up-front on the filing path; `evals/w285_f320_f323_probes.py` f322-severity-aware-dedup HELD; `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` fl-severity-blind-dedup now HELD

## F323: load_findings_md defaults entries without **Status:** to verified -- legacy OPEN findings silently closed on import (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-284 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` (probe `fl-md-import-default-verified`).

**Defect:** `_entry_fields` (`gov/finding_lifecycle.py:452`) sets `status = "verified"` when the entry body has no `**Status:**` marker, despite the `load_findings_md` docstring claiming "nothing is inferred beyond that". Battery: a legacy prose entry with no status marker imports as `verified` (and a `(MEDIUM)` title-end marker still parses severity correctly -- that part holds). `verified` is SLA-excluded (`_SLA_EXCLUDED`) and metrics-excluded, so a legacy OPEN finding lacking the marker is silently closed on import: no evidence, no transition, no SLA. The import path is the registry's onboarding ramp for the whole prose history.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): marker-less entry imports as verified, confirmed by the battery; falsifiable: defaulting to `open`/`under_review` (loud triage) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): the prose history always has markers -- falsified: the heuristic is advertised for legacy prose, which by definition may not follow the current convention.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Import-time only; the consequence is silent closure of legacy findings in the registry's view.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) entries without an explicit status marker import as `open` or `under_review` (never `verified`), or are flagged for human triage; (2) probe `fl-md-import-default-verified` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-285 lane 4). **Closure record:** `_entry_fields` (`gov/finding_lifecycle.py`) now defaults marker-less entries to `open` (human triage) instead of `verified`; `**Status:** CLOSED` still maps to `verified` explicitly, so the governed history parses unchanged; `load_findings_md` docstring updated; `evals/w285_f320_f323_probes.py` f323-md-import-no-silent-close HELD; `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` fl-md-import-default-verified now HELD

## F324: produces on="always" fires on ERROR verdicts -- campaign closes objectives-met with zero real execution (MEDIUM)

**Cells:** wave-284 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py` (probe `cp-produces-always-on-error`).

**Defect:** `CampaignRunner._run_one` (`gov/campaign.py:623`, lines 650-652) filters `produces` entries only for `on=="break"` (needs BREAK) and `on=="held"` (needs HELD); `on=="always"` (a registered `_PRODUCES_ON` value, `battery_lang.py:684`) passes for EVERY verdict, including `ERROR`/`atomic-error` (executor raised, dependency refused). The static `entry["value"]` is written to the FactStore, and `_eval_goals` then counts it toward `objectives-met`. Battery: an atomic whose executor raises, with `produces=[{fact: goal.flag, on: always}]` and an `eq` objective, closes `objectives-met`, `objectives_met: true`, `breaks: 0`, step verdict ERROR. The evidence claims the objective was met; nothing actually executed.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): ERROR-step campaign closes objectives-met, confirmed by the battery (objectives_met true, breaks 0); falsifiable: `always` meaning "any completed verdict" (excluding errors) flips the probe to HELD. H2 (alternative, FALSIFIED): `always` is documented to include errors -- falsified: the static value is written as if the atomic produced it; an atomic that raised produced nothing, so the fact is false and the evidence is false.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Evidence integrity: `objectives_met` is the campaign's success signal (the thing a design partner or auditor consumes); a crashing atomic can manufacture it. The blast radius is bounded by registry control (the produces entry is declared by the atomic author), but the false-success evidence is exactly what the campaign layer sells.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `on="always"` does not fire on ERROR/atomic-error verdicts (or the campaign distinguishes "objectives met by error" loudly); (2) probe `cp-produces-always-on-error` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-285 lane 2). **Closure record:** `on="always"` produces entries no longer fire on ERROR/atomic-error verdicts ("always" = any completed verdict); the fact is withheld, the suppression is recorded on the step record as `produces_suppressed` with coded emission `campaign-produces-suppressed` (new decision code, taxonomy pin 1621 -> 1622); `w285_f324_f316_probes.py` f324 probes HELD (incl. f324-parser-not-on-error: spec-review residual -- an ERROR step's fact_parser could still fabricate facts via the ungated `_run_parser` path; parser writes now gated on completed verdicts with the same coded suppression, closed in-lane); `w284_redteam` cp-produces-always-on-error re-verified HELD

## F325: unbounded regex backtracking in template matchers/extractors -- ReDoS in gov/attack_manifest.py (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-285 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w285_redteam_probes.py` (probes `f325-redos-matcher`, `f325-redos-extractor`).

**Defect:** `validate_template` (`gov/attack_manifest.py`) accepts any `re.compile`-able regex in `matchers`/`extractors`; there is no pattern-complexity gate, step budget, or timeout at run time. Pattern `^(a+)+$` on a 29-byte non-matching observation takes 17.34 s (~1.85x/byte exponential); extractor path `(a+)+$` identical. Unsigned templates run freely at `target="isolated"`, and a signed template from any trusted-but-compromised key runs at production -- the design's load-time vetting (`re.compile` only) does not bound this.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): matcher ReDoS, confirmed by timing probe (17.34 s on 29 bytes); falsifiable: load-time refusal of nested-quantifier patterns or bounded evaluation flips the probes to HELD. H2 (confirmed): extractor path has the same hole (validated after fixing a probe bug: the first probe omitted the required `name` field and was refused for the wrong reason; with `name` present the evil pattern is accepted). H3 (falsified): the DSL matcher path is also affected -- falsified: the closed-vocabulary DSL has no regex engine.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Availability-only: no decision/audit bypass, no confidentiality/integrity impact. Blast radius is the template-evaluation worker, not the governance decision path.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `validate_template` refuses nested-quantifier/backtracking-prone patterns with a coded `manifest-*` refusal, or `run_template` evaluates regexes under a bounded step budget/timeout with a coded refusal; (2) probes `f325-redos-matcher`/`f325-redos-extractor` flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (closed 2026-10-02, wave-286 lane 1).

**Closure record:** `validate_template` now runs every matcher/extractor regex through a load-time static gate (`_check_regex_safety`, `gov/attack_manifest.py`): a hand-written pattern parser builds an AST and refuses -- with the new coded `manifest-regex-unsafe` refusal (`RegexUnsafe`, a `ManifestError`) -- any repetition applied to a nullable operand (`(a*)*`), an ambiguous operand (`(a|a)+`), or a self-overlapping variable-length operand (`(a+)+`, detected via mid(X) ∩ first(X) ≠ ∅; fixed-length operands like `(\d{4})+` are exempt because their iteration boundaries are forced). Group nesting is depth-capped at 64 (the DSL parser's `_MAX_NEST_DEPTH` precedent) so pathological nesting surfaces as the coded refusal, never an uncaught RecursionError. The analysis is deliberately True-biased (documented: `(a|ab)+`, `(ab|ac)+` are refused though linear -- verified empirically); template authors restructure, never silently pass. New decision code `manifest-regex-unsafe` (domain `manifest`, severity low); taxonomy pin 1641 -> 1642 (raw/unique/sorted on source literals; value-token-only repoint across 262 files, history comments preserved). Verification: new battery `evals/w286_f325_probes.py` -- 5 BREAK on pristine base (evil matcher/extractor accepted, all 11 evil variants accepted, no refusal) -> **0 BREAK / 12 HELD / 0 ERROR** after the fix (staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`); `evals/w285_redteam_probes.py` f325 probes now HELD (`manifest-regex-unsafe`), 6 BREAK remain (F326-F330 expected-open); adjacent green (`tests.test_attack_manifest`, `evals/w284_nuclei_probes.py`, `evals/w284_redteam_probes.py`). Residuals (not filed): run-time matching has no step budget -- patterns passing the gate are at most polynomial in input length, which the isolated target's fixture sizes bound; hand-built matcher dicts that skip `validate_template` bypass the gate (documented API requires validation; the red-team seam is `validate_template`).

Red-first battery `evals/w286_f326_probes.py`: 3 BREAK on pristine base (exactly the F326 defects) -> **0 BREAK / 9 HELD / 0 ERROR** on the fixed tree (staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`), incl. no-over-refusal guards (covering `proj/` and `*` policies still succeed) and a prefix-boundary probe (`pro/` vs `proj/a`). `w285_redteam` `f326-update-wraps-scope` / `f326-rotate-scope` re-verified HELD with the coded refusal; adjacent `w284_sops` 0 BREAK / 40 HELD; `tests.test_bundle_envelope` + `tests.test_decision_codes` 41 OK.

## F327: KmsKeyset.from_dict on a ceremony missing new_key_id raises raw KeyError, not coded KeysetError (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-285 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w285_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f327-ceremony-keyerror`).

**Defect:** `_digest_for` (`gov/kms_keyset.py:306`) does `doc["ceremony"]["new_key_id"]` without `.get()`; `_parse` calls it before any structural validation of that field for phases `none`/`complete` (the in-progress check only covers rolling-out/roll-out-failed/verified). `from_dict` on `{"phase": "none"}` with no `new_key_id` raises raw `KeyError('new_key_id')`; the public `_repin` crashes identically. Fail-closed by accident, but callers branching on `KeysetError.code` (repo convention) miss it -- e.g. a request handler turns a coded refusal into an uncoded 500.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Availability/robustness: fail-closed by accident, but the uncoded exception breaks the repo's coded-refusal contract at a deserialization seam that faces persisted state.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) malformed ceremonies refuse with a coded `keyset-*` KeysetError; (2) probe flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (closed 2026-10-02, wave-286 lane 3).

**Closure record:** `_validate_ceremony` (gov/kms_keyset.py) now validates
the whole ceremony shape before the digest is recomputed: a missing or
non-mapping ceremony, an unknown phase, a missing/wrongly-typed
`new_key_id` slot on settled phases, and a missing attempt counter on

primary_key_id) no longer demotes the successor, so the ceremony
completes with the new primary enabled and minting works. The ordinary
rotation path is unchanged (old primary still winds down to disabled).

## F329: keyset content pin is self-contained and recomputable via public _repin -- out-of-band forgery undetectable (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-285 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w285_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f329-pin-self-forgeable`).

**Defect:** The module claims `keyset_digest` pins the configuration "so any out-of-band edit is detectable", but the pin lives inside the document it protects and recomputation needs no secret: `KmsKeyset._repin` is a public classmethod. Repro: `to_dict`, flip a key status to `destroyed`, wipe `audit_chain`, `_repin`, `from_dict` -- accepted, and `verify_chain()` returns True. Arbitrary status forgery + full audit-trail wipe is undetectable at load (unlike `sandbox_policy`'s *external* pin store, the wave-284 precedent).

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): status forgery + chain wipe accepted with valid chain; H2 (held): DESTROYED is terminal *via the API* (7 probes: enable/disable/re-add/rotate-onto all refused); H3 (held): provider posture disagreements refuse loudly; H4 (latent, not filed): edits to non-digested informational fields undetectable but carry no authorization impact.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires write access to the persisted keyset file (0600 perms are the primary control); the digest still catches accidental corruption. But the documented "detectable" claim is false against malicious writers.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) the pin moves to an external pin store (the `sandbox_policy` precedent) or becomes a keyed MAC over the document, so out-of-band edits are detectable; (2) probe flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-285 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-286 lane 4).

**Closure record (wave-286 lane 4):** `keyset_digest` is now a keyed MAC (HMAC-SHA256, domain-separated) under a deployment-held 256-bit pin key. `new`/`from_dict`/`_repin` REQUIRE the key and refuse LOUD and coded (`keyset-pin-key-invalid`) without it -- there is no silent fallback to an unkeyed pin. A writer holding only the document cannot recompute the pin: the F329 attack (flip status, wipe `audit_chain`, keyless `_repin`, `from_dict`, `verify_chain() == True`) now refuses at the keyless `_repin` step, and a stale pin fails closed at load (`keyset-verify-failed`, `hmac.compare_digest`). New module helpers `generate_pin_key` (0600, atomic, refuses overwrite) / `load_pin_key` (size-checked, LOUD). Trust model documented honestly in the class docstring: a holder of the pin key is the authorized operator and can re-pin; that is the intended use of `_repin`, never a back door. New decision code `keyset-pin-key-invalid` (low); taxonomy pin 1641 -> 1642. Battery `evals/w286_f329_f330_probes.py`: base 4 BREAK (incl. the F329 attack) -> fixed 0 BREAK / 7 HELD / 0 ERROR (staging + clean env + depth-1 green checks); standing `evals/w285_redteam_probes.py` F329 probe re-pinned to the fixed contract -> HELD; `evals/w284_tink_probes.py` 0 BREAK / 11 HELD; unit `tests/test_kms_keyset.py` 45/45 (incl. 8 new pin-key contract tests). No new findings filed.

## F330: CompiledPolicy is mutable after the pin check -- enforcement flips while the stale digest still matches (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-285 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w285_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f330-policy-mutable-after-pin`).

**Defect:** `check_policy_use` (`gov/sandbox_policy.py:751`) compares the compile-time cached `policy.digest` string and never recomputes it from the live object; `_rule_denies`, `allow`, `namespaces` are plain mutable attributes. Repro: `compile_policy` -> `pin_policy` -> `check_policy_use` (passes) -> `p._rule_denies.discard("execve")` -> `bind` (pin re-check passes on the stale digest) -> `decide("execve")` flips `kill` -> `allow`. The gate's promise ("a sandbox never runs under a drifted policy") is broken for in-process mutation.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires a holder of the in-process `CompiledPolicy` reference (buggy or compromised deployment code, not the supervised tool script). Cheap fix: recompute the digest from `_normalized()` inside `check_policy_use`, or freeze the compiled attributes.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) post-check mutation is detected (`sandbox-policy-drift`) or the compiled object is immutable; (2) probe flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-285 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-286 lane 4).

**Closure record (wave-286 lane 4):** defense in depth, both halves of the close-when. (a) `CompiledPolicy` is now immutable after compilation: all attributes are frozen containers (`frozenset`/`tuple`/`MappingProxyType`) and `__setattr__`/`__delattr__` refuse once `__init__` finishes, so the F330 attack (`p._rule_denies.discard("execve")` after the gate) is blocked at the source with `AttributeError`. (b) `check_policy_use` recomputes the digest from the LIVE object via `_normalized()` (constant-time `hmac.compare_digest` against the pin) instead of trusting the cached digest string -- even a freeze-bypassing in-process edit (`object.__setattr__`) is caught as `sandbox-policy-drift`. The normalized digest now also covers the derived `_rule_denies`/`_rule_allows` sets (the bypass probe caught that the first cut missed them: `decide()` reads the derived sets, so they must be pin inputs). Legitimate compile -> pin -> check -> bind -> decide flow unchanged (`evals/w284_nsjail_probes.py` 0 BREAK / 15 HELD). Battery `evals/w286_f329_f330_probes.py`: base 4 BREAK (incl. both F330 attacks) -> fixed 0 BREAK / 7 HELD / 0 ERROR; standing `evals/w285_redteam_probes.py` F330 probe re-pinned to the fixed contract -> HELD. No new findings filed.

**Defect:** the repo's coded-refusal contract (F327 precedent) is that public seams refuse LOUD with a coded exception; callers branching on `AnchorError.code` miss raw exceptions. **Severity rationale:** LOW. Robustness: both paths fail (nothing is silently accepted), but the uncoded exception breaks the repo's coded-refusal contract at public seams that face caller-supplied input (a checkpoint note assembled by a deployment) and operator-supplied paths.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) both seams refuse with coded `AnchorError` (new or existing `anchor-*` codes); (2) probes `f331-uncoded-render-sig`/`f331-uncoded-logroot-file` flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

missing-key / non-string sigs refuse `anchor-checkpoint-invalid`),

string (`anchor-checkpoint-invalid`), `TransparencyLog.__init__` guards
`os.makedirs` (file-as-`log_root` refuses `anchor-log-corrupt`;
