## F332: whitespace-only justification satisfies the mandatory-justification control in gov/governed_exceptions.py (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-286 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w286_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f332-whitespace-justification`).

**Defect:** `ExceptionStore.grant` enforces `len(justification) >= MIN_JUSTIFICATION_CHARS (20)`, and the module's core control is "a justification must say something". A justification of 20 spaces (or a tab/newline/space mix) says nothing but passes the length check: the exception is granted, audited as granted, and covers evaluations as SKIPPED. The control is bypassed while its letter is satisfied. Confirmed on the wave-285 base (19-char justification is correctly refused with `exception-justification-missing`; 20 spaces accepted).

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): 20-space justification granted; H2 (confirmed): whitespace-mix (tabs/newlines) granted; H3 (held): sub-20-char justifications still refused; H4 (falsified): empty-string justification accepted -- falsified: refused.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Governance-bypass of a human-facing control: the justification exists to force a human to write a reason; whitespace defeats the purpose while leaving a "justified" audit trail. Requires an approved approver (the bypass is laziness/malice by an insider approver, not an outsider break-in).

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `grant` refuses whitespace-only (and blank-equivalent) justifications with a coded refusal (e.g. strip-then-length check); (2) probe `f332-whitespace-justification` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-287 lane 2): `ExceptionStore.grant` in `gov/governed_exceptions.py` now applies the `MIN_JUSTIFICATION_CHARS` (20) floor to the STRIPPED justification (fail-closed reading: the floor measures meaningful content, not raw bytes). Whitespace-only (20 spaces, tab/newline/space mixes) and sub-20-stripped justifications refuse LOUD with the existing coded `exception-justification-missing`; legitimate padded justifications still grant (no over-refusal). The digest and stored record keep the raw text (no digest-semantics change); zero-width-space padding is explicitly out of scope (documented). Verification: `evals/w287_f332_probes.py` 3 BREAK (defects reproduced on pristine base) → **0 BREAK / 7 HELD / 0 ERROR** (staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`); `w286_redteam` F332 probe → HELD (F331×2/F333 remain BREAK, other lanes' work); unit `test_governed_exceptions` 27/27, `test_exception_ttl` + `test_policy_exception` 48/48; `w285_exceptions` 0 BREAK. Taxonomy pin unchanged (1660/1660/0/sorted, no new codes).

## F333: WitnessPolicy accepts duplicate public keys under distinct key ids -- one witness satisfies a quorum of N (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-286 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w286_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f333-dup-witness-keys`).

**Defect:** `WitnessPolicy.__init__` validates each witness key's format (32-byte hex) and that `quorum` is in `[1, len(witnesses)]`, but never checks key UNIQUENESS across key ids. The module documents a "quorum of DISTINCT witnesses". Repro on the wave-285 base: pin the same Ed25519 public key under `w1` and `w2` with `quorum=2` -- the policy is accepted; `await_publication` with `witness_seeds={"w1": seed, "w2": seed}` (ONE real key) succeeds (the `_cosign` fail-fast counts distinct key ids, not distinct keys); `check_witness_quorum` counts 2/2 and the checkpoint verifies. A single compromised witness key satisfies any quorum when the policy pins it under N ids. The policy is pinned by the auditor out-of-band, so exploitation needs a misconfigured (or attacker-influenced) policy -- but the module is the last line of defense for its own documented "distinct witnesses" semantic and performs no check.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): duplicate-key policy accepted; H2 (confirmed): end-to-end quorum satisfaction with one key (issuance + count 2/2 + verify); H3 (falsified): the operator's key id double-counts as a witness -- falsified: both `_cosign` and `check_witness_quorum` exclude the operator key id; H4 (falsified): a duplicated signature LINE double-counts -- falsified: `seen` set counts each key id once; H5 (falsified): removing a witness line still passes -- falsified: quorum fails LOUD.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires a misconfigured witness policy (auditor pins one key under two ids); the operator-issuance path is otherwise sound (fail-fast on under-quorum seeds, seed/key match enforced). But it silently voids the quorum's compromise-threshold promise: the auditor believes two independent witnesses are required when one suffices.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `WitnessPolicy` refuses duplicate public keys across key ids with a coded `anchor-witness-quorum-failed` refusal (or canonicalizes by key); (2) probe `f333-dup-witness-keys` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-286 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-287 lane 3).

**Closure record:** `WitnessPolicy.__init__` (gov/evidence_anchor.py) now tracks seen public-key material across key ids and refuses LOUD with coded `anchor-witness-quorum-failed` when the same 32-byte key is pinned under more than one key id. Refusal-at-construction (not canonicalization): the receipts module's `_cosign` validates `isinstance(witness_policy, WitnessPolicy)`, so the shared root covers `gov/evidence_receipt.py` witness cosigning too — a duplicate-key policy can never be constructed on either path. Verified red-first: evals/w287_f333_probes.py 2 BREAK / 3 HELD on base -> 0 BREAK / 7 HELD / 0 ERROR (staging + clean env, depth-1 green checks w285_tessera and w286_receipts all-HELD); the w286_redteam `f333-dup-witness-keys` probe flips to HELD (`duplicate-key policy refused: anchor-witness-quorum-failed`); units tests.test_evidence_anchor + tests.test_evidence_receipt + tests.test_decision_codes 79/79 OK; taxonomy pin unchanged 1660/1660/0/sorted (no new codes). Residual (not filed): post-construction in-process mutation of `policy.witnesses` is not guarded — same in-process threat class as F330's pre-fix state; construction is the documented trust boundary.

## F334: suppress_with_exception binds the exception scope by caller discipline, not to the denied alert (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-287 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w287_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f334-scope-not-bound`).

**Defect:** `suppress_with_exception` (`gov/tool_call_policy.py`) takes the exception `scope` as a free caller parameter and never binds it to the suppressed alert. The docstring states the scope value "must name the denied tool or the policy", but the code only checks `scope[0] in ("tool", "policy")` and exact-matches the scope against the store -- it never verifies that a `("tool", X)` scope names the denied alert's tool or that a `("policy", P)` scope names the compiled policy. Repro on the wave-286 base: DENY decision for tool-b; live exception granted for `("tool", "tool-a")`; `suppress_with_exception(comp, alert_hash, store, "CHECK", ("tool", "tool-a"))` records the tool-b alert as SKIPPED under the tool-a exception digest (action=SKIPPED, verdict=DENY, `suppressed_alert_identity` = tool-b's hash, `scope` = tool-a). A confused or compromised deployment attributes tool-b's accepted risk to tool-a's approval. The alert lookup is already "best effort" by identity hash; the binding check is simply absent.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The verdict stays DENY (no enforcement bypass); the mismatch is visible in the suppression record (`scope` vs `suppressed_alert`), so an auditor can spot it. But it silently voids the scope-binding promise that makes governed exceptions least-privilege: the module is the last line of defense for binding accepted risk to the specific tool/policy the approver approved, and it performs no check.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `suppress_with_exception` refuses LOUD with a coded refusal when a `("tool", X)` scope does not name the suppressed alert's tool, or a `("policy", P)` scope does not name the compiled policy; (2) probe `f334-scope-not-bound` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-287 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-288 lane 1). Closure: `suppress_with_exception` (`gov/tool_call_policy.py`) now binds the exception scope to the suppressed alert in code, before consulting the store: the alert is resolved by identity hash; an unknown alert refuses LOUD; a `("tool", X)` scope must fnmatch-cover the alert's tool (the module's existing tool-naming semantics) and a `("policy", P)` scope must name the compiled policy by name or digest; anything else refuses LOUD with the new coded `toolcall-exception-scope-mismatch`. New decision code `toolcall-exception-scope-mismatch` (domain `toolcall`, severity low); taxonomy pin 1684 -> 1685. Battery `evals/w288_f334_f337_probes.py`: 0 BREAK / 17 HELD / 0 ERROR (staging and clean env); `w287_redteam` probe `f334-scope-not-bound` flips to HELD; adjacent units 126/126 OK.

## F335: uncoded exceptions escape the keyset pin-key custody seams (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-287 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w287_redteam_probes.py` (probes `f335-pinkey-stale-tmp`, `f335-pinkey-malformed-doc`).

**Defect:** the wave-286 keyed-pin hardening (`gov/kms_keyset.py`) left raw builtins escaping at the key-custody seams, breaking the repo's coded-refusal contract (F327/F331 class). (a) `generate_pin_key`: a stale `<path>.tmp` raises raw `FileExistsError` -- the `os.open(..., O_EXCL)` sits outside the try/except that wraps failures as coded `keyset-pin-key-invalid` -- and the path is never created, so every subsequent call fails identically: generation for that path is permanently bricked until the tmp file is manually removed. (b) `_repin`/`from_dict` on malformed documents: non-ASCII `keyset_digest` raises raw `TypeError` from `hmac.compare_digest`; an audit entry lacking `digest` raises raw `KeyError` from `_mac_for` (runs before the pin comparison); a non-mapping audit entry raises raw `TypeError`; `_repin` on docs missing `keys`/`audit_chain`/`format` raises raw `KeyError` (only the missing-ceremony case is caught coded via `_validate_ceremony`). All cases refuse (fail-closed on the data), but operator tooling branching on `KeysetError.code` crashes instead of handling a coded refusal.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. No forgery path (every case refuses); fail-closed on the data. But the uncoded crash on (a) is an operational DoS with manual-cleanup recovery, and (b) re-opens the exact F327-class seam the wave-286 lane closed.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `generate_pin_key` wraps the stale-tmp case in a coded `keyset-pin-key-invalid` refusal (and either cleans up or reports the bricking loudly); malformed documents refuse with coded `keyset-verify-failed`/`keyset-ceremony-incomplete` at every `_repin`/`from_dict` seam; (2) probes `f335-pinkey-stale-tmp`/`f335-pinkey-malformed-doc` flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-287 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-288 lane 2). Closure: `generate_pin_key` wraps the stale-tmp case, the directory creation, and the write/replace tail in coded `keyset-pin-key-invalid` refusals -- the stale-tmp refusal names the recovery (the tmp file is NOT a live key file; remove it manually and retry); `_mac_for` extraction is fail-closed (any KeyError/TypeError/IndexError/AttributeError becomes coded `keyset-verify-failed`); the `_parse` digest comparison is explicit about non-ASCII candidates before `hmac.compare_digest`. Battery `evals/w288_f335_f336_probes.py`: 8 defect BREAKs on pristine base -> 0 BREAK / 15 HELD / 0 ERROR (staging + clean env); w287_redteam F335 probes HELD.

## F336: load_pin_key silently loads a world-readable pin key (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-287 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w287_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f336-pinkey-perms`).

**Defect:** `load_pin_key` (`gov/kms_keyset.py`) size-checks the key file but performs no permission check: a 0600-generated key file `chmod 644`'d (copy, backup restore, umask slip) loads silently with the round-trip intact. The module's own trust model (class docstring) says "the pin key lives in a separate 0600 file" -- nothing enforces the precondition at load. The deployment then believes the pin is a deployment-held secret while it is world-readable on the host.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Hygiene fail-open, not a forgery: the threat model assumes the operator guards the file. But the module could cheaply verify its own precondition and report LOUD instead of silently accepting a weakened posture.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `load_pin_key` refuses LOUD (coded) when the key file is group/other-readable, or documents the deliberate non-check with a rationale; (2) probe `f336-pinkey-perms` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-287 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-288 lane 2). Closure: `load_pin_key` now `os.stat`s the file and refuses LOUD with coded `keyset-pin-key-invalid` before reading any bytes when the mode is group/other-readable (0600 stays loadable; 0644 and 0640 both refused). Battery `evals/w288_f335_f336_probes.py`: 0 BREAK / 15 HELD / 0 ERROR; w287_redteam `f336-pinkey-perms` HELD.

## F337: bind_receipt signs anchor tuples it never re-verifies (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-287 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w287_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f337-bind-no-reverify`).

**Defect:** `bind_receipt` (`gov/evidence_receipt.py`) fail-fasts the operator seed (checkpoint operator-signature check) and the witness quorum at issuance, but never re-verifies that `anchored["inclusion_proof"]` chains `anchored["bundle_digest"]` to the checkpoint root. A fabricated anchor dict (digest swapped to an unrelated-but-valid digest) produces a fully operator-signed receipt whose payload confirms the swapped digest. `verify_receipt_offline` fails closed (`receipt-inclusion-mismatch`), so no false acceptance is possible -- the impact is issuance-side confusion: a corrupted/buggy anchor pipeline (or confused caller holding the operator seed) mints operator-signed receipts that every auditor will reject, and the failure surfaces only at audit time instead of at issuance where the module's own fail-fast philosophy already checks the seed and the quorum.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. No false acceptance (verify fails closed); an external attacker without the operator seed cannot reach this (wrong seed refuses at bind). But it is inconsistent with the module's documented issuance-time checks and turns a pipeline bug into signed-but-dead receipts.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `bind_receipt` re-verifies the inclusion proof (digest -> root) before signing and refuses LOUD with a coded refusal on mismatch; (2) probe `f337-bind-no-reverify` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-287 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-288 lane 1). ## F338: DENY arg carve-outs evaded by explicit null / wrong-typed args (MEDIUM)

**Cells:** wave-287 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w287_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f338-deny-null-arg`).

**Defect:** `_args_satisfy` (`gov/tool_call_policy.py`) with `deny_semantics=True` treats a *missing* arg key as a match (fail-closed, documented) but requires a *present* arg to satisfy its matcher -- and `_match_value` returns False for `None`/non-string values. With a "broad ALLOW + narrow DENY carve-out" policy, `{"cmd": "rm -rf /"}` -> DENY and `{}` (missing) -> DENY, but `{"cmd": None}` -> **ALLOW**, `{"cmd": 5}` -> ALLOW, `{"cmd": ["rm -rf /"]}` -> ALLOW. Same for `regex`/`prefix`/`any_of` carve-outs (`path=None` dodges `^/etc/.*`). The documented "fail-closed on under-specification" guarantee holds only for key-absence, not for the wire-equivalent null -- and null is what common JSON serializers emit for unset optionals, so benign callers silently opt out of the carve-out too. Repro on the wave-286 base via `compile_policy` + `decide` (probe in battery).

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Defeats an explicit DENY rule using only caller-controlled args, and the caller is the authorization module's primary threat actor. Bounded end-to-end by the tool's own None-handling, but the authorization contract is violated at the seam: the module's core promise is broken by a one-token change (omit -> null).

**Close-when criteria:** (1) under DENY semantics, null/ill-typed arg values are treated as missing (fail-closed match), or matchers explicitly refuse them coded; (2) probe `f338-deny-null-arg` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-287 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-288 lane 3). Fix: `_args_satisfy` in `gov/tool_call_policy.py` now treats a null or ill-typed arg value as missing under DENY semantics (new `_value_evaluable` mirrors the matchers' validated type contract: str for equals/prefix/regex, scalar for any_of) -- `{"cmd": None}`, `{"cmd": 5}`, `{"cmd": ["rm -rf /"]}` all match the DENY carve-out fail-closed. The ALLOW path is unchanged (already fail-closed on ill-typed args). Battery `evals/w288_f338_f339_probes.py`: 0 BREAK / 11 HELD (incl. no-over-refusal guards: benign well-typed args still ALLOW; missing-arg behavior unchanged).

## F339: ReDoS residual in tool_call_policy is independently exploitable -- the F325 gate is not routed (MEDIUM)

**Cells:** wave-287 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w287_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f339-toolpolicy-redos`).

**Defect:** `gov/tool_call_policy.py` documents regex backtracking as a "residual", but the residual is caller-triggerable and the in-tree defense is not wired in: the module has zero references to `_check_regex_safety`/`attack_manifest` (grep-verified); `_validate_arg_matchers` enforces only `MAX_REGEX_LEN=256` + `re.compile`. Caller-controlled arg values pass through `re.fullmatch` at decide time, so the *caller* (the actual threat-model attacker for an authorization module, not just a malicious operator) hangs the deciding thread: operator-plausible pattern `^([a-z]+)*$` with input `"a"*n+"!"` measured 0.00s/0.11s/2.44s at n=15/20/25 (exponential; ~30 chars never returns). The F325 gate in `gov/attack_manifest.py` *would* refuse exactly this pattern class ("nested/overlapping quantifiers") -- the defense exists in-tree but isn't routed.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Availability-only, but the attacker is the governed caller itself (the primary threat actor), the target is the authorization decision path, and the fix is wiring an existing in-tree gate -- a genuine coverage miss of F325's closure, not a new unknown-unknown.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) arg-matcher regexes pass through the F325 `_check_regex_safety` gate (or equivalent) at compile time, refusing the dangerous pattern class coded; (2) probe `f339-toolpolicy-redos` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-287 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-288 lane 3). Fix: `_validate_arg_matchers` in `gov/tool_call_policy.py` now routes every arg-matcher regex through the shared F325 `_check_regex_safety` gate (same mechanism, not a duplicate); backtracking-prone patterns are refused at compile with the new coded `toolcall-regex-unsafe` refusal (the ManifestError is translated, never let escape raw). Taxonomy pin 1684 -> 1685. Battery `evals/w288_f338_f339_probes.py`: 0 BREAK / 11 HELD (incl. no-over-refusal: ordinary anchored patterns `^rm -rf /$`, `^/etc/.*`, `^\d{4}$` still compile).

Repro on the wave-286 base (probe in battery).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires in-process reference access (malicious CUSTOM authorizer, compromised plugin); the deployment process is the trust boundary and such an attacker has easier paths. Still a genuine gap between the documented "bound to a pin" guarantee and the implementation.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `_doc` frozen (F330 pattern: MappingProxyType/frozen attrs) or the pin re-verified per `decide()`; (2) probe `f340-policy-not-frozen` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

## F343: RULE_OPERATOR_TRUST affirms on a producer_id string match -- pinned key ids never consulted (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-288 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w288_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f343-operator-trust-name-only`).

**Defect:** `gov/trust_vector.py`'s `operator-trust` dimension rule affirms whenever `evidence.producer_id in policy.trust_anchors`, but no signature exists anywhere in the evidence model and the pinned key ids in `trust_anchors` (which `compile_policy` requires to map producer id -> key id) are never consulted -- grep shows the only use of `trust_anchors` is that membership test. Key rotation changes nothing; a claimant needs no key at all to be "affirmed"; the key id is decoration. The module's honest-limitations block says appraisal runs over declared claims and that anchors are pinned out of band, but does not disclose that operator-trust is name-only, so an operator who believes key-pinning provides authentication is wrong.

**Ranked falsifiable hypotheses:** H1 (confirmed): evidence from producer "prodA" with trust_anchors {"prodA": "keyid-..."} appraises overall affirmed with zero signatures in the pipeline; H2 (falsified): the key id is verified somewhere -- falsified: the only reference is the membership test; H3 (held): endorsed-match dimensions still require endorsements (the honest limitation made structural).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The evidence model is explicitly declared-claims, not observed runtime; the gap is semantic (the trust-anchor contract overpromises). An attacker who can submit evidence as a named producer gets an affirmed vector under operator-trust without any key -- but submission is itself the privileged act in this model.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) operator-trust requires key-based producer verification (signed evidence bound to the pinned anchor key), or the dimension is renamed/re-documented to a name-allowlist with the key-id requirement removed from the policy contract; (2) probe `f343-operator-trust-name-only` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-288 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-02, wave-289 lane 1). Closure: the second close-when option was taken -- key-based verification would be bolted-on theater because the evidence model carries no signatures anywhere (declared-claims; submission is the privileged act in this model). `trust_anchors` (producer id -> key id) was RENAMED to `trusted_producers` (producer id -> non-empty authority label): `compile_policy` refuses LOUD coded `trustvec-policy-invalid` when the old key-implying field is present, and the module's honest-limitations block now discloses the name-allowlist contract ("operator-trust is a NAME-ALLOWLIST over declared producer_id values"). No new decision codes; taxonomy pin stays 1700. Battery `evals/w288_f343_probes.py`: 0 BREAK / 8 HELD / 0 ERROR (staging and clean env); `w288_redteam` probe `f343-operator-trust-name-only` flips to HELD; adjacent units 45/45 OK; `w287_ear` 0 BREAK.

## F349: admit_at_risk's floor gate reads a caller-synthesized field -- a refuse dict omitting floor_failed admits at risk (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-289 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w289_redteam_probes.py` (probe `f349-forged-refuse`).

**Defect:** `admit()` RAISES on REFUSE (it never returns a refuse decision record), so every `refuse_decision` dict passed to `admit_at_risk` is caller-synthesized; nothing binds it to the actual `admit()` outcome, and `decision_digest` is an unkeyed content hash the caller computes. `admit_at_risk` refuses floor-failed evidence only when `refuse_decision.get("floor_failed")` is truthy. A caller that synthesizes `{"verdict": "REFUSE", "policy_id": "p1"}` without `floor_failed` -- or an attacker able to influence that dict -- gets `ADMIT-AT-RISK` for evidence whose floor checks failed. The module's "the integrity floor can NEVER be exceptioned" guarantee is caller-attested, not mechanism-enforced. Repro: grant a live `SAS_ADMISSION_ACCEPT_RISK` exception for `("policy", "p1")`, call `admit_at_risk` with the synthesized dict -> `ADMIT-AT-RISK` returned.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The synthesizing caller is the operator's own workflow code (trusted); the evidence producer cannot reach this seam. Filed because the guarantee is stated unconditionally ("NEVER") while the mechanism cannot distinguish a faithful reconstruction from a careless or hostile one, and the floor-failure detail does not survive the `admit()` raise in any machine-checkable form.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) the floor-failed state is mechanism-bound: e.g. `admit()` returns (as well as raises) the refuse record, or the `AdmissionError` carries the decision record, or `admit_at_risk` re-derives floor status instead of trusting the dict; (2) probe `f349-forged-refuse` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (closed 2026-10-02, wave-290 lane 2 (`admit()` registers a bounded-1024 deepcopy of every REFUSE decision in `_REFUSE_REGISTRY` and raises it on `AdmissionError.err.decision`; `admit_at_risk` takes ONLY the error `admit()` raised -- synthesized/forged/unregistered inputs refuse coded `admission-exception-refused`; `evals/w290_f348_f349_probes.py` 0 BREAK / 10 HELD)).

## F353: ceremony_leaf/anchor_binding raise uncoded KeyError on a keyless payload (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-290 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w290_redteam_probes.py` (probes `f353-ceremony-leaf`, `f353-anchor-binding`).

**Defect:** `ceremony_binding.ceremony_leaf` (public seam) validates the record's envelope shape -- `_require_record_shape` checks the format string and that `protected`/`payload` are dicts -- but not the payload's keys; `payload["content_digest"]` then raises a bare `KeyError` (`code=None`) on a shape-valid-but-keyless record. `anchor_binding` hits the same path (it calls `ceremony_leaf` first). F351/F342/F344 class: the repo's all-refusals-coded contract. `verify_binding` on the same record refuses coded (`challenge-nonce-mismatch`/`challenge-invalid-shape` first), so only the leaf/anchor path leaks.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed (no leaf minted, nothing anchored); contract/robustness only. Records arriving at this seam are verifier-side inputs, so the threat is log noise / crash surface in a verifier pipeline, not bypass.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) keyless payloads refuse LOUD with a coded `challenge-*` decision code from both `ceremony_leaf` and `anchor_binding`; (2) probes `f353-ceremony-leaf` and `f353-anchor-binding` flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (closed 2026-10-02, wave-291 lane 2). Closure mechanism: gov/ceremony_binding.py `_require_leaf_keys` extracts the (content_digest, challenge_nonce, challenge_purpose) tuple with .get(); absent or non-string keys refuse LOUD coded `challenge-invalid-shape` from both `ceremony_leaf` and `anchor_binding` (direct indexing removed). No new decision codes; taxonomy pin unchanged at 1710. Red-first: evals/w291_f353_f355_probes.py base 5 BREAK -> post-fix 0 BREAK / 13 HELD / 0 ERROR (staging and env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE); w290_redteam re-pinned 2 BREAK (f352, f354 genuinely OPEN); adjacent units 134/134 OK.

## F355: non-hex signature strings escape uncoded from verify_binding/verify_posture (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-290 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins: `evals/w290_redteam_probes.py` (probes `f355a-ceremony-sig`, `f355b-posture-sig`).

**Defect:** `ceremony_binding.verify_binding` and `runtime_posture.verify_posture` check only that `signature` is a non-empty `str` in the shape gate; `bytes.fromhex` then raises a bare `ValueError` (`code=None`) on a non-hex signature string. Fail-closed, but uncoded. F351/F342/F344 class: the repo's all-refusals-coded contract. Positive control: a forged but well-formed hex signature refuses coded (`challenge-signature-invalid` / `posture-signature-invalid`) on both paths, so forgery is covered -- only the malformed-signature path leaks.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed; contract/robustness only. Verify paths accept attacker-supplied records, so the uncoded path is reachable, but the outcome (refusal) is correct.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) non-hex signatures refuse coded (`challenge-signature-invalid` for ceremony, `posture-signature-invalid` for posture); (2) probes `f355a-ceremony-sig` and `f355b-posture-sig` flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (closed 2026-10-02, wave-291 lane 2). Closure mechanism: `verify_binding` (gov/ceremony_binding.py) and `verify_posture` (gov/runtime_posture.py) now gate the signature with `_is_hex(signature, 128)` before `bytes.fromhex`; non-hex and wrong-length hex signatures refuse LOUD coded `challenge-signature-invalid` / `posture-signature-invalid` (existing codes reused, no new codes). Forged-but-well-formed hex signatures still refuse coded; valid records still verify (positive controls HELD). Red-first: evals/w291_f353_f355_probes.py 0 BREAK / 13 HELD / 0 ERROR.

## F356: execute_rebuild skips the registration gate on direct calls (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-291 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w291_redteam_probes.py` (probes `rb-execute-unvalidated-keyerror`,
`rb-execute-unvalidated-unknown-op`).

**Defect:** `gov/evidence_provenance.py::execute_rebuild` is a public
(non-underscore) seam whose docstring claims execution "trusts nothing and
still bounds every operation", but unlike `verify_rebuild` /
`_rederive_and_compare` it never runs `check_rebuild_recipe`. Two facets:
(a) a malformed recipe (`{}`) escapes as a bare `KeyError` (`code=None`) —
F351/F344/F342 class, every public seam must refuse coded; (b) a step with an
unknown op (`{"op": "weaponize"}`) **silently passes the bytes through
unchanged** instead of refusing coded `provenance-rebuild-transform-unknown`.
All in-repo callers validate first, so reachability requires a caller that
skips validation — but the seam's own contract claims to bound every
operation.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Defense-in-depth; the silent pass-through is the
worse facet (data transformed without refusal) but only a non-validating
caller reaches it. No signature or digest bypass: `verify_rebuild` always
gates first.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `execute_rebuild` runs `check_rebuild_recipe`
itself (or maps every malformed-input path to a coded
`provenance-rebuild-*` refusal); (2) both probes flip to HELD; (3) adjacent
batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (closed 2026-10-02, wave-292 lane 1 —
`execute_rebuild` self-validates: `check_rebuild_recipe` runs at the seam's
top against the supplied materials, so malformed recipes refuse LOUD coded
`provenance-rebuild-invalid` and unknown ops refuse coded
`provenance-rebuild-transform-unknown`; no new codes. `evals/w292_f356_probes.py`
0 BREAK / 13 HELD / 0 ERROR (staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`);
`w291_redteam` 0 BREAK; `w290_rebuild` 0 BREAK; adjacent units
73/73 OK (test_evidence_provenance, test_rebuild_receipts,
test_finding_lifecycle). The only in-repo caller (`_rederive_and_compare`)
already validated, so the double validation is a no-op for it. Docstring
contract updated: the seam's claim to bound every operation is now true by
construction.)

## F360: verify_enveloped_ledger leaks uncoded parse exceptions on corrupt bundle files (LOW)

**Renumber note:** filed 2026-10-02 by the wave-292 independent red-team as F357; renumbered F360 at the wave-292 merge -- the wave-292 lane-6 sweep filed F357-F359 first (~18:39 UTC) and keeps them per the wave-272 earliest-filed rule (red-team filed at ~18:43 UTC).

**Cells:** wave-292 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w292_redteam_probes.py` (probes `ob-pubkey-hex-uncoded`,
`ob-manifest-enveloped-uncoded`, `ob-ledger-line-uncoded`,
`ob-manifest-json-uncoded`; positive control `ob-valid-bundle-verifies`).

**Defect:** `gov/offline_bundle.py::verify_enveloped_ledger` -- the public,
auditor-facing seam for verifying an offline evidence bundle (the "sell
evidence" path) -- lets four stdlib parse failures escape uncoded instead of
the module's own fail-closed `OfflineBundleError`: (a) a corrupt
`ENVELOPE_PUBKEY.hex` escapes raw `ValueError` from `bytes.fromhex`
(`code=None`); (b) a corrupt `manifest.enveloped.json` escapes raw
`json.JSONDecodeError` (`code=None`); (c) a corrupt `ledger.jsonl` line
escapes raw `json.JSONDecodeError` (`code=None`); (d) a corrupt
`manifest.json` (reached once a valid sealed manifest opens) escapes raw
`json.JSONDecodeError` (`code=None`). The module DOES wrap the analogous
parse on `ledger.enveloped.jsonl` lines (`except ValueError` ->
`OfflineBundleError`), so these four are inconsistent uncoded escapes --
F351/F344/F342/F354 class. All four verified red with non-vacuous probes
(each corrupt file is reached: earlier checks pass; a well-formed bundle
verifies `True` in the positive control).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed (no corrupt bundle verifies);
contract/robustness only. The seam is auditor-facing: a corrupt bundle
handed to an auditor's tooling produces a raw traceback instead of the
module's fail-closed error, complicating triage of exactly the evidence
artifacts the product sells.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) all four parse sites refuse via the module's
fail-closed `OfflineBundleError` (no raw `ValueError`/`JSONDecodeError`
escapes `verify_enveloped_ledger`); (2) all four probes flip to HELD;
(3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-292 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-02, wave-293 lane 1: all four parse sites in
`verify_enveloped_ledger` now refuse via the module's fail-closed
`OfflineBundleError` (`ENVELOPE_PUBKEY.hex` non-hex, `manifest.enveloped.json`
non-JSON, `ledger.jsonl` bad line, `manifest.json` non-JSON), using the
module's own `except ValueError -> OfflineBundleError` pattern; no new
decision codes; `evals/w293_f360_probes.py` 4 BREAK -> 0 BREAK / 10 HELD /
0 ERROR (staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`); `w292_redteam`
re-pin 4 BREAK -> 0 BREAK; `tests/test_offline_bundle.py` +
`tests/test_finding_lifecycle.py` 34/34 OK).

## F364: verify_provenance silently drops revocation demand for rids outside the gate's coverage (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-293 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w293_redteam_probes.py` (probe `rvc-provenance-demand-coverage-gap`).

**Defect:** `gov/evidence_provenance.py::verify_provenance` enforces the opt-in
revocation demand by calling `revocation_gate.require_all(revocation_statuses)`,
but the gate's `required_rids` are never bound to the policy's
`revocation_required`. A `RevocationGate` constructed with FEWER rids than the
policy demands silently passes: the demanded-but-uncovered rids are never
checked and verification returns `True`. Reproduced: policy
`revocation_required=("cred-001", "cred-002")`, gate `required_rids=("cred-001",)`,
status supplied for `cred-001` only -> `verify_provenance` returns `True`;
the demand for `cred-002` is silently dropped. The module's own contract says
"missing coverage refuses `revocation-status-unverifiable`" and "a demand
without a trust anchor is a misconfiguration, never a silent pass" -- a demand
with an under-covering gate IS a silent pass.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The demand and the gate are both caller-constructed
(opt-in); no attacker bypass without verifier misconfiguration. But the seam
advertises fail-closed coverage, and a stale gate config (fewer rids than the
policy demands) silently under-enforces a demand the operator declared --
fail-open of an opt-in demand. A retired/revoked rid still refuses coded when
the gate covers it.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `verify_provenance` refuses coded
`revocation-status-unverifiable` when `set(gate.required_rids)` does not cover
`set(policy.revocation_required)`; (2) probe
`rvc-provenance-demand-coverage-gap` flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay
green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-02, wave-294 lane 1). `verify_provenance`
now binds the gate's coverage to the policy demand: when
`set(gate.required_rids)` does not cover
`set(builder_policy.revocation_required)`, verification refuses coded
`revocation-status-unverifiable` (fail-closed; a stale gate is a
misconfiguration, never a silent pass). No new codes; taxonomy pin
stays 1730. Red-first battery `evals/w294_f364_probes.py`: base
1 BREAK / 7 HELD / 0 ERROR -> 0 BREAK / 8 HELD / 0 ERROR
(staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`); the w293 red-team probe
`rvc-provenance-demand-coverage-gap` flips HELD. Adjacent suites:
`tests.test_evidence_provenance`, `tests.test_provenance_policy`,
`tests.test_finding_lifecycle` 79/79 OK; depth-1 green checks
w293_redteam 0 BREAK, w292_revocation 0 BREAK.

**Renumber:** filed by the wave-293 independent red team as F361 (2026-10-02, ~19:57 UTC); the wave-293 sweep lane filed F361-F363 first (~19:53 UTC) and keeps them per the wave-272 earliest-filed rule, so this finding is renumbered to **F364**.

## F365: tool_rules secret-shape gate silently allows secrets beyond its scan bounds (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-294 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w294_redteam_probes.py` (probes `tr-depth5-secret-bypass`,
`tr-64kb-secret-bypass`).

**Defect:** `gov/tool_rules.py`'s secret-shape gate scans arg values with
two hard bounds -- `MAX_SECRET_DEPTH = 4` and a 64KB scan budget
(`MAX_SECRET_SCAN_BYTES`). When args exceed either bound the scan simply
stops and the call is ALLOWED: a secret nested at depth 5
(`{"a":{"b":{"c":{"d":{"e":"sk-..."}}}}}`) is never scanned
(`_scan_value` returns False at depth > 4 without inspecting the
string), and a secret placed past byte 65536 of a single large string
arg is never scanned (only `value[:budget]` is searched). Reproduced:
both calls return `{"allowed": True}` on the wave-293 base. The module's
own convention for scan bounds is to refuse beyond-bound input coded --
`_check_history_shape` refuses a session history longer than
`MAX_HISTORY_SCAN` with `toolcall-sequence-violated` instead of
silently evaluating a prefix. The secret gate does the opposite:
beyond-bound args are silently allowed, so the documented bound IS the
bypass for anyone who reads the open product code.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The gate is an opt-in, bounded heuristic by
design (shape-based detection; the lane-2 report documents the bounded
pattern set); defeating it grants no privilege -- it only defeats the
"secrets never as tool arguments" tripwire, and secrets in args are
already a misuse the typed-context direction is meant to replace. But
the inconsistency is real: one bound in the same module refuses
fail-closed, the other silently allows, and the module doc frames the
gate as fail-closed ("fail-closed on match") without naming the
silent-allow-beyond-bound behavior.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `check_call` refuses coded (existing
`toolcall-secret-in-args` or a new code) when the secret scan cannot
complete within its bounds -- depth beyond `MAX_SECRET_DEPTH` or budget
exhausted mid-scan -- i.e. unevaluatable args refuse fail-closed,
consistent with the `MAX_HISTORY_SCAN` convention; (2) probes
`tr-depth5-secret-bypass` and `tr-64kb-secret-bypass` flip to HELD;
(3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Documented residuals (probed, NOT filed):** base64-encoded PEM blocks
and secrets split across two arg values also evade the gate (confirmed
by probes `tr-base64-pem-residual`, `tr-split-secret-residual`). These
are inherent to the bounded pattern set -- there is no falsifiable
close-when for arbitrary encodings that does not demand the impossible
-- so they stay documented residuals per the lane-2 report.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-294 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-02, wave-295 lane 1). **Closure record (2026-10-02, wave-295 lane 1):**
- `_scan_value` is now tristate: True = secret found, False = fully
  scanned and clean, None = scan could not complete within the declared
  bounds (nesting deeper than `MAX_SECRET_DEPTH`, or bytes left to scan
  after the 64KB budget is exhausted). A None outcome is never treated
  as clean.
- `check_call` refuses fail-closed with the new code
  `toolcall-secret-scan-incomplete` when the scan is incomplete
  (documented choice: the refusal reason is genuinely different from a
  detected secret -- unevaluatable, not found -- so operators can
  distinguish a tripped tripwire from a missed scan). A detected secret
  still refuses `toolcall-secret-in-args`.
- New battery `evals/w295_f365_probes.py`: base 4 BREAK / 8 HELD
  (the two defect probes, a deep-clean-but-unevaluatable probe, and the
  1743 pin) -> fixed 0 BREAK / 12 HELD / 0 ERROR under staging and
  `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; depth-1 green checks
  `w293_tool_rules` and `w294_redteam` green (F365 probes flipped to
  HELD; only stale lane-local pin/repin BREAKs remain pending the merge
  repoint).
- Taxonomy 1742 -> 1743 (+1 `toolcall-secret-scan-incomplete`, at its
  true sorted position); raw literals 1743/1743/0 sorted.
- All three close-when criteria met. Adjacent batteries green.
- Residuals unchanged: base64-encoded PEM and split-across-values
  secrets still evade the bounded pattern set (inherent, documented,
  not falsifiable).

## F366: key_succession.advance(record=...) is not atomic -- a malformed advance record poisons the ceremony (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-294 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w294_redteam_probes.py` (probes `ks-advance-record-not-atomic`,
`ks-from-records-atomic`).

**Defect:** the operator path `KeySuccession.advance(record=envelope)`
validates the mandatory overlap window AFTER applying the phase
transition: it calls `_apply_record` (phase -> "completing", record
appended, digest marked seen) and only then `_check_window(window)`.
A well-signed advance record with a missing (or out-of-bounds) window
raises coded `keysuccession-window-missing` but leaves the ceremony at
phase "completing" with `_overlap_window = None`,
`overlap_window_seconds = None`, `_completing_at = None` -- a state
unreachable via the seed path (which checks the window BEFORE applying)
and unreachable via the auditor path `from_records` (which checks the
window before mutating and refuses the same chain cleanly). The two
verifier paths therefore disagree on the same record chain: the auditor
refuses it, the operator is left holding a poisoned ceremony whose
old-key material fails closed as retired-reuse even though no valid
ceremony ever completed. Reproduced on the wave-293 base: after the
refusal, `c.phase == "completing"` and `c._overlap_window is None`.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed direction (the old key becomes
unusable; the new key still verifies at "completing"); requires the
operator to feed a malformed record -- no attacker bypass without the
old key. But it breaks the ceremony's atomicity invariant and creates
operator/auditor path disagreement on identical input, which is exactly
the class of inconsistency an auditor replay is meant to exclude.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `advance(record=...)` validates
`overlap_window_seconds` via `_check_window` BEFORE `_apply_record`
(or rolls the ceremony back on validation failure), so a malformed
advance record leaves the ceremony at "prepared" with no mutation;
(2) probe `ks-advance-record-not-atomic` flips to HELD;
(3) the operator path and `from_records` agree on malformed chains
(probe `ks-from-records-atomic` stays HELD); (4) adjacent batteries
stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-294 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-02, wave-295 lane 2). **Closure record:** the record
path of `KeySuccession.advance` now extracts
`overlap_window_seconds` from the envelope and calls `_check_window`
BEFORE `_apply_record`, so a malformed advance record refuses coded
`keysuccession-window-missing` without mutating the ceremony (phase
stays "prepared", no window stashed, no `advance_record`, no digest
marked seen). New red-first battery `evals/w295_f366_probes.py`: 8
probes -- missing window coded / no poisoning (missing +
out-of-bounds) / no state leaked / path agreement with `from_records`
/ seed path still refuses clean / valid record still advances /
ceremony reusable after a failed advance. On the pristine base, the
battery showed the poisoning (phase "completing" with
`_overlap_window = None`, and the ceremony then unrecoverably refused
a later valid advance as phase-skipped); the fixed tree is 0 BREAK.
`w294_redteam` flips from 3 BREAK to 2 BREAK (F365's two secret-scan
probes still OPEN), `w293_key_succession` 0 BREAK. No new decision
codes; taxonomy pin unchanged at 1742 (raw literals verified).
Commit made locally with trailer; lane 2 reports and stops.


## F367: coordination_lease.acquire with a future-dated issued_at bypasses coord-lease-denied and evicts a live lease (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-295 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w295_redteam_probes.py` (probe `lease-future-issued-preempts`).

**Defect:** `LeaseManager.acquire` evaluates the "an unexpired lease already
covers the scope" check at the caller-supplied `issued_at`
(`live = self._live(scope, issued_at)`) instead of at grant time. An
`acquire` with a future-dated `issued_at` (past the current lease's
`not_after`) passes the check, is granted, and OVERWRITES the manager's
single per-scope slot -- evicting the currently-live, non-overlapping
lease. The preempted holder's subsequent `check_write` then refuses
(reproduced: `coord-lease-fencing`, token generation advanced under them).
The docstring promises "coded `coord-lease-denied` when an unexpired lease
already covers the scope"; at grant time the old lease does cover the
scope, so the bypass contradicts the documented contract. The window is
narrow (it requires the issuing authority seed -- the documented
compromised-host class -- or a badly skewed authority clock), and the
direction is denial of the legitimate holder rather than a privilege
grant, hence LOW.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires the authority seed (or authority
clock skew); the seed holder can already mint arbitrary leases. But the
eviction is silent -- no `coord-lease-denied`, no release -- and it breaks
the standing "authority is leased, never held" invariant for the current
holder, whose valid grant dies without any ceremony.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `acquire` refuses coded `coord-lease-denied`
when a lease is live at grant time regardless of the new lease's claimed
`issued_at` (or the manager queues non-overlapping future grants instead
of evicting the live record); (2) probe `lease-future-issued-preempts`
flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-295 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-02, wave-296 lane 1).

**Closure record (2026-10-02, wave-296 lane 1):** implemented the
close-when's queueing option -- the manager no longer keeps a single
per-scope slot. `LeaseManager._leases` now maps scope -> list of
granted, non-overlapping lease records; every grant is retained and a
later grant can never evict an earlier one. `acquire` refuses coded
`coord-lease-denied` when the new grant's `[issued_at, not_after)`
overlaps any stored grant (no new decision codes; pin stays 1750);
non-overlapping future-dated grants QUEUE alongside the live record.
Lookups (`_live` / `_require_live` / `check_write`) resolve the single
lease covering the queried instant (`issued_at <= checked_at <
not_after`); `renew` refuses coded `coord-lease-denied` when the
extension would steal a queued future grant's interval; `release`
surrenders one interval by fencing token, leaving queued grants
untouched. Reuse choice: `coord-lease-denied` for overlap (a grant
that would collide with an existing grant is denied, matching the
pre-existing denial semantics); `coord-lease-invalid` was not needed.
Battery `evals/w296_f367_probes.py`: 0 BREAK / 12 HELD / 0 ERROR in
staging and under `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (depth-1 green checks:
`w295_redteam` 3 BREAK expected-open F368/F369/F370 / 0 ERROR --
`lease-future-issued-preempts` now HELD via the coexistence branch;
`w294_coord_lease` 0 BREAK / 0 ERROR). Residuals: the grant list is
unbounded per scope (a compromised seed could spam acquires; the
seed holder is already the compromised-host class -- documented,
not fixed); synthetic-clock callers that relied on
`_live(scope, t)` returning a future-issued lease for `t <
issued_at` now get no-covering-lease (coded `coord-lease-expired`,
same code as before).

## F368: invocation_pipeline invoke-time drift digest covers filter names only -- same-name replacement bypasses toolcall-filter-frozen (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-295 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w295_redteam_probes.py` (probes `pipeline-drift-samename`,
`pipeline-drift-othername`).

**Defect:** `FilterStack.invoke` re-verifies `_stack_digest`, which digests
`[_filter_name(fn) for fn in filters]` -- function `__name__` strings only.
A wholesale in-process replacement of `_filters` with same-named functions
keeps the digest byte-identical, so the drift check passes and the
replacement filters execute inside the "unavoidable" pipeline (reproduced:
a same-named evil filter ran and rewrote the result). No SHA-256 preimage
is needed -- the digest is name-based, not code-based. The class docstring
claims "even a freeze-bypassing wholesale replacement of `_filters` is
caught as `toolcall-filter-frozen`"; that claim is falsified by the
same-name swap (a different-named replacement IS caught, probe
`pipeline-drift-othername` HELD).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires in-process access, and the module's
honest boundary already says filters are trusted in-process code -- but the
drift check exists precisely to catch in-process replacement (the
CompiledToolPolicy pattern), and its documented guarantee does not hold.
The practical effect is limited to weakening a defense-in-depth tripwire,
not granting a new privilege.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) the invoke-time drift digest covers filter
code identity (e.g. a stable fingerprint of each filter's code object),
so a wholesale `_filters` replacement with same-named functions refuses
coded `toolcall-filter-frozen`, while the unchanged stack's digest stays
stable across invocations; (2) probe `pipeline-drift-samename` flips to
HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-295 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-02, wave-296 lane 2). **Closure record:** the drift digest
now binds each filter's name + code object (marshal-dumped SHA-256) +
callable identity (`gov/invocation_pipeline.py::_filter_fingerprint`);
a same-named different-code replacement AND a same-code closure-instance
replacement both refuse coded `toolcall-filter-frozen` (code reused --
the defect is a freeze-bypass, and that code is the freeze contract; no
new codes minted, taxonomy pin 1750 unchanged). Red-first battery
`evals/w296_f368_probes.py`: base 1 BREAK / 6 HELD attack probes (both
sub-cases bypassed) -> 0 BREAK / 7 HELD / 0 ERROR fixed, identical under
`env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; depth-1 green checks `w295_redteam`
(`pipeline-drift-samename` HELD, F367/F369/F370 probes still BREAK
expected-open) and `w294_filter_pipeline` (0 BREAK) green; unit tests
`test_invocation_pipeline` + `test_finding_lifecycle` 58/58 OK.

## F369: invocation_pipeline.audit_log() returns shallow copies aliasing the stored records (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-295 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w295_redteam_probes.py` (probe `pipeline-audit-aliasing`).

**Defect:** `FilterStack.audit_log` promises "copies of the signed per-call
records" but returns `[dict(entry) for entry in log]` -- a shallow copy.
The nested `record` dict is shared with the stored entry: mutating the
returned `record` (e.g. flipping `outcome`) rewrites what subsequent
`audit_log()` calls return (reproduced). Any signature verification over
the tampered record would fail (detectable), and reaching the seam already
requires in-process access, so this is an API-hygiene defect, not a
forgery primitive -- but the documented "copies" promise is false.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. In-process only; tampering is detectable via
the record signature. The defect is the violated copy contract on an
accountability seam.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `audit_log()` returns deep copies -- mutating
the returned record (including nested dicts) does not affect subsequent
`audit_log()` results; (2) probe `pipeline-audit-aliasing` flips to HELD;
(3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-295 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-02, wave-296 lane 3). **Closure record:**
`FilterStack.audit_log` now returns `[copy.deepcopy(entry) for entry in
self._audit_fn.log]`, so the nested `record` dict is an independent
copy: mutating the returned record (scalars and nested lists) leaves
the stored log byte-identical, while the canonical-signature contract
is unchanged (tampering a returned record still fails signature
verification, verified with `ed25519.verify` `is True` / `is False`
checks). New red-first battery `evals/w296_f369_probes.py`: on the
pristine wave-295 base, 1 BREAK (`audit-aliasing-record` reproduces:
mutating the returned `record["outcome"]` rewrote the stored log) /
8 HELD / 0 ERROR; the fixed tree is 0 BREAK / 9 HELD / 0 ERROR under
both staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`. Depth-1 green checks:
`w295_redteam` probe `pipeline-audit-aliasing` flips to HELD (3 BREAK
remain: F367, F368, F370 still OPEN), `w294_filter_pipeline` 0 BREAK /
30 HELD. Adjacent unit tests green. No new decision codes (correctness
fix, no refusal path); taxonomy pin unchanged at 1750 (raw literals
1750/1750/0/sorted).

## F370: tool_schemas call-time validation never name-checks dict keys nested in arg values -- credential-named keys pass both gates (LOW)

**Cells:** wave-295 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w295_redteam_probes.py` (probes `schema-nested-credkey-1`,
`schema-nested-credkey-2`).

**Defect:** the credential-field gate runs at COMPILE time on declared
field names only; the call-time gate checks string VALUES against
secret SHAPES only. Dict keys nested inside arg values are never
name-checked: `{"config": {"password": "hunter2"}}` and the two-level
`{"config": {"db": {"secret": "hunter2"}}}` both validate clean (the
values are not secret-shaped, the keys are never inspected), so a
credential travels as a tool argument past both gates. Top-level args are
safe (undeclared args refuse), but any declared dict field is an
uninspected smuggling channel. This is the seam the wave-295 brief
explicitly named ("nested 'secret' two levels deep").

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The value still has to be a non-shape
plaintext credential (shape-based values are already refused); defeating
the gate grants no privilege, only passage for the "credentials never as
tool arguments" tripwire. But the design rule is explicit -- credentials
travel in typed execution context, never in the call schema -- and the
dict-value channel is entirely uninspected.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) call-time dict validation refuses coded
(`toolcall-secret-in-args` or a new code) when any nested dict key
normalizes to a credential token under the module's existing
normalization; (2) probes `schema-nested-credkey-1` and
`schema-nested-credkey-2` flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Documented residuals (probed, NOT filed):** leetspeak field names
(`passw0rd` compiles -- the token list is documented as bounded; closing
it is an unbounded arms race, same class as F365's base64-PEM residual);
secret-shaped author-declared DEFAULTS are injected without the call-time
secret check (`for_default=True` skips it) -- the schema author is
trusted, so this is author misuse, not an attacker primitive.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-295 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-02, wave-296 lane 4). **Closure record (2026-10-02, wave-296 lane 4):**
- `_validate_value`'s dict branch now name-checks every dict key nested in
  arg values against the module's existing credential-name gate
  (`_is_credential_name`, the same bounded token list as the compile-time
  gate) at call time; a match refuses coded
  `toolcall-schema-secret-field`. No new code was minted: the nested key
  is a field name, so the compile-time code's mechanism applies;
  `toolcall-secret-scan-incomplete` does not apply because the check rides
  the complete structural-validation walk (bounded by the compiled
  schema's `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH`), so an incomplete-scan outcome cannot
  occur.
- Author-declared defaults skip the key check (`for_default`), mirroring
  the secret-value gate's author-trust boundary; nested keys inside
  defaults still refuse fail-closed at compile.
- Post-fix battery `evals/w296_f370_probes.py`: red-first 5 BREAK on the
  pristine base (the two close-when probes plus deep-4, list-of-dicts,
  and key-before-value-shape coverage) -> **0 BREAK / 14 HELD / 0 ERROR**
  on the fixed tree (staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`); the
  w295 red-team's F370 probes flip HELD (3 BREAK remain: F367/F368/F369,
  open this wave); w294_tool_schemas and w293_tool_rules re-pin 0 BREAK;
  taxonomy pin 1750 unchanged.

## F371: verify_trace crashes uncoded on validly-signed malformed traces -- post-signature shape assumptions (LOW, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-297 independent red-team, 2026-10-02. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w297_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F371-signed-missing-verdict`,
`F371-signed-final-not-dict`, `F371-signed-edges-not-list`,
`F371-signed-edge-missing-seq`).

**Defect:** `gov/decision_trace.py::verify_trace` shape-checks the envelope
PRE-signature (missing body, missing signature, missing required fields,
unknown format/replay rule, non-hex pubkey/signature all refuse coded
`decision-trace-invalid`), but POST-signature it dereferences body fields
it never validates: a validly-signed trace whose `final_decision` lacks
`"verdict"` raises a bare `KeyError` (code=None); a validly-signed trace
whose `final_decision` is not a dict raises a bare `TypeError`; a
validly-signed trace whose `edges` is not a list raises a bare
`TypeError`; a validly-signed edge dict missing `"seq"` raises a bare
`KeyError` in `fold_edges`. `emit()` can never produce these shapes (it
validates via `_check_edges` and always builds `{"verdict", "code"}`), so
the reachable authors are a compromised trace-signing key or a buggy
alternate implementation of the trace contract -- but the F351 contract
is that EVERY public-seam refusal carries a coded decision code, and the
verifier is the auditor's own tool. Same defect class as F361-F363
(fail-closed uncoded escapes, LOW).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. All four escapes are fail-closed (no malformed
trace verifies); the blast radius is a raw traceback from the verifier
seam rather than a coded refusal. Exploitation requires a valid signature,
so the signer (the trust anchor) is already compromised or non-conforming
-- this is defense-in-depth on the auditor's seam, not an attacker
primitive.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `verify_trace` refuses coded
`decision-trace-invalid` for every malformed-but-signed shape it
dereferences: `final_decision` not a dict / missing `"verdict"`, `edges`
not a list / an edge not a dict / an edge missing `"seq"` (reusing
`_check_edges` post-signature is the natural fix); (2) the four F371
probes flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-02, wave-297 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-298 lane 1). **Closure record (2026-10-03,
wave-298 lane 1):**
- `gov/decision_trace.py::verify_trace` now validates every
  post-signature dereferenced shape before touching it: `final_decision`
  must be a dict containing `"verdict"`, and `_check_edges` (the same
  validator `emit()` uses -- no second validation language) runs on
  `body["edges"]` after the signature check; every malformed shape
  refuses coded `decision-trace-invalid`. No new code minted. The
  signature check still uses `is True`/`is False` (wave-243).
- Red-first: pristine base `evals/w297_redteam_probes.py` showed
  **4 BREAK / 43 HELD / 0 ERROR** (the four F371 probes: bare
  `KeyError`/`TypeError` escapes) -> **0 BREAK / 47 HELD / 0 ERROR**
  on the fixed tree, identical under staging and
  `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; the four F371 probes
  (`F371-signed-missing-verdict`, `F371-signed-final-not-dict`,
  `F371-signed-edges-not-list`, `F371-signed-edge-missing-seq`) flip
  HELD. Six new regression probes added to the battery (edge missing
  outcome, duplicate seq, final_decision None, non-standard verdict
  divergence -> replay-mismatch, empty-edges ALLOW claim -> replay-mismatch,
  well-formed trace still verifies): battery final
  **0 BREAK / 53 HELD / 0 ERROR** both modes.
- New unit tests `tests/test_decision_trace_f371.py`: **13/13 OK**
  (the four F371 shapes + three more malformed shapes refuse coded
  `decision-trace-invalid`; divergence cases refuse coded
  `decision-trace-replay-mismatch`; pre-signature malformed and forged
  traces unchanged; `is True`/`is False` contract pinned).
- Adjacent green: `w296_decision_trace` 0/22/0, `w297_supervision`
  0/34/0, `w294_filter_pipeline` 0/30/0; adjacent unit suites

## F372: policy_ci.load_artifact accepts artifacts with extra files added -- the derived file set is not closed (LOW, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-298 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w298_redteam_probes.py` (probe `F372-artifact-extra-file`).

**Defect:** `gov/policy_ci.py::load_artifact` verifies that every file in
`derived` matches its entry in `digests`, but it never checks that the file
set is CLOSED: an artifact copied from `derive()` output with an added file
(e.g. `derived["evil.yaml"] = "..."` plus a matching `digests["evil.yaml"]`
entry) passes verification. The embedded manifest (`policy.manifest.json`)
lists the files `derive()` emitted, but `load_artifact` never compares the
manifest's `files` map against the artifact's actual `derived` keys -- the
manifest is inert (no consumer in `gov/` reads its `files` map;
`compile_authoring` verifies the artifact but compiles from the source text,
never from derived files). The lane-297 report's claim -- "Derived artifacts
... hand-edited files refuse coded `policy-ci-derived-tampered`" -- is true
for edits to existing files but not for additions to the set: the artifact
is not the frozen closed set `derive()` emitted.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Currently no consumer reads the extra files, so
there is no exploit path in this tree -- this is a claim-vs-implementation
gap on the evidence seam (same defense-in-depth class as F371). It becomes
a real primitive the moment any consumer enumerates `artifact["derived"]`
or trusts the manifest's file list: a tampered artifact store could smuggle
a file past verification.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `load_artifact` refuses coded
`policy-ci-derived-tampered` when the derived file set differs from the
closed set `derive()` emits (or when the manifest's `files` map disagrees
with the artifact's `derived` keys); (2) the F372 probe flips to HELD;
(3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-298 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-299 lane 1). **Closure record (2026-10-03,
wave-299 lane 1):**
- `gov/policy_ci.py::load_artifact` now enforces the closed derived
  file set: after the per-file digest checks it parses the embedded
  `policy.manifest.json`, requires its `format` to be
  `sasanam-policy-manifest/v1` and its `source_digest` to match the
  artifact's, requires `set(derived.keys()) == set(manifest["files"]) |
  {"policy.manifest.json"}` (the manifest lists every file except
  itself, by `derive()`'s construction), and requires each manifest
  digest to agree with the artifact's `digests` map. Any deviation
  refuses coded `policy-ci-derived-tampered` -- no new codes minted.
- Red-first: pristine wave-298 base `evals/w298_redteam_probes.py`
  **3 BREAK / 19 HELD / 0 ERROR** (`F372-artifact-extra-file` BREAK);
  fixed tree **0 BREAK / 22 HELD / 0 ERROR** under staging and
  `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`.
- New unit tests in `tests/test_policy_ci.py::LoadTests`
  (`test_f372_extra_file_refused`,
  `test_f372_removed_file_refused`,
  `test_f372_manifest_files_disagree_refused`,
  `test_f372_closed_set_happy`): all OK; full
  `tests.test_policy_ci` + `tests.test_approval_quorum` **57/57 OK**.
- Adjacent batteries green: `w297_policy_ci` 0/20/0,
  `w297_approval_quorum` 0/22/0, `w298_redteam` 0/22/0.
- Taxonomy pin 1780 unchanged (1780/1780/0 sorted, no new codes);
  `git diff` == `git diff -w`.

## F373: QuorumPredicate slot attributes are reassignable post-construction -- the "immutable after construction" claim is overstated (LOW, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-298 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w298_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F373-predicate-min-mutable`,
`F373-predicate-veto-mutable`).

**Defect:** `gov/approval_quorum.py::QuorumPredicate` documents "Immutable
after construction" and the wave-297 lane-2 code comments claim "the object
itself is slot-locked (no `__dict__`)" so "a post-build in-process mutation
cannot silently change decisions under a still-valid digest". `__slots__`
prevents NEW attributes but does not prevent reassignment of the declared
slots: `p._min_approvals = 1` and `p._blocking_veto_roles = frozenset()`
both succeed silently, and `tally` reads `predicate.min_approvals` /
`predicate.blocking_veto_roles` live, so a mutated predicate decides under
weakened rules while the deployment believes the declared predicate holds.
The lane's own freeze test (`test_veto_roles_frozen`) only proves the
frozenset itself rejects `.add` -- it never probes slot reassignment.
The F330/F340 precedent (`ChildSpec.__setattr__` refusing coded
`supervision-invalid`) shows the intended pattern; it was not applied here.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Exploitation (or accidental weakening by buggy
deployment code) requires in-process write access -- the compromised-host
class -- and `tally_digest` binds `predicate.digest()`, so the weakened
predicate is forensically visible. But the module explicitly claims
immutability as a security property, and the fix is the one-line
`__setattr__` guard the tree already uses elsewhere.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `QuorumPredicate` refuses coded
`approval-quorum-invalid` on any post-construction attribute assignment
(F330/F340 pattern); (2) the two F373 probes flip to HELD; (3) adjacent
batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-298 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-299 lane 1). **Closure record (2026-10-03,
wave-299 lane 1):**
- `gov/approval_quorum.py::QuorumPredicate` now defines
  `__setattr__` refusing coded `approval-quorum-invalid` on any
  post-construction attribute assignment (the F330/F340
  `supervision.ChildSpec` pattern); `__init__` writes via
