## F374: memory_store retraction authority migrates to the newest writer -- a conflicting writer can permanently tombstone another principal's key (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-299 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w299_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F374-hostile-tombstone`,
`F374-victim-loses-retract`).

**Defect:** `gov/memory_store.py::retract_fact` authorizes the retractor
against the NEWEST record's source key (`authorized =
{newest["source_pubkey"]}` plus archivists), not the claim's original
source key. The documented contract says "The retractor must be the
claim's source key or a named archivist." Attack chain, verified
empirically: (1) the victim records a fact on key K with their own key;
(2) the attacker -- holding only legitimate write access under their own
key -- records a CONFLICTING fact on K (the graphiti supersession rule
closes the victim's record, by design); the attacker is now the newest
writer; (3) the attacker retracts K, which succeeds because the newest
record's source key is the attacker's. The tombstone closes every record
under K and is keyed by statement_key forever: the victim re-records a
fresh fact, but `recall` still refuses `memory-store-tombstoned` -- the
key is permanently dead for recall. Two facets: (a) a conflicting writer
gains destructive, irreversible authority over another principal's key
history; (b) the ORIGINAL author loses retraction authority over their
own superseded claim the moment someone else writes a conflicting fact
(their own retract then refuses `memory-store-unsigned-retraction`).

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. No key compromise is needed -- any
authorized writer can permanently deny recall of another principal's
key, which exceeds what supersession alone permits (a superseded victim
could otherwise re-assert). The tombstone is irreversible by design
("no un-retract"), so the damage is permanent. History remains
queryable via `history()`, bounding the harm to recall denial.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `retract_fact` authorizes against the
claim's ORIGINAL source key (first record under the key) or a named
archivist -- not the newest writer; or, alternatively, retraction
closes only records authored by the retractor's own key (per-record
tombstones); (2) the F374 probes flip to HELD (hostile retract refuses
coded; the victim retains retract authority over their own claim);
(3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-03, wave-300 lane 1). Closure evidence:
`gov/memory_store.py::retract_fact` now authorizes against the first
record's `source_pubkey` under the statement key (authorship fixed at
first write; superseding writers never inherit it) or a named
archivist; docstring and inline comment updated. Red-first: pristine
base `evals/w299_redteam_probes.py` 3 BREAK (incl.
`F374-hostile-tombstone`) -> fixed tree hostile retract refuses coded
`memory-store-unsigned-retraction`, victim's own retract after
supersession succeeds, archivist override intact, double-retract still
refuses `memory-store-tombstoned`; new probes
`F374-hostile-retract-refused` + `F374-regression-pins` HELD; new unit
tests `F374RetractionAuthorityTests` (3 tests) green; existing 24
`test_memory_store` tests green (single-writer behavior unchanged).

## F375: memory_reconcile write-rate bound is keyed on a self-reported principal string and is evaded by rotation (LOW, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-299 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w299_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F375-rate-bound-evasion`,
`F375-rate-bound-control`).

**Defect:** `gov/memory_reconcile.py::_check_write_rate` bounds writes
per `candidate["provenance"]["source_principal"]` -- a free-form string
inside the owner-signed candidate. The namespace owner, who signs every
candidate, rotates the string per write (`principal-0`, `principal-1`,
...) and the bound never fires: 6/6 writes accepted with
`max_writes_per_principal=2` (verified empirically; the control -- same
string 3 times -- correctly refuses the 3rd with
`memory-reconcile-invalid`). The wave-298 lane-3 report explicitly
claims "Defenses bound even the owner (rate, evidence, snapshots)"; the
rate defense does not bind the owner, because the identity it keys on
is self-reported by the bound party. The per-principal bound only
constrains honest principals who keep a stable name.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The namespace owner is already the trust
anchor for their own namespace (a compromised owner key is the
compromised-host class), so the incremental blast radius is a flood the
owner could partly achieve anyway -- but the flood is exactly what the
bound exists to stop, and the lane claimed it binds the owner. This is a
claim-vs-mechanism gap on a poisoning defense (qdrant checklist item).

**Close-when criteria:** (1) the rate bound is keyed on an
authenticated identity -- the namespace owner's key (per-owner bound)
in addition to, or instead of, the self-reported principal string;
(2) the F375 evasion probe flips to HELD (rotated-principal flood
refuses); (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-03, wave-300 lane 2). Red-first: the
`F375-rate-bound-evasion` probe reproduced on the pristine base (6/6
rotated-principal writes accepted, bound=2). Fix:
`gov/memory_reconcile.py::reconcile` now keys the write-rate bound on
the authenticated namespace-owner key (`"owner:" + owner_pubkey`,
whose signature was just verified) IN ADDITION TO the self-reported
provenance string (`"principal:" + source_principal`); both keys must
pass. String rotation no longer evades (3rd rotated write refuses
`memory-reconcile-invalid`); distinct owners keep independent budgets
(pinned by `test_f375_distinct_owners_keep_independent_budgets`);
existing same-principal behavior unchanged
(`test_rate_bound`, `mr-rate-bound` probe). Post-fix:
`evals/w299_redteam_probes.py` 1 BREAK (F374 expected-open) / 36 HELD /
0 ERROR; `evals/w298_memory_reconcile_probes.py` 0/30/0; adjacent
`w298_memory_store`, `w298_supervision_lease`, `w297_supervision`
green; `tests.test_memory_reconcile` 24/24. Close-when (1)(2)(3) all
met. Residual: the bound is per (owner key, principal string) pair;
two colluding owners still get independent budgets each (bounded,
fail-closed per budget).

## F376: memory_reconcile cross-namespace recall authorization rests on a self-asserted caller_namespace -- the grant check is bypassable (LOW, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-299 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w299_redteam_probes.py` (probe `F376-caller-assertion-bypass`).

**Defect:** `gov/memory_reconcile.py::recall(scope, caller_namespace,
at)` enforces cross-namespace sharing grants via
`self._grant_live(ns, caller_namespace, at)` -- but `caller_namespace`
is a bare caller-supplied string, validated only by `_check_id`
(shape). Nothing binds the caller to the asserted namespace: any caller
that knows a grant exists (e.g. alice -> bob) asserts
`caller_namespace="bob"` and reads alice's facts, with no key material
and no grant presentation (verified empirically: an unauthenticated
caller asserting "bob" read alice's fact covered by a live alice -> bob
grant, while a non-grantee name correctly refused). The documented
contract -- "Cross-namespace recall requires a live sharing grant or
refuses" -- is therefore enforced only against honest callers; the
grant mechanism's access-control purpose is vacuous against a caller
who lies about their name. The lane-3 report's honest residuals do not
list caller authentication as deployment-owned, and the battery pins
only the honest case.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Same claim-vs-mechanism class as F373: the
security property reads as module-enforced access control, but the
authorization decision rests on an unauthenticated input. Exploitation
requires being an API caller (the deployment mediates who calls), and a
fully in-process attacker could reach internals anyway -- but the
reference-monitor-between-agents threat model is exactly what the grant
system is for, and it does not deliver it.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) EITHER the caller presents the signed
sharing grant and the module verifies it against the owner's declared
key before serving cross-namespace reads (bearer-grant model), OR the
module contract explicitly documents that `caller_namespace` must be a
deployment-authenticated identity (docstring + module docs, battery
pins the precondition); (2) the F376 probe flips to HELD under the
documented contract; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-03, wave-300 lane 2). Chose close-when
option (a): bearer-grant model. Red-first: the
`F376-caller-assertion-bypass` probe reproduced on the pristine base
(unauthenticated caller asserting "bob" read alice's fact). Fix:
`gov/memory_reconcile.py::recall(scope, caller_namespace, at,
grant=None)` now requires cross-namespace callers to PRESENT the
signed sharing grant; `_verify_presented_grant` verifies it against
the owner namespace's DECLARED owner key (never caller-supplied key
material), its window, and the live grant inventory (revocation
honored, presented signature must match the inventory record). A bare
namespace string never authorizes cross-namespace reads (refuses
`memory-reconcile-unauthorized-namespace`). Same-namespace reads keep
the documented precondition that `caller_namespace` is the
deployment-authenticated caller identity (docstring states it
loudly; no cryptographic artifact exists for the owner reading their
own namespace). Post-fix: the F376 probe flips HELD; new regression
pins (`test_f376_grant_must_be_presented`,
`test_f376_presented_grant_verifies`,
`test_f376_wrong_grantee_name_refused`, `mr-grant-absent`,
`mr-grant-forged`); forged/wrong-grantee/expired/revoked grants all
refuse coded; adjacent batteries green. Close-when (1)(2)(3) all met.
Residual: same-namespace caller identity remains deployment-owned;
a deployment that lies about the caller defeats the check
(documented, not a module defect).
## F377: embedded DID documents override the verifier's pinned trust roots in offline chain verification (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-300 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w300_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F377-native-override`,
`F377-local-override`, `F377-tampered-embedded`, `F377-honest-flow`).

**Defect:** In `gov/delegation_identity.py`, both
`verify_native_chain_offline` and `verify_chain_offline` build the
verifier's DID trust roots by first copying the caller's
`trusted_did_docs` and then, for every DID document embedded in the
chain document, executing `roots[did] = doc` -- silently REPLACING the
verifier's own pinned root for the same DID. The embedded document is
only "re-verified" via `verify_did_document`, which checks the
document's controller self-signature -- always valid for an
attacker-controlled DID. Attack chain, verified empirically on BOTH
paths: (1) Mallory holds a link in a chain rooted at a trust root
Victor accepts; (2) Mallory self-issues a DID document for
`did:example:alice` naming HER key in `delegation_keys`, self-signs it
as controller (a valid signature), and attaches it as the embedded DID
document with a matching `did`-method identity-evidence block;
(3) Mallory exports the chain herself (`export_native_chain` verifies
the evidence -- it is internally consistent); (4) Victor verifies
offline while passing his PINNED real Alice document in
`trusted_did_docs` -- verification SUCCEEDS, and Victor's verifier now
treats Mallory's key as bound to Alice's DID. The pinned trust root
was replaced, not honored. (A tampered embedded doc -- broken
controller signature -- is still refused, `delegation-identity-invalid`;
the flaw is substitution of a valid self-signed doc, not acceptance of
invalid ones.)

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. The attacker must already hold a link
in a chain the victim will verify (the "evidence IS the chain"
handoff), and native delegation rights are still enforced -- this
corrupts identity attribution (which key is bound to whose DID), not
authorization scope. But it defeats the explicit purpose of
`trusted_did_docs` pinning: a verifier who pins roots gets no
protection against a chain document that carries its own replacement
roots.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) embedded DID documents never replace
verifier-supplied roots: when a DID is already present in the caller's
`trusted_did_docs`, either refuse coded `delegation-identity-invalid`
on digest mismatch or ignore the embedded document and use the pinned
one -- in BOTH `verify_chain_offline` and
`verify_native_chain_offline`; (2) the F377 override probes flip to
HELD on both paths while the tampered-embedded and honest-flow probes
stay HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-300 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-03, wave-301 lane 1).

**Closure record (2026-10-03, wave-301 lane 1):** fixed in `gov/delegation_identity.py` only. Both `verify_chain_offline` and `verify_native_chain_offline` no longer execute `roots[did] = doc` unconditionally: when a DID is already present in the caller's `trusted_did_docs`, the embedded document is accepted only when its canonical unsigned-body digest matches the pinned document's digest (`did_document_digest`); any conflicting embedded document refuses coded `delegation-identity-invalid` (the close-when's refuse-on-digest-mismatch option). A byte-identical embedded copy stays authoritative via the pinned root. Embedded documents for DIDs the verifier never pinned are still admitted as that DID's root for the verification (documented residual; pinning stays the trust decision).
Red-first evidence: `evals/w300_redteam_probes.py` F377 probes BREAK on the pristine base (2 BREAK / 27 HELD on the lane tree before the fix) and flip HELD after it (0 F377 BREAKs; the only remaining BREAKs are the expected-open F378 probes, wave-301 lane 2's work); tampered-embedded and honest-flow probes stay HELD under staging and `env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`. New unit tests `TestF377PinnedTrustRoots` (4 tests) in `tests/test_delegation_identity.py`: conflicting embedded docs refuse coded on both paths, byte-identical embedded copy verifies, unpinned embedded doc admitted (residual pinned). Adjacent green: `tests/test_delegation_identity.py` 18/18, `evals/w299_delegation_probes.py` 28/28, full `evals/w300_redteam_probes.py` 27 HELD / 0 ERROR (2 expected-open F378 BREAKs). No new decision codes; taxonomy pin unchanged at 1802.
## F378: ticket presentation never consults revocation -- a ticket anchored on a revoked receipt still presents (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-300 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w300_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F378-present-after-revoke`,
`F378-issue-on-revoked`, `F378-native-revoke-enforced`).

**Defect:** `gov/delegation_tickets.py::present()` takes no revocation
input at all -- no revocation-list parameter, no revoker -- and no
function in the ticket module references revocation (the revocation
story stops at the receipt layer). Two facets, both verified
empirically on native receipt chains: (a) PRESENTATION: a ticket
issued on a receipt via `issue_ticket_on_receipt` presents
successfully via `present(..., receipt_chain=..., trust_roots=...)`
AFTER the anchoring receipt is revoked with
`DelegationRevoker.revoke`; (b) ISSUANCE: `issue_ticket_on_receipt`
succeeds on an already-revoked receipt (the issue path verifies the
chain via `gov/delegation.verify_chain` but never revocation). The
control holds: `DelegationRevoker.assert_live_native` correctly
refuses `delegation-revoked` for revoked chains -- the ticket
presentation path simply never calls it. A revoked delegation's
presentation token survives revocation indefinitely.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Revocation is the delegation stack's
kill switch, and the revocation lane claims power-of-attorney
semantics (revocation binds ALL downstream copies). A presentation
token that outlives the revocation of its anchoring authority record
silently defeats that claim. The ticket remains attenuated (scope and
rights are still enforced), so the blast radius is bounded to the
ticket's original scope -- but that scope was revoked, and
presentation still grants it.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `present()` accepts an optional
revocation input (revocation list or revoker) and refuses coded
`delegation-revoked` when the anchoring receipt -- or any receipt in
the presented chain -- is revoked; `issue_ticket_on_receipt` likewise
refuses issuance on a revoked anchoring receipt; (2) the F378 probes
flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-300 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-03 wave-301 lane 2: `gov/delegation_tickets.py` `present()` and `issue_ticket_on_receipt()` now accept `revocation={'revoker': DelegationRevoker}` and enforce revocation liveness fail-closed whenever a receipt chain is consulted (wave-300 lane-4 `coordination_lease` precedent) -- no revocation state refuses coded `delegation-ticket-invalid`; the presented revoker must be the anchoring receipt's own delegator's revoker (delegator_id + key match, anti-substitution); a revoked anchor or revoked ancestor refuses coded `delegation-revoked` via `assert_live_native` (revocation beats expiry); expired anchor refuses `delegation-expired`. Pure ticket chains need no revocation input. Red-first: both facets reproduced BREAK on pristine base (present-after-revoke, issue-on-revoked); re-pinned `evals/w300_redteam_probes.py` F378 probes (incl. new fail-closed / substituted-revoker / ancestor-revocation probes) HELD with exact coded refusals; `tests/test_delegation_compose.py` receipt-anchored call sites updated to the new API; w299 delegation batteries green.)
## F380: workflow authority verification treats the revocation ledger as optional -- a revoked chain authorizes when the caller omits the ledger, and the completed-step replay path skips all authority checks (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-302 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w302_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F380-revoked-no-ledger-executes`,
`F380-replay-no-authority-check`, `F380-replay-cross-actor`).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow.py::_verify_authority` consults the revocation
ledger only "when a revocation ledger is presented"
(`ledger = authority.get("revocation_ledger"); if ledger is not None`).
The authority dict is constructed by the caller -- the same agent whose
authority is being checked -- so a holder of a REVOKED delegation chain
omits the key and the step executes: verified empirically
(`run_step` returned outputs under a revoked chain with the ledger
omitted; the control with the ledger presented refuses coded
`workflow-authority-revoked`). Worse, the completed-step replay path in
`run_step` returns BEFORE `_verify_authority` is reached, so replaying
completed steps performs NO authority check at all -- not even the
actor binding. Verified empirically: `replay()` of completed steps
succeeded with a revoked chain and no ledger, and succeeded again with
a DIFFERENT actor presenting garbage authority (`{"actor_id":
"mallory", "chain": [], "trust_roots": []}`), returning the victim
run's recorded outputs. The module's standing design rule -- "every
resume re-proves its authority" -- is violated on both paths. Contrast
the sibling modules: `gov/workflow_idempotency.py` requires
`authority_verifier` positionally, and `gov/workflow_saga.py` holds
verifiers deployment-side where the caller cannot omit them.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Revocation is the delegation stack's
kill switch; this is the same class as F377/F378/F379 (revocation
visibility on a revocation-enforcement seam). The replay variant is a
cross-actor read of another run's step outputs with zero
authentication. Preconditions are plausible: any agent that can call
the library constructs its own authority dict.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) revocation liveness is enforced whenever a
chain is verified -- require the revocation ledger on every authority
verification (fail closed when absent, the F378 precedent), or the
deployment pins and tests that it always supplies one; (2) the
completed-step replay path re-verifies authority (including the actor
binding) before returning recorded outputs; (3) the F380 probes flip to
HELD; (4) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-302 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-303 lane 1).

**Closure record (wave-303 lane 1):** chose the feature-preserving
close-when: the revocation ledger is REQUIRED on every
`WorkflowStore._verify_authority` call -- `gov/workflow.py` now fails
closed coded `workflow-authority-revoked` when
`authority.get("revocation_ledger")` is absent (the F378 precedent;
no new codes minted, pin stays 1820). The ledger check itself is
unchanged otherwise (`assert_live_native`, revoked -> the same
`workflow-authority-revoked`). Second, `run_step` re-proves authority
on EVERY entry: the `_verify_authority` call moved ahead of both
completed-step replay paths (the seq-slot path and the step-level
idempotency-key path), so `replay()` -- which delegates to
`run_step` -- re-verifies authority including the actor binding before
returning recorded outputs. The same defect class was closed in
`sleep_step` and `recv_step`: their completed paths also re-prove
authority before trusting the checkpoint. Module docstring updated:
the authority shape is now `"revocation_ledger": DelegationRevoker`
(required).
Red-first: pristine wave-302-merge base repro via the w302 red-team
battery's own probes: `F380-revoked-no-ledger-executes`,
`F380-replay-no-authority-check`, `F380-replay-cross-actor` 3 BREAK ->
all 5 F380 probes HELD on the fixed tree (the two controls stayed
HELD; the fresh-chain control was re-pinned to present a ledger, the
honest path). New standing regression pins: `evals/w303_f380_probes.py`
(21 probes: ledger-required on start_run/run_step/replay/notify/
complete_run; replay re-verification incl. cross-actor; sleep/recv
completed-path re-verification; honest-path execute/replay/resume)
0 BREAK / 21 HELD / 0 ERROR under staging and
`env -u GOV_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`; `tests/test_workflow_f380.py` 12/12.
Re-pinned for the new contract: `tests/test_workflow.py::\ntest_authority_without_ledger_refuses` (was
`test_authority_without_ledger_still_verifies`), the w302 red-team
F380 probes, and the w302 approval battery/unit `_authority` helpers
(now mint a fresh empty revoker when none is passed). Adjacent suites
green: test_workflow 26/26, test_workflow_approval 17/17,
test_workflow_composed 17/17, test_workflow_branch 18/18,
test_workflow_saga 21/21, test_workflow_idempotency 18/18,
test_workflow_routing 16/16, test_decision_codes 19/19.
Honest residuals: revocation-list freshness remains
deployment-owned (a fail-closed refusal when no ledger is presented
does not prove the presented ledger is fresh); a compromised
delegator key is the compromised-host class.
## F381: idempotency complete()/checkpoint() are not caller-bound and evict_completed() is unauthenticated -- any authorized caller can complete another actor's in-flight operation with an arbitrary result (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-302 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w302_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`F381-cross-caller-complete-poisons`, `F381-evict-unauthenticated`,
`F381-cross-caller-checkpoint`).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow_idempotency.py` re-verifies authority at
`begin()` on every path, but the returned `BeginOutcome` is not bound
to the beginning caller: `complete()` and `checkpoint()` consult no
caller identity. Verified empirically: alice begins key K (op `pay`);
mallory begins the same key with the same digest (authorized for the
namespace/op_class) and gets a RETRY outcome on alice's in-flight
record; mallory's `complete()` with a fabricated result digest/ref
succeeds, and alice's subsequent re-begin replays mallory's fabricated
`result_ref` -- the replay cache is poisoned and the acks_late
discipline ("marked complete only AFTER its effects are durably
recorded") is defeated by someone who recorded no effects. Separately,
`evict_completed()` takes an `operator` NAME but no `authority_verifier`
at all: verified empirically that an unauthenticated caller evicts a
completed record, forcing re-execution. The module's own threat model
names the authority verifier the trust anchor, yet two of the three
state-mutating paths after `begin()` never consult it.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Cross-actor result poisoning in a
component whose contract is exactly-once execution with recorded
results; unauthenticated eviction defeats the completed-set durability
the module exists to provide. Any caller authorized for the
(namespace, op_class) scope can do this -- no key theft needed.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `BeginOutcome` records the beginning
caller and `complete()`/`checkpoint()` refuse when the completing
caller differs (or re-verify authority with the completing caller's
identity); (2) `evict_completed()` requires and verifies an authority
verifier like `begin()` does; (3) the F381 probes flip to HELD; (4)
adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (closed 2026-10-03, wave-303 lane 2).
## F382: workflow journal reload re-appends every record -- the file doubles on every restart (LOW, OPEN)

**Cells:** wave-302 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w302_redteam_probes.py` (probe `F382-reload-doubles-journal`).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow.py::WorkflowStore._load()` replays the
journal through `self._append(record)`, and `_append` writes to the
file whenever `self._path` is set. Loading therefore re-appends every
record it just read. Verified empirically: a 2-record journal became 4
records after one `WorkflowStore(path=...)` reload, with byte-identical
duplicated records. Every process restart doubles the file: unbounded
disk growth under normal operation of a durable-execution library,
where restarts are routine. (Duplicate records are also re-indexed
idempotently in memory, so the corruption is silent -- nothing refuses.)

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Correctness/availability bug, no attacker
needed; integrity of the in-memory state is preserved (digests
recompute), but the store file grows without bound and a flipped byte
in a duplicated record would then refuse `workflow-checkpoint-tampered`
on the next load.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `_load()` populates memory without
re-appending to the file (or opens the file in a read phase distinct
from the append phase); (2) the F382 probe flips to HELD (reload is a
fixed point: N records before == N after); (3) adjacent batteries stay
green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-302 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-303 lane 3).

**Closure record (red-first verified):** reproduces BREAK on the
pristine wave-302 base (2 -> 4 -> 8 lines across two reloads, silent)
and HELD on the fixed tree. Fix in `gov/workflow.py`:
`_append(record, persist=True)` with the file write gated on
`persist`; `_load()` now calls `_append(record, persist=False)` so
loading populates the in-memory indexes without re-appending the
journal file -- reload is a fixed point (N == N across any number of
reloads; loaded indexes equal live indexes; tamper-refusal and
crash-tear behavior unchanged). New regression pins:
`evals/w303_f382f383_probes.py` (6 F382 probes: fixed point, double
reload, index equality, replay+resume after load, tamper refuses,
tear tolerated) and `tests/test_workflow_f382f383.py` (13/13 OK);
adjacent suites 165/165 OK. No new decision codes; pin stays 1820.
## F383: workflow step-level idempotency key path replays stale outputs for a different step name/inputs, bypassing the drift refusal (LOW, OPEN)

**Cells:** wave-302 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w302_redteam_probes.py` (probe `F383-key-path-skips-drift`).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow.py::run_step` has two replay paths. The
seq-slot path refuses definition drift coded
(`workflow-step-unauthorized`) when the name or inputs differ. The
step-level idempotency-key path (`self._step_idem.get((run_id,
idempotency_key))`) returns the recorded outputs WITHOUT checking the
step name or the inputs digest. Verified empirically: step (seq 0,
name "step-a", inputs `{"in": 1}`) completed under key K; step (seq 5,
name "step-B-DIFFERENT", inputs `{"in": 999}`) under key K returned
`{"v": "A"}` with `replayed=True` -- a different operation's outputs,
without executing. The module documents "a step-level idempotency key
replays across seq slots" but does not document that the replay ignores
name/inputs; the inconsistency with its own drift refusal (and with
`gov/workflow_idempotency.py`, where same-key-different-digest is a
coded conflict) makes this a silent-wrong-result path: downstream steps
act on outputs from an operation that never ran with these inputs.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Exploitation needs key reuse across
different steps (caller-side), but the module's own contract treats
drift as an attack signal on the adjacent path -- the key path
silently bypasses it.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) the idempotency-key replay path applies
the same name and inputs-digest drift checks as the seq-slot path
(refusing `workflow-step-unauthorized` on mismatch); (2) the F383 probe
flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-302 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-303 lane 3).

**Closure record (red-first verified):** reproduces BREAK on the
pristine wave-302 base (seq 5, "step-B-DIFFERENT", different inputs
under key K replayed step-A's outputs with `replayed=True`) and HELD
on the fixed tree (refuses `workflow-step-unauthorized`). Fix in
`gov/workflow.py::run_step`: the idempotency-key hit path now applies
the same name/inputs-digest drift checks as the seq-slot path before
returning recorded outputs; the refusal is sticky (a refused drift
attempt neither executes nor corrupts the binding; a later correct
key hit still replays). Reuses the existing
`workflow-step-unauthorized` code -- no new decision codes; pin stays
1820. Intended test maintenance: `tests/test_workflow.py::
RunStepTests::test_step_idempotency_key_replays_across_seq` and
`evals/w301_workflow_probes.py::p_idempotency` were re-pinned from the
F383-vulnerable expectation (different name replays across slots) to
the closed expectation (same name/inputs replay across seq slots;
name/inputs drift refuses coded). New regression pins:
`evals/w303_f382f383_probes.py` (6 F383 probes) and
`tests/test_workflow_f382f383.py`; adjacent suites 165/165 OK.
## F384: escalated sagas have no operator recovery path -- escalation is terminal despite "until an operator intervenes" (LOW, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-302 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w302_redteam_probes.py` (probe `F384-escalation-terminal`).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow_saga.py::SagaManager.run()` and `resume()`
refuse an `escalated` saga, and the docstring says escalation lasts
"until an operator intervenes" -- but no manager API resolves,
retries, or clears an escalation (`dir(SagaManager)` exposes no
escalation/recover/resolve/retry method; `dump`/`load` round-trip
preserves the terminal status). Verified empirically: after a
compensation exhausted its attempts, `run` and `resume` both refuse
coded `workflow-saga-compensation-failed` with no path forward. A
transient compensation failure (e.g. a downstream service down for the
retry window) therefore bricks the saga permanently: completed steps
stay uncompensated-or-worse with no operator mechanism to finish the
rollback or re-drive the saga. Escalation is loud, as designed -- but
loud without recourse is a liveness bug in a durability component.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Availability/liveness; no silent wrong
behavior (the refusal is loud and coded), but the documented operator
intervention cannot be performed through the module.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) an operator recovery path exists and is
tested -- e.g. `resolve_escalation()` / `retry_compensation()` that
re-drives the failed compensation after the underlying cause is fixed,
or a documented, tested manual recovery procedure via dump/load; (2)
the F384 probe flips to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-302 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-303 lane 4).

**Closure record (wave-303 lane 4):** built the operator recovery path
in `gov/workflow_saga.py`: `describe_escalation()` (operator
inspection of the escalated state -- escalation code, outstanding
steps, attempt budget, history tail) + `resolve_escalation()` /
`retry_compensation()` (resolve). Three resolution actions:
`retry_compensation` re-drives the failed compensation with a FRESH
attempt window after the underlying cause is fixed;
`abort_and_compensate_all` continues the pass with the REMAINING budget
(no reset -- for causes fixed externally); `accept_manual_remediation`
accepts the operator's attestation for exactly the outstanding steps
(marked compensated, flagged `manual_remediation`, journaled --
dump/load round-trips the flag). Operator authority uses the same
verifier model as step authorities (`operator_authority_ref` on the
manager), re-verified NOW at every recovery call; a missing/refusing
operator fails closed `workflow-saga-operator-unauthorized` and the
escalation is untouched. Every recovery action is journaled
(`escalation_recovery_started` / `escalation_resolved` /
`manual_remediation_accepted`); non-escalated sagas, unknown actions,
and incomplete attestations refuse `workflow-saga-resolution-invalid`,
so double-recovery is safe. Red-first: pristine base BREAK (no
recovery API; run/resume refuse terminally) -> fixed tree 0 BREAK /
20 HELD (`evals/w303_f384_probes.py`) + 16/16 unit
(`tests/test_workflow_f384.py`); the w302_redteam F384 probe re-pinned
to the fixed behavior; adjacent saga/workflow suites green; pin
1820 -> 1822 (+2 workflow-saga-*); raw literals 1822/1822/0/sorted.
## F379: multi-hop delegation-bound leases honor only the root delegator's revocation list -- an intermediate delegator's revocation of the bound receipt is invisible (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-301 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w301_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F379-intermediate-revocation-invisible`,
`F379-correct-revoker-refused`).

**Defect:** `gov/coordination_lease.py::_check_delegation_binding_live`
accepts exactly one revoker, and its anti-substitution check demands the
CHAIN ROOT's delegator (`revoker.delegator_id != root_delegator` refuses
`coord-lease-invalid`), while `DelegationRevoker.assert_live_native`
checks every chain member against that single revoker's list. For a
multi-hop chain bound at the leaf (A delegating to B delegating to C,
binding on the B->C receipt), a revocation of the bound receipt by its
own delegator B -- recorded in B's revocation list -- is invisible: the
holder presents A's revoker (the only one the code accepts), A's list
has no such revocation, the chain verifies, and `check_write` returns
True. Verified empirically on native chains: after
`rev_b.revoke(child["receipt_id"])`, `check_write` with
`{"revoker": rev_a, "chain": [root, child], "trust_roots": [pub_a]}`
succeeds. Worse, the presenter cannot fix it: presenting B's revoker
(the one that actually revoked the bound receipt) is refused
`coord-lease-invalid` -- there is no path to get the genuine
revocation recognized. This contradicts the module's own docstring
("the presented revoker must be the bound receipt's delegator") and the
wave-300 lane-4 close-when ("Revoked receipt/ancestor maps to
coord-lease-fencing"): the REVOKED bound receipt does not map to
fencing. The tested direction ("revoked ancestor kills
descendant-bound grant") holds; the untested direction (revoked
descendant, revoked by its own delegator) does not.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Same class as F377/F378 (revocation
visibility on a revocation-enforcement seam). Preconditions are
plausible: multi-hop delegation-backed leases are explicitly
supported, and any intermediate delegator may revoke. Impact: a
delegatee whose capability was revoked by its direct delegator keeps
writing under the lease -- revocation does not beat expiry on this
path.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `check_write` consults every chain member
against its own delegator's revocation state -- e.g. accept a
per-delegator revoker mapping and verify each revoker speaks for its
delegator (extending the existing anti-substitution check per
revoker), refusing `coord-lease-fencing` when any member is revoked by
its delegator; alternatively, explicitly restrict bindings to
single-hop chains (refuse multi-hop bound chains coded at
`check_write`) with the restriction documented and tested; (2) the
F379 probes flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-301 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-302 lane 1).

**Closure record (wave-302 lane 1):** chose close-when option (a) --
per-delegator revoker sets with per-revoker anti-substitution, keeping
the multi-hop feature. `gov/coordination_lease.py::
_check_delegation_binding_live` now normalizes the revocation state
to a `{delegator_id: DelegationRevoker}` mapping: the new
`delegation_context["revokers"]` mapping, or the legacy
`delegation_context["revoker"]` single shape normalized to a
one-entry mapping (the single revoker must still speak for the chain
ROOT, preserving wave-300's wrong-delegator-substitution refusal).
Every chain member's revocation is checked against ITS delegator's
list, each with per-revoker anti-substitution (revoker's
`delegator_id` must match the member's; native: revoker key must
equal the receipt's `delegator_pubkey`, root additionally in
`trust_roots`; local-shape: revoker key must equal the keyring
entry). A member with no presented revoker refuses fail-closed
`coord-lease-fencing` -- a multi-hop chain presented with only the
root's list can no longer pass on the root's clean list. Refusal
order preserved: revoked -> `coord-lease-fencing`, expired ->
`coord-lease-expired`, other defects -> `coord-lease-invalid`.
Red-first: pristine-base repro (`/tmp/repro_f379.py`: B revokes the
bound leaf, A's revoker presented) BREAK (write returned True) ->
HELD (`coord-lease-fencing`) on the fixed tree; w300 battery F379
probes 3 BREAK / 0 ERROR on pristine base -> 5/5 HELD fixed;
`tests/test_revoke_lease.py` 20/20 (12 existing + 8 new
`TestF379PerDelegatorRevokers`); w300 battery 0/28/0; w301 F379
probes re-pinned to the fixed behavior (HELD). No new codes; pin
stays 1812. Honest residuals: revocation-list freshness remains
deployment-owned (a presenter can withhold new revocations until the
verifier demands a fresh list -- fail-closed only when no state for a
hop is presented); compromised delegator key is the
compromised-host class.

## F385: workflow_branch resume_lease never verifies the suspension's XID against the coordinator's live transactions -- the documented XID binding is decorative (LOW, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-303 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w303_redteam_probes.py` (probe `F385-resume-xid-unenforced`).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow_branch.py::BranchCoordinator.suspend_lease`
records the transaction XID into the suspension record ("parks the
lease (scope, fencing token, holder, XID binding, suspension
instant)"), but `resume_lease` never resolves that XID against the
coordinator's live transactions: it shape-checks the XID
(`_check_xid`) and calls `lease_manager.check_write` on the
(scope, token, holder) triple only. Verified empirically on the
wave-302 base: a suspension created under transaction xid_A resumes
`True` when the record's XID is swapped for xid_B (a different live
transaction), and resumes `True` for a well-formed XID that was never
begun. The XID binding therefore constrains nothing -- a suspension
record is portable across transactions, and a coordinator that trusts
`resume_lease`'s success as "this lease is parked for transaction X"
is reasoning about an unenforced property. The underlying lease
liveness check (`check_write`) still holds, so no unauthorized write
results; this is a binding-integrity gap, not an authorization
bypass.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The lease itself is still liveness-gated
by `check_write` (expired/stale leases refuse coded); the missing
check lets a suspension record drift across transaction contexts,
which matters only to coordinators that rely on the XID binding the
record claims.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `resume_lease` resolves
`suspension["xid"]` through `self._txn` (fail closed on unknown XID),
so resume is bound to a live transaction of this coordinator; (2)
the F385 probe flips to HELD (both the cross-transaction and the
never-begun variants refuse); (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-303 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-304 lane A: `gov/workflow_branch.py::
resume_lease` now resolves `suspension["xid"]` through `self._txn`
(fail closed on unknown XIDs), requires the transaction to still be
open (committed/rolled-back refuse), and requires the presented record
to match field-for-field the suspension parked for that XID by
`suspend_lease` (the coordinator stores the parked record in the
transaction; mismatch refuses `workflow-branch-xid-mismatch`,
existing high-severity code). The exact parked-record match also
closes the same-seed A->B swap variant caught by the SPEC-axis review
(a pubkey-only binding misses it when both transactions share the
coordinator's key). The w303_redteam `F385-resume-xid-unenforced`
probe flips HELD (both the cross-transaction and never-begun variants
refuse coded); new `evals/w303_f385_probes.py` (9 probes) +
`tests/test_workflow_f385.py` (9 tests) pin the closure; taxonomy pin
unchanged at 1826 (no new codes). Residual: the suspension record is
an unauthenticated dict -- a fully-fabricated record is not
detectable unless it exactly matches a parked one (which requires
observing it); the lease liveness oracle (`check_write`) still gates
every resume, so this remains a binding-integrity fix, not an
authorization bypass.)

## F386: workflow_composed installs saga authority verifiers into the shared process-global SagaManager under plan-scoped refs bound to per-composer mutable context, and never removes them -- a second composer sharing the manager overwrites the first's verifier (LOW, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-303 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w303_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F386-verifier-collision`,
`F386-control-no-collision`).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow_composed.py::WorkflowComposer._install_saga_verifier`
writes `self._saga._verifiers[ref] = verify` where `ref =
"composed-auth:<plan_digest[:12]>:<unit>"` (plan-scoped) but the
`verify` closure reads `self._exec_ctx` (per-composer-instance mutable
state), and the entry is never removed when the saga unit completes.
Two `WorkflowComposer` instances sharing one `SagaManager` (a
constructor argument, plausible in a server) and executing the same
plan with overlapping lifetimes collide on the ref: the second
install silently overwrites the first's. Verified empirically two
ways on the wave-302 base. (a) Mechanism (white-box): composer c1
installs a verifier under ref R with a revoked authority A in its
context (its own verifier correctly returns False); composer c2
installs under the same ref R with valid authority B; the manager's
entry is now c2's closure and returns True -- A's revocation is
invisible to c1's saga, which would re-prove B's authority instead of
A's, violating "every compensation re-proves the ORIGINAL step's
authority". (b) Consequence (public API, deterministic): c1 executes
a saga plan; inside its s2 compensation it reentrantly runs
c2.execute of the SAME plan; c2's install overwrites c1's verifier
and c2 completes (its context clears); c1's subsequent s1
compensation authority check then fails closed and the saga escalates
coded `workflow-saga-compensation-unauthorized` -- where the control
(c2 executing a different plan, hence a different ref) compensates
normally. The fail-closed direction is a robustness escalation (and
F384, OPEN, makes escalation terminal); the wrong-authority direction
is an authority-integrity break. The per-composer plan-actor pin
(`_check_plan_actor`) does not help: the verifier never consults it.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Triggering needs two composers sharing
one saga manager with overlapping execution of the same plan
(concurrent threads or reentrancy) -- narrow, same trust plane -- but
the consequence is genuine authority confusion on the compensation
path, the exact path Decision 3 claims is unified.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) verifier refs are scoped per composer
instance (e.g. a per-composer/per-execute nonce in the ref) so two
composers cannot collide, AND verifier entries are removed when the
saga unit's execution completes (finally) so no stale closures linger
on the shared manager; (2) the F386 collision probe flips to HELD
(c1 compensates normally despite the reentrant same-plan execute)
and the control stays HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Closure (2026-10-03, wave-304 lane B):** all three close-when
criteria met. `gov/workflow_composed.py` mints a per-composer-instance
nonce in `__init__` (`secrets.token_hex(8)`); `_execute_saga_unit`
builds a nonce-scoped unit tag (`<nonce>:<plan_digest[:12]>:<unit>`)
so the verifier ref (`composed-auth:<scoped_tag>`) AND the
process-global op registry names (`composed:<scoped_tag>:action|comp:<sid>`)
are both composer-scoped -- this also closes a masked second collision
the red-first loop found: the wrapper ops were registered under
plan-scoped names, so the second composer's registration shadowed the
first's compensation closures (reading the second composer's
`_exec_ctx`, which is None after its execute completes -- a
TypeError crash on the first composer's later compensation steps).
The verifier entry is removed deterministically in a `finally`
(`_remove_saga_verifier`) covering run, compensation end, and the
outbox drain, on success and on failure. The compensation authority
model is unchanged: the closure still re-proves the workflow
authority NOW via `WorkflowStore._verify_authority`, and a
mid-flight revocation still refuses coded
`workflow-saga-compensation-unauthorized` (probed). No new decision
codes; taxonomy pin unchanged at 1826/1826/0. New regression pins:
`evals/w303_f386_probes.py` (collision / verifier-removed /
op-names-scoped / compensation-authority-intact / control, all HELD)
and `tests/test_workflow_f386.py` (8/8 OK). The w303 red-team
`F386-verifier-collision` and `F386-control-no-collision` probes flip
to HELD; adjacent batteries (composed/branch/approval) stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-303 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-304 lane B).
## F387: workflow recv_step/sleep_step completed paths skip the inputs-drift refusal that run_step enforces -- a slot completed for one event/wake_at replays for a different event/wake_at (LOW, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-304 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w304_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F387-recv-event-drift`,
`F387-sleep-wakeat-drift`).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow.py::WorkflowStore.recv_step` and `::sleep_step`
check the step NAME on the completed path but never the recorded
inputs. `recv_step` records `inputs_digest = _digest({"event": event})`
and `sleep_step` records `inputs_digest = _digest({"wake_at": wake_at})`,
yet the completed-path replay checks only `rec["name"] != name`. The
`run_step` replay paths (sequence slot AND step-level idempotency key)
both refuse `workflow-step-unauthorized` on name/inputs drift, and the
module docstring promises drift refusal "for an already-completed step
slot". Verified empirically on the wave-303 base: (a) a slot completed
for event "settled" (payload `{"amount": 100}`) replayed
`(payload, True)` for a "refunded" subscription -- the recorded payload
for one event is returned as the receipt for another, silently;
(b) a slot completed with `wake_at=T1` returned `(True, True)` for
`wake_at=T2` (timing semantics only -- the outputs are constant
`{"awake": True}`; the recv instance carries the severity). The F380
closure (authority re-proof ahead of the replay path) is intact -- this
is the F383 defect class (stale-output replay across inputs drift) on
the two paths lane 3 did not touch.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Same defect class as F383 (filed LOW):
the trigger is the run's own authorized actor re-presenting a changed
workflow definition (or a definition bug), not a cross-actor attack;
the consequence is payload confusion on the recv path (a step records
"received event X" while subscribed to event Y) rather than a bypass.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `recv_step` and `sleep_step` completed
paths apply the same inputs-drift checks as `run_step`: refuse coded
`workflow-step-unauthorized` when the re-presented event/wake_at does
not match the recorded `inputs_digest`; (2) the F387 probes flip to
HELD (both drift cases refuse coded, the matching case still replays);
(3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (2026-10-03, wave-305 lane A). **Closure record:** the
`recv_step`/`sleep_step` completed paths in `gov/workflow.py` now apply
the same name AND inputs-digest drift checks as `run_step`'s
sequence-slot path: re-presented event/wake_at differing from the
recorded `inputs_digest` refuses coded `workflow-step-unauthorized`
(F383 defect class). Authority re-proof (F380) stays first -- a revoked
ledger refuses `workflow-authority-revoked` even when inputs also drift.
Red-first: `evals/w304_redteam_probes.py`
`F387-recv-event-drift`/`F387-sleep-wakeat-drift` BREAK on the pristine
wave-304 base, flip HELD on the fixed tree; new `evals/w303_f387_probes.py`
0 BREAK / 6 HELD (staging and clean env) + pin/footer/depth-1 green
checks; `tests/test_workflow_f387.py` 8/8 OK; adjacent suites
(`tests.test_workflow`, `w303_f380`, `w303_f381`, `w303_f382f383`,
`w303_f384`, `w303_f385`, `w303_f386`, `w303_f388`,
`w303_authority_lifecycle`) green. Residual: none beyond the
pre-existing deployment-owned boundaries; the timeout-completed recv
path is covered by the same check (inputs_digest over `{"event":
event}`).
## F388: composed _resolve_replay trusts a poisoned (digest, ref) pair -- a foreign run's checkpoint outputs can be returned without executing (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-304 lane C (this lane), claim 2026-10-03T08:42:50Z,
first numbered F387, renumbered to F388 at 2026-10-03 08:45Z when the
wave-304 independent red team filed F387 first (wave-272
earliest-filed rule). Standing regression pins:
`evals/w303_f388_probes.py` (probes `F388-foreign-run-replay`,
`F388-same-run-ref-repoint`, `F388-legit-replay-survives`,
`F388-detached-resolution-refused`), `tests/test_workflow_f388.py`
(7/7).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow_composed.py::WorkflowComposer._resolve_replay`
resolved the idempotency record's `(result_digest, result_ref)` pair
back to a workflow checkpoint without checking the pair is NATIVE to
the composed execution. Wave-303 lane 2's caller binding
(`gov/workflow_idempotency.py`, code
`workflow-idempotency-caller-mismatch`) covers the idem-store layer,
but an attacker who begins AND completes as one caller can plant a
record whose `result_ref` names a foreign run's completed step: the
composer returned the foreign run's outputs without executing.
Verified two ways on the pristine wave-303 base (c9138cc53888). (a)
Public API: attacker begins+completes a record as `mallory` with the
real digest of a victim run's completed step and ref
`wfstep:victim:1`; the composer's own `execute` (run R) of a plan
with the same idem key returns `{"stolen": 1}` and the unit fn never
runs. (b) Same-run re-point: a record begun by a different caller
whose ref names another unit's step of the CURRENT run is accepted,
returning the wrong unit's outputs. The run-id parse existed but was
only used for the `get_step` lookup -- never compared to the run the
composer is executing.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Attribution/visibility defeated and a
foreign run's outputs are silently substituted for execution -- the
composed path's "never silently trust" contract is broken -- but the
attacker must plant the record in the idem store under a digest the
victim plan will actually present (same trust plane as the store),
and no data leaves the system.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `_resolve_replay` refuses coded
`workflow-composed-replay-foreign` when the ref names a run other
than `ctx["run_id"]`, when the record's begin-time caller differs
from the plan actor, and when no composed execution is in progress
(detached resolution -- previously crashed uncoded or resolved
foreign); (2) the F388 attack probes flip to HELD on the fixed tree
and the legit-replay control stays HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay
green; (4) exactly one new decision code at its true sorted position,
pin repointed.

**Fix** (wave-304 lane C): `gov/workflow_composed.py::_resolve_replay`
now fails closed in order: no execution context ->
`workflow-composed-replay-foreign`; unparseable ref -> existing
`workflow-composed-divergent`; ref run != `ctx["run_id"]` ->
`workflow-composed-replay-foreign`; `outcome.record_caller` (new
read-only property on `BeginOutcome` in `gov/workflow_idempotency.py`,
snapshotting the begin-time record caller) != `ctx["actor"]` ->
`workflow-composed-replay-foreign`; then the existing
missing/incomplete/digest-mismatch divergent checks unchanged. The
new code (`critical`, evidence

## F379: multi-hop delegation-bound leases honor only the root delegator's revocation list -- an intermediate delegator's revocation of the bound receipt is invisible (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-301 independent red-team, 2026-10-03. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w301_redteam_probes.py` (probes `F379-intermediate-revocation-invisible`,
`F379-correct-revoker-refused`).

**Defect:** `gov/coordination_lease.py::_check_delegation_binding_live`
accepts exactly one revoker, and its anti-substitution check demands the
CHAIN ROOT's delegator (`revoker.delegator_id != root_delegator` refuses
`coord-lease-invalid`), while `DelegationRevoker.assert_live_native`
checks every chain member against that single revoker's list. For a
multi-hop chain bound at the leaf (A delegating to B delegating to C,
binding on the B->C receipt), a revocation of the bound receipt by its
own delegator B -- recorded in B's revocation list -- is invisible: the
holder presents A's revoker (the only one the code accepts), A's list
has no such revocation, the chain verifies, and `check_write` returns
True. Verified empirically on native chains: after
`rev_b.revoke(child["receipt_id"])`, `check_write` with
`{"revoker": rev_a, "chain": [root, child], "trust_roots": [pub_a]}`
succeeds. Worse, the presenter cannot fix it: presenting B's revoker
(the one that actually revoked the bound receipt) is refused
`coord-lease-invalid` -- there is no path to get the genuine
revocation recognized. This contradicts the module's own docstring
("the presented revoker must be the bound receipt's delegator") and the
wave-300 lane-4 close-when ("Revoked receipt/ancestor maps to
coord-lease-fencing"): the REVOKED bound receipt does not map to
fencing. The tested direction ("revoked ancestor kills
descendant-bound grant") holds; the untested direction (revoked
descendant, revoked by its own delegator) does not.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Same class as F377/F378 (revocation
visibility on a revocation-enforcement seam). Preconditions are
plausible: multi-hop delegation-backed leases are explicitly
supported, and any intermediate delegator may revoke. Impact: a
delegatee whose capability was revoked by its direct delegator keeps
writing under the lease -- revocation does not beat expiry on this
path.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `check_write` consults every chain member
against its own delegator's revocation state -- e.g. accept a
per-delegator revoker mapping and verify each revoker speaks for its
delegator (extending the existing anti-substitution check per
revoker), refusing `coord-lease-fencing` when any member is revoked by
its delegator; alternatively, explicitly restrict bindings to
single-hop chains (refuse multi-hop bound chains coded at
`check_write`) with the restriction documented and tested; (2) the
F379 probes flip to HELD; (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-301 independent red-team;
closed 2026-10-03, wave-302 lane 1).

**Closure record (wave-302 lane 1):** chose close-when option (a) --
per-delegator revoker sets with per-revoker anti-substitution, keeping
the multi-hop feature. `gov/coordination_lease.py::
_check_delegation_binding_live` now normalizes the revocation state
to a `{delegator_id: DelegationRevoker}` mapping: the new
`delegation_context["revokers"]` mapping, or the legacy
`delegation_context["revoker"]` single shape normalized to a
one-entry mapping (the single revoker must still speak for the chain
ROOT, preserving wave-300's wrong-delegator-substitution refusal).
Every chain member's revocation is checked against ITS delegator's
list, each with per-revoker anti-substitution (revoker's
`delegator_id` must match the member's; native: revoker key must
equal the receipt's `delegator_pubkey`, root additionally in
`trust_roots`; local-shape: revoker key must equal the keyring
entry). A member with no presented revoker refuses fail-closed
`coord-lease-fencing` -- a multi-hop chain presented with only the
root's list can no longer pass on the root's clean list. Refusal
order preserved: revoked -> `coord-lease-fencing`, expired ->
`coord-lease-expired`, other defects -> `coord-lease-invalid`.
Red-first: pristine-base repro (`/tmp/repro_f379.py`: B revokes the
bound leaf, A's revoker presented) BREAK (write returned True) ->
HELD (`coord-lease-fencing`) on the fixed tree; w300 battery F379
probes 3 BREAK / 0 ERROR on pristine base -> 5/5 HELD fixed;
`tests/test_revoke_lease.py` 20/20 (12 existing + 8 new
`TestF379PerDelegatorRevokers`); w300 battery 0/28/0; w301 F379
probes re-pinned to the fixed behavior (HELD). No new codes; pin
stays 1812. Honest residuals: revocation-list freshness remains
deployment-owned (a presenter can withhold new revocations until the
verifier demands a fresh list -- fail-closed only when no state for a
hop is presented); compromised delegator key is the
compromised-host class.
## F389: workflow_branch suspend_lease performs no authority check -- anyone who knows the xid can re-park a different suspension record, clobbering the legitimate holder's parked suspension (LOW, CLOSED)

**Defect:** `BranchCoordinator.suspend_lease(xid, lease_manager, scope, fencing_token, holder_id, suspended_at)` accepts any caller who presents a well-formed xid. It performs no authority check -- no holder proof, no fencing-token liveness check at suspend time. An attacker who knows the xid (64-hex random ids are documented for uniqueness, not as secret bearer capabilities) can re-park a different suspension record under the same xid, overwriting the legitimate holder's parked record (`txn["suspension"] = dict(record)`).

**Consequence:** the legitimate holder's subsequent `resume_lease` with the original record then refuses `workflow-branch-xid-mismatch` -- the F385 exact-parked-record match makes the clobbering stick. The suspension is broken until the holder re-suspends. The attacker cannot complete the resume themselves (`lease_manager.check_write` still gates on the fencing token at resume time), so this is availability-only, not an authorization bypass.

**Repro (public API):** park under xid_A with a live lease; call `suspend_lease(xid_A, lm, scope, 999999, "mallory", ...)` -- accepted, no authority parameter exists; `resume_lease(original_record)` now refuses `workflow-branch-xid-mismatch`. Battery probe `F389-suspend-lease-clobber` in `evals/w305_redteam_probes.py`.

**Severity:** LOW (availability only; recoverable by re-suspending; requires xid knowledge).

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `suspend_lease` proves lease-holdership at suspend time -- e.g. `lease_manager.check_write(scope, fencing_token, holder_id, checked_at=suspended_at)` before parking, refusing coded on a stale/foreign token -- so an unauthenticated re-park cannot overwrite the parked record; (2) the F389 probe flips to HELD (attacker's re-park refused; legitimate holder's suspend+resume still works); (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Cells:** wave-305 lane E (independent red team), claim 2026-10-03T09:15:00Z. Standing regression pin: `evals/w305_redteam_probes.py` (probe `F389-suspend-lease-clobber`).

**Status: CLOSED** (filed 2026-10-03, wave-305 independent red-team; closed 2026-10-03, wave-306 lane A: `suspend_lease` now proves lease-holdership at suspend time via `lease_manager.check_write(scope, fencing_token, holder_id, checked_at=suspended_at)` BEFORE parking -- a stale/foreign token refuses `coord-lease-fencing`, a dead lease refuses `coord-lease-expired`; the fencing token is the lease capability, so only the current holder can park. Legitimate re-suspending with the current token (latest park wins) still works. No new decision codes; pin unchanged 1827. Red-first: the `F389-suspend-lease-clobber` probe BREAKs on the pristine wave-305 base and is HELD on the fixed tree; new `evals/w303_f389_probes.py` (4 probes) + `tests/test_workflow_f389.py` (6 tests) green under staging and clean env; adjacent workflow_branch/f385 suites 27/27 OK.)

## F390: composed _resolve_replay does not bind the ref's step to the replaying unit -- a poisoned (digest, ref) pair naming a different completed step of the SAME run returns the wrong unit's outputs without executing (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-306 lane B (this lane), claim 2026-10-03T10:05:00Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w303_f390_probes.py` (probes
`F390-same-run-wrong-step`, `F390-legit-replay-survives`,
`F390-saga-action-step-bound`, `F390-cross-unit-ref-refused`),
`tests/test_workflow_f390.py`.

**Defect:** `gov/workflow_composed.py::WorkflowComposer._resolve_replay`
(F388-hardened) binds the idempotency record's `(result_digest,
result_ref)` pair to the run (`run_id` match), the caller
(`record_caller == plan actor`), completion, and digest -- but NOT the
ref's step to the replaying unit. An attacker who begins AND completes
as the legitimate plan actor (the F388 threat model) can plant a record
under the victim unit's idempotency key whose `result_ref` names a
*different completed step of the same run*: every F388 check passes
(run matches, caller matches, step completed, digest matches) and the
composer returns the wrong step's outputs without executing the unit's
fn. Verified on the pristine wave-305 base (d9554021) through the public
API: (1) legitimately execute u1 under run R (step R:1 completes with
`{"one": 1}`); (2) plant under u2's key as the plan actor with the exact
op_digest, `result_digest = _digest({"one": 1})`, `ref = "wfstep:R:1"`;
(3) execute u2 under run R -- u2 returns `{"one": 1}` and its fn never
runs. The idempotency key's integrity (key k2 must map to u2's outputs)
is violated; the F388 "native to this composed execution" guarantee
held only at run+caller granularity, not unit granularity.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `_resolve_replay` verifies the resolved
step's recorded name matches the replaying unit's step name
(`"fn:<unit>"`, `"saga:<unit>:<step>"`, `"saga-comp:<unit>:<step>"`,
`"slip:<unit>:leg:<idx>"`), refusing coded
`workflow-composed-replay-foreign` on mismatch; (2) the F390 probes flip
to HELD (wrong-step replay refused coded; legitimate replays -- fn,
saga action/comp, slip leg -- still return their own outputs); (3)
adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed and closed 2026-10-03, wave-306 lane B: step-name
binding in `_resolve_replay`; no new decision codes, reuses
`workflow-composed-replay-foreign`).

## F397: WorkflowComposer.retry_saga_unit accepts a stale `at` -- the step authority is re-verified at a caller-chosen past instant, resurrecting an expired delegation for the compensation re-drive (LOW, CLOSED 2026-10-03, wave-313 lane A)

**Cells:** wave-312 independent red-team (this lane), claim 2026-10-03T17:44:00Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w312_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`F397-stale-at-retry`, `F397-stale-at-zero`).

**Defect:** F394 (wave-310 lane A) added
`WorkflowComposer.retry_saga_unit(unit_name, resolution, *, at)`. The
`at` parameter is documented as "the retry instant ... The step
authority is re-verified AT this instant per the F384 'NOW' contract:
pass the current time so post-execution revocation or expiry is
honored." The code enforces only `_is_int(at) and at >= 0`
(`gov/workflow_composed.py`): nothing requires `at` to be the retry
time. The retry builds `retry_ctx = {..., "at": at, "now": at}`, sets
it as `_exec_ctx`, and re-installs the step authority verifier, which
calls `WorkflowStore._verify_authority(authority, run, ctx["at"])`;
that calls `_delegation.authorize(chain, action, actor, at=at, ...)`
(expiry is instant-relative: `at >= expires_at` refuses) and
`ledger.assert_live_native(chain, at, ...)` (chain defects
instant-relative; recorded revocations are sticky and NOT bypassed).
So an operator holding a valid operator authority retries with a stale
`at` -- any instant in `[0, expires_at)`, e.g. the original execution
instant or even `at=0` (the check has no lower bound against the
delegation's `issued_at`) -- and the expired delegation verifies: the
compensation re-drive executes under expired authority. Verified on
the wave-311 merge tree (e8cdd51f) through the public API: delegation
`expires_at = AT_EXEC+3600`; saga escalates at AT_EXEC; retry at the
true retry instant (AT_EXEC+7200) refuses coded
`workflow-saga-compensation-unauthorized` (compensation never runs --
control); retry with `at=AT_EXEC` succeeds, compensation re-runs
(3->4 calls), saga reaches `compensated`; retry with `at=0` likewise
succeeds. The operator's own authority is still re-verified at
recovery time (F384 intact); only the STEP authority's time-box is
defeated, and only its expiry arm (revocation stays sticky).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Requires an already-authorized operator
(the recovery action itself is legitimate and operator-gated); the
blast radius is the plan's own compensation fns executing under an
expired (not revoked) step delegation. Same subsystem and rating as
F394/F384 (operator-recovery path).

**Close-when:** (1) `retry_saga_unit` refuses (coded) a stale `at` --
e.g. `at` must not precede the escalation (the escalation's logical
instant is available in the retained retry material; no wall clock
needed), or the step authority is re-verified at a
caller-independent retry instant; (2) the F397 probes flip to HELD
(stale-`at` retry refused coded; fresh-`at` retry on a live delegation
still re-drives; expired delegation still fails closed at the true
retry instant); (3) the F394 operator path keeps working and
F386/F384 are not weakened; (4) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-03, wave-313 lane A.** `retry_saga_unit` now
retains the escalation's logical instant (`escalated_at`) in the
`_saga_retry_ctx` material and refuses coded
`workflow-saga-resolution-invalid` when the caller's `at` is not
strictly after it -- the retry is causally after the escalation, so a
retry instant at or before the escalation (replayed execution instant,
`at=0`, ...) is a stale clock claim. The step authority is therefore
never re-verified at a past instant; no wall clock is introduced and
no new decision code was needed (pin unchanged 1851). Standing
regression pins: `evals/w313_f397_probes.py` (0/13/0 staging and clean
env); the w312 red-team F397 probes flip to HELD. Residual: under the
system's pure logical-time model (every `at` in the tree is
caller-supplied, including `execute`), an operator can still claim a
post-escalation instant inside the delegation's validity window (e.g.
`at=escalation+1` while true time is later) -- unfalsifiable without a
trusted time source; the demonstrated breaks (exact-instant replay,
`at=0`) and all backward time travel are closed. The wave-313 red
team's `F397-stale-at-boundary` probe (`at=expires_at-1`) exercises
exactly this residual and is kept as a HELD residual pin (a genuine
in-window retry must succeed; refusing it would break the F394
happy path).

## F396: the F393 code binding ignores __defaults__/__kwdefaults__ -- two fns with identical bytecode but different default argument values share a plan digest, defeating the run->plan binding (MEDIUM, CLOSED 2026-10-03, wave-312 lane A)

**Cells:** wave-311 independent red-team (this lane), claim 2026-10-03T15:35:10Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w311_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`F396-defaults-fn`, `F396-defaults-saga`, `F396-kwdefaults-fn`).

**Defect:** F393 (wave-309 lane A) bound the plan digest to the unit's
code via `_code_fingerprint` (`__code__` fields plus `_closure_fingerprint`
for closed-over values). The fingerprint never reads `__defaults__` or
`__kwdefaults__`: two fns with identical bytecode whose default argument
values differ (e.g. a shared factory `mkfn(client)` binding the client as
a default `def fn(i, c=client)` -- the realistic shape is a shared library
whose functions take per-deployment client/config objects as defaults)
yield identical `code_digest` and therefore identical plan digests. The
run->plan binding then passes (same digest), the fn-unit `op_digest`
matches, `_begin_unit` returns REPLAY, and every `_resolve_replay` check
passes -- the victim's fn never executes and the attacker's outputs
return as native. Verified on the wave-310 merge tree (38650946) through
the public API: fn path (victim outputs `{"data": "from-evil"}`, victim
default object untouched 0 times) and saga action path (victim saga
"succeeds" with attacker outputs, victim action 0 calls). This is a
distinct channel from F395: F395 covers closed-over values (`co_freevars`);
defaults are function-object state outside `__code__` entirely, and the
collision holds even for JSON-native defaults -- an F395-scoped fix
(binding exotic closure values by value) would NOT close this.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Silent integrity violation with the same
impact as F393/F395: the victim's code never runs, attacker-controlled
outputs are returned as the victim's native results. The precondition
(bytecode-identical fns differing only in defaults) is the natural
generalization of the F395 shape.

**Close-when:** (1) two fns with identical bytecode but different
`__defaults__`/`__kwdefaults__` yield different code digests (or
`ComposedPlan` refuses the unit coded); (2) the F396 probes flip to HELD;
(3) JSON-native defaults keep crash-recovery stability (same source
reconstructs the same digest); (4) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-03, wave-312 lane A.** `_code_fingerprint`
now binds `__defaults__` and `__kwdefaults__` via the new
`_defaults_fingerprint` (JSON-native values by value, positional order
preserved, keyword-only sorted by name; non-JSON-native defaults
refuse coded `workflow-composed-definition-invalid`, F395-shaped fail
closed). The binding flows through `_unit_code_digest` into
`ComposedPlan.digest`, so the run->plan binding, `op_digest`, and
`_begin_unit`/`_resolve_replay` all compare default-bound digests.
Close-when evidence: (1) identical-bytecode fns with different
JSON-native `__defaults__`/`__kwdefaults__` yield different code
digests and plan digests; (2) the three w311 red-team F396 probes
(rewritten to assert the fix: digest distinction + coded
`workflow-composed-plan-mismatch` under the attacker's run + native
victim execution on a fresh run + coded refusal of exotic defaults)
flip to HELD; (3) same-source reconstruction yields identical digests
(incl. nested defaults, kwdefaults-only, None/empty defaults);
(4) `evals/w312_f396_probes.py` 0/13/0, `w311_redteam_probes.py`
0/25/0, `w311_f395_probes.py` green, `w310_f394_probes.py` green,
`w309_f393_probes.py` green; 278 workflow unit tests OK. No new
decision codes; pin unchanged 1841. Residuals: defaults mutated after
plan construction bind construction-time values (same TOCTOU class as
F395 closures); bound-method defaults bind via the method's
`__defaults__` delegation; exotic-default users must use JSON-native
configuration values (behavioral, documented).

## F395: the F393 code binding collides for exotic closures -- two fns with identical bytecode but different exotic closure state share a plan digest, defeating the run->plan binding (MEDIUM, CLOSED 2026-10-03, wave-311 lane A)

**Cells:** wave-310 independent red-team (this lane), claim 2026-10-03T13:27:00Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w310_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`F395-exotic-closure-fn`, `F395-exotic-closure-saga`), `evals/w311_f395_probes.py`.

**Defect:** F393 (wave-309 lane A) bound the plan digest to the unit's code
via `_code_fingerprint` (bytecode, constants, names, argcounts) plus
`_closure_fingerprint` for closed-over values. JSON-native closure values
are bound by value, but non-JSON-native ("exotic") values bind only
`type(value).__name__` -- a documented residual. The residual is
exploitable end-to-end: two fns with identical bytecode whose closures
differ only in exotic objects of the same type (e.g. a shared factory
`mkfn(client)` closing over different `Client` instances -- the realistic
shape is a shared library closing over per-deployment client/config
objects) yield identical `code_digest` and therefore identical plan
digests. The run->plan binding then passes (same digest), the fn-unit
`op_digest` (which covers the plan digest) matches, `_begin_unit`
returns REPLAY on the attacker's record, and every `_resolve_replay`
check passes (run, record-caller, digest, F390 name, F392 idempotency
binding) -- the victim's fn never executes and the attacker's outputs
return as native. Verified on the wave-309 tree (f0d6c9c1) through the
public API: fn path (victim outputs `{"data": "from-evil"}`, victim fn 0
calls) and saga action path (victim saga "succeeds" with attacker outputs,
victim action 0 calls).

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Silent integrity violation with the same
impact as F393: the victim's code never runs, attacker-controlled outputs
are returned as the victim's native results. The precondition is narrower
than F393 (requires bytecode-identical fns differing only in exotic closure
state), but the break is complete and silent once the shape holds.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `ComposedPlan` refuses (coded) fns that close
over non-JSON-native values, or binds them by a stable,
behavior-reflecting digest -- type-name-only binding is insufficient;
(2) the F395 probes flip to HELD (refused at construction, or digests
differ and the run->plan binding refuses coded
`workflow-composed-plan-mismatch`); (3) JSON-native closures keep working
with crash-recovery stability (same source reconstructs the same digest);
(4) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Closed:** 2026-10-03, wave-311 lane A. Direction (a) of the filed
close-when: `ComposedPlan` refuses (coded) exotic closures. A
behavior-reflecting digest for arbitrary objects is not well-defined
or stable -- `repr` carries memory addresses (breaks crash-recovery
re-execution), `hash()` defaults to identity, pickling is not
behavior and can fail -- so `_closure_fingerprint` fails closed:
any non-JSON-native closed-over value refuses
`workflow-composed-definition-invalid` (the F393 refusal code, no new
codes; pin stays 1829). The check is recursive via the new
`_is_json_native` helper (iterative, cycle-safe): an exotic value
nested inside a dict/list/tuple refuses too, because `_canon`'s
`default=str` would otherwise bind its `repr` silently. Refusal is
deterministic -- a plan that refuses refuses identically on every
rebuild -- and fires at plan construction (before any execution).
JSON-native closures keep the exact F393 by-value path
(crash-recovery stable, value-distinguishing). F393's
uninspectable-callable refusal is untouched (checked first, same
code). Verified: the original F395 attack (evil plan executes,
victim replays the attacker's record) cannot be constructed -- both
plans refuse coded at construction. Battery
`evals/w311_f395_probes.py` (10 probes + depth-1 green checks) pins
the closure: 0 BREAK / 14 HELD / 0 ERROR; adjacent batteries
w310_redteam / w309_f393 / w310_f394 / w308_f391 all green via green
checks.

**Status: CLOSED.**

pin unchanged 1829. Regression battery: `evals/w310_f394_probes.py`

the supported composer-API call pattern (probe IDs and intent
unchanged). Verified: `retry_compensation` and
