**Cells:** wave-309 independent red-team (this lane), claim 2026-10-03T12:13:00Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w309_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`F394-op-retry-composed`, `F394-abort-composed`,
`F394-direct-saga-retry-works`).

**Defect:** F384 (wave-303 lane 4) built the operator recovery path on
`SagaManager` -- `describe_escalation()` / `resolve_escalation()` /
`retry_compensation()` -- so an operator can re-drive a failed
compensation after fixing the underlying cause. For a DIRECT saga
(deployment-registered ops, persistent verifiers) this works
(probe `F394-direct-saga-retry-works`: retry re-invokes the fixed
compensation, saga ends `compensated`). For a COMPOSED saga unit it
cannot work: when the unit escalates, the composer's `finally` block
(`_execute_saga_unit`) deterministically removes the nonce-scoped
wrapper ops (`_remove_saga_ops`, wave-305 hygiene) AND the step
authority verifier (`_remove_saga_verifier`, F386). Both are
prerequisites for re-driving compensation. Verified on the wave-308
tree (018887f1) through the public API: a composed saga whose action
fails and whose compensation fails transiently 3x escalates; after the
downstream is "fixed", `retry_compensation()` raises misleading
`workflow-saga-compensation-unauthorized` ("authority
'composed-auth:<nonce>:...' revoked or unknown at compensation time"
-- nothing was revoked; the verifier was removed), the fixed
compensation is never invoked (0 calls), and the saga stays
escalated. `abort_and_compensate_all` fails identically. Even if the
operator re-installs a verifier for the nonce-scoped ref, the next
layer fails: the comp op name is unresolvable ("not registered in
this process") and the saga re-escalates. The only working resolution
is `accept_manual_remediation` (attestation without re-running) --
the re-drive actions, the point of F384, are dead for composed sagas.
This limitation is documented nowhere in `gov/workflow_composed.py`.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Availability of recovery, fail-closed
(the saga stays safely escalated; the refusals are loud and coded),
but the documented operator intervention cannot be performed through
the module for composed sagas, and the first error the operator sees
is actively misleading (misdiagnosis as a verifier-config problem).

**Close-when criteria:** (1) `retry_compensation()` (and
`abort_and_compensate_all`) re-drive the failed compensation for an
escalated COMPOSED saga after the underlying cause is fixed -- e.g.
the composer retains/re-registers the wrapper ops and step verifiers
until the saga reaches a terminal compensated state, or the composer
exposes an operator-retry API that re-establishes them; (2) the
misleading `workflow-saga-compensation-unauthorized` on operator
retry of a composed saga is gone; (3) the F394 probes flip to HELD
(compensation re-invoked, saga compensated); (4) adjacent batteries
stay green.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-03, wave-310 lane A.**

## F393: composed idempotency identity (op_digest) does not bind the unit's code -- a descriptor-identical plan with a different fn/saga-action poisons another plan's replay under the same run (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-308 independent red-team (this lane), claim 2026-10-03T11:19:50Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w308_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`F393-fn-code-confusion`, `F393-saga-code-confusion`); wave-309 independent red-team adds the slip-leg variant as supporting evidence
(`evals/w309_redteam_probes.py`, probe `F393-slip-code-confusion` --
descriptor-identical slip plans differing only in leg_fns yield
identical digests; the victim's leg replays the attacker's outputs).

**Defect:** the F392 closure binds the replayed step to the exact
idempotency record via the (namespace, op_class, key) triple -- but the
record's own identity, the op_digest, does not bind the code that
executed. `ComposedPlan.digest` covers kind/name/idem_key/inputs_digest
and `_fn_op_digest` covers plan/op/unit/inputs digests; the `fn`
callable (or saga `action_fns`) is deliberately excluded (not
JSON-able). Under the F388/F392 threat model (attacker as the
legitimate plan actor), the attacker executes a descriptor-identical
plan -- same kind, name, idem_key, inputs -- with an evil fn under the
same run. The evil op_digest is bit-identical to the victim's, so the
victim's `_begin_unit` returns REPLAY on the attacker's record and
`_resolve_replay` passes every check: run, record-caller, digest, F390
step name, and the F392 idempotency binding (same namespace/op_class/
key). The victim's fn never executes; the attacker's outputs return as
native. Verified on the wave-307 tree (57068df1) through the public
API on the fn path (victim outputs `{"evil": 1}`, victim fn never ran)
and the saga action path (victim saga "succeeded" with the attacker's
step outputs, victim action never ran). This refutes the F392 residual
claim that "the binding now makes plan-sharing a run safe at the replay
seam": plan-sharing is still unsafe when descriptors collide.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) executing a plan whose digest differs from
the first plan executed under a run refuses coded -- the run binds to
the first plan digest, so crash-recovery re-execution of the SAME plan
still replays while a different (even descriptor-identical) plan cannot
share the run; or, equivalently, the op identity binds the executed
code; (2) the F393 probes flip to HELD (descriptor-identical evil plan
refused; legitimate same-plan re-execution still replays); (3)
adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-03, wave-309 lane A.** Both close-when
directions implemented (the "(even descriptor-identical)" parenthetical
requires the digest to distinguish descriptor-identical plans):
(1) `ComposedPlan.digest` now includes a per-unit `code_digest` --
a fingerprint of the fn's code object (bytecode, constants incl. nested
code objects, names, argcounts, flags; line numbers/filenames excluded
so crash-recovery rebuilds keep the digest) plus JSON-native closed-over
values bound by value. Callables without `__code__` (builtins,
functools.partial) refuse `workflow-composed-definition-invalid` at
plan construction (fail closed). (2) `WorkflowStore.bind_plan_digest`
records the first plan digest executed under a run (journal-appended as
a `"run_plan"` record, surviving crash-recovery/store reload);
`WorkflowComposer.execute()` refuses coded
`workflow-composed-plan-mismatch` on a different digest. A refused
execute never clobbers the binding; same-plan re-execution still
replays. Red-first: both filed probes reproduced BREAK on pristine
018887f1 (victim fn/action never executed, attacker outputs returned
as native). Green: the filed attack shapes now refuse coded
workflow-composed-plan-mismatch at the run->plan gate (victim fn/action
never runs); descriptor-identical plans have different digests;
crash-recovery replays with exactly 1 fn call; binding survives journal
reload. Regression pins: `evals/w309_f393_probes.py` (8 closure probes),
`tests/test_workflow_f393.py` (9 unit tests); the w308 F393 probes now
assert the coded refusal. Adjacent batteries green (w308 0/23/0, w307
step-collision 0/9/0, w303_f390 0/8/0, w303_f388 0/9/0, w306 0/22/0,
w307 redteam 0/27/0, w307 saga-signal 0/8/0). +1 decision code
(workflow-composed-plan-mismatch); pin 1828 -> 1829. Documented
residuals: exotic (non-JSON-native) closure values bind by type name
only; the first plan digest is recorded even if execute later fails
mid-run (same-plan retry still correct); line numbers excluded from the
fingerprint (same-source rebuilds keep the digest).

## F392: composed _resolve_replay does not bind the ref's step to the exact idempotency record that created it -- a poisoned (digest, ref) pair naming a DIFFERENT plan's same-named step of the same run returns the wrong unit's outputs without executing (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-307 lane A (this lane), claim 2026-10-03T10:41:10Z, filed as F391, renumbered F391->F392 at the wave-307 merge per the wave-272 earliest-filed rule (lane E claimed F391 at 2026-10-03T10:37:32Z).
Standing regression pins: `evals/w307_step_collision_probes.py` (probes
`F392-same-run-same-name`, `F392-saga-action-binding`,
`F392-legit-replay-survives`, `F392-crash-replay-no-rerun`),
`tests/test_workflow_f392.py`.

**Defect:** `gov/workflow_composed.py::WorkflowComposer._resolve_replay`
(F390-hardened) binds the ref's step to the replaying unit by step NAME
(`expected_step_name`). But step names are unique per (plan, unit) --
not per run: `ComposedPlan.__init__` refuses duplicate unit names
within ONE plan, and `SagaDefinition._validate` refuses duplicate
step_ids within one definition, but `execute()` takes a
caller-provided run_id and never binds a run to a single plan (nor does
`WorkflowStore.start_run` bind a run to a plan). An attacker who begins
AND completes as the legitimate plan actor (the F388 threat model) can
(1) legitimately execute plan_evil = [fn "u2" -> {"evil": 1}, idem_key
"ke"] under run R, recording "fn:u2" at seq 1; (2) plant under the
victim's key "k2" a record with the exact op_digest, the real digest of
the evil step, `ref = "wfstep:R:1"`; (3) the victim's plan_victim = [fn
"u2" -> {"real": 2}, idem_key "k2"] executed under run R then replays:
every F388 check passes (run matches, caller matches, step completed,
digest matches) AND the F390 name check passes ("fn:u2" == "fn:u2"),
returning `{"evil": 1}` without the victim fn ever executing. Verified
on the pristine wave-306 base (f6248a18) through the public API
(evals/w307_step_collision_probes.py A1 BREAKs on pristine, HELDs on
the fixed tree; the same defect class through the saga action path --
A2 -- BREAKs on pristine and HELDs on the fixed tree, where the coded
refusal surfaces as a compensated saga). Reusing the victim's idem_key
instead of planting under a fresh key fails closed already at `begin`
(loud `IdempotencyConflict` on same-key different-digest), so the plant
is the viable vector. Cross-kind collisions are impossible (step-name
prefixes `fn:`/`saga:`/`saga-comp:`/`slip:` are kind-distinct); the
residual is same-kind across plans under one run.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) every composed unit's workflow step
records the (namespace, op_class, key) triple of the idempotency record
that created it as its `idempotency_key` (via `_step_binding`, NUL-
separated so a ":" inside a key cannot blur fields); (2)
`_resolve_replay` (new required `key` param, fail-closed by
construction) refuses coded `workflow-composed-replay-foreign` when the
resolved step's binding does not match the replaying record's key;
(3) the F392 probes flip to HELD; (4) legitimate replay still works
(same plan re-executed under the same run replays its own outputs;
crash-before-complete replays via the binding with no duplicate
execution); (5) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED** (filed and closed 2026-10-03, wave-307 lane A:
idempotency-record binding in `_resolve_replay`; no new decision
codes, reuses `workflow-composed-replay-foreign`; pin unchanged 1827).

## F391: workflow_branch suspend_lease/resume_lease take the lease manager as a caller-supplied argument -- the F389 suspend-time holdership proof (check_write before parking) is vacuous against an attacker who brings their own rubber-stamp manager (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-307 independent red-team (this lane), claim 2026-10-03T10:37:32Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w307_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`F391-fake-manager-clobber`, `F391-fake-manager-resume`).

**Defect:** `gov/workflow_branch.py::suspend_lease` (F389 closure) proves
lease-holdership at suspend time by calling
`lease_manager.check_write(scope, fencing_token, holder_id,
checked_at=suspended_at)` BEFORE parking -- but `lease_manager` is a
caller-supplied parameter. An attacker who knows only the xid (the F389
threat model: "anyone who knows the xid") passes a fake manager whose
`check_write` is a no-op rubber stamp: the re-park is ACCEPTED, the
legitimate holder's parked suspension is clobbered, and the holder's
subsequent `resume_lease` refuses `workflow-branch-xid-mismatch` -- the
exact F389 availability impact, unclosed. Worse, the attacker's own
`resume_lease(attacker_record, fake_manager)` returns True: the F385
exact-parked-record match passes (the attacker parked it themselves) and
the resume-time liveness `check_write` is answered by the attacker's own
oracle -- a fake liveness attestation the coordinator believes. The
wave-305 probe's assumption ("the attacker cannot complete the resume
themselves -- check_write still gates on the fencing token") holds only
when the manager is the real one; nothing binds the manager. Verified on
the wave-306 tree (f6248a18) through the public API: (1) holder-1
acquires a real lease and parks via `suspend_lease` with the real
manager; (2) attacker calls `suspend_lease(xid, FakeManager(),
"scope-x", 999999, "mallory", ...)` -- accepted; (3) holder's
`resume_lease` with the real manager refuses
`workflow-branch-xid-mismatch`; (4) attacker's
`resume_lease(evil_record, FakeManager(), ...)` returns True. The F389
closure is overstated: the holdership proof verifies "the
caller-supplied oracle accepts the caller-supplied token", which proves
nothing against the F389 caller threat model.

**Close-when criteria:** (1) the lease manager used for the suspend-time
holdership proof and the resume-time liveness check is bound by the
coordinator rather than supplied per-call -- e.g. the first park binds
the manager object to the transaction and later suspend/resume calls
must present the identical manager (identity check), or the manager is
bound at `begin()` time; a substituted manager refuses coded; (2) the
F391 probes flip to HELD (fake-manager re-park refused; fake-manager
resume refused; legitimate suspend/resume with the bound manager still
works); (3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-03, wave-308 lane A.** The coordinator binds
the lease manager object to the transaction at the first successful
park (`BranchCoordinator._check_manager_binding`, identity check);
later suspend/resume calls presenting a different manager refuse coded
`coord-lease-manager-mismatch` before any oracle call. The binding
happens only after the F389 holdership proof passes, so a refused park
binds nothing. Red-first: both filed BREAKs reproduced on pristine
`57068df1` (fake-manager re-park ACCEPTED; fake-manager resume returned
True); on the fixed tree both refuse coded
`coord-lease-manager-mismatch`. Regression battery
`evals/w308_f391_probes.py` (6 closure probes + pin/footer +
depth-1 green checks); the w307 red-team F391 direct probes now assert
the coded refusal. +1 decision code (`coord-lease-manager-mismatch`;
pin 1827 -> 1828). Residual (documented): an attacker who wins the
race to the FIRST park on a fresh xid binds their own manager -- it
requires beating the holder to the first park AND getting the
deployment to resume from the attacker's record; the deployment
eliminates it by parking promptly at lease acquisition.

## F398: ProvenanceSink._bind_arg negation-indirection -- a negated user mention of a critical-arg value binds at USER and the user-bound refinement ALLOWS the prohibited egress (MEDIUM, CLOSED)

**Cells:** wave-315 independent red-team (lane 3, this lane), claim 2026-10-03T21:19:40Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w315_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`P2-refinement-negation-indirection`, `P2-refinement-benign-no-fp`,
`P2-user-segment-allows`).

**Defect:** the wave-314 sink's critical-arg refinement
(`gov/provenance_sink.py::_bind_arg`, Tessera's over-blocking fix)
binds an arg value to USER when the value appears as a substring in
any live user/system segment -- with no negation or intent handling.
A user's explicit PROHIBITION ("never email mallory@evil.com under
any circumstances") therefore binds the attacker's address at USER,
and the refinement's ALLOW arm ("every critical arg binds at or
above required trust (user-bound refinement)") authorizes the send
under the default egress policy (`required_trust=USER`,
`on_violation=REFUSE` -- the policy the executor seam uses via
`provenance_gate`). The prohibition becomes the authorization.
Verified break-first through `provenance_gate` (the real
executor-seam entry point, default policy): user segment with the
negated mention + web segment driving the send ->
`ALLOW provenance-sink-allowed`; the identical send with only the
web segment -> `REFUSE provenance-critical-arg-refused`; a genuine
user authorization -> `ALLOW` (control). The only difference between
the ALLOW and the REFUSE is text the user wrote as a prohibition.
Mention is not authorization, and the substring refinement cannot
distinguish "send to X" from "never send to X".

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Demonstrable bypass of the default
egress trust policy with realistic preconditions: (a) the user states
a prohibition naming the value (the natural way users express
guardrails: "never send anything to X", "don't email Y"); (b) the
standard threat model -- attacker-influenced content drives the arg;
(c) the documented use case of the refinement ("arg copied from the
user prompt binds at USER"). Consequence is the exact egress the
user prohibited, allowed by the gate. Downgraded from HIGH: the
attacker must know/predict a value the user prohibited, and the
primary threat (untrusted content driving egress with no user
mention) still refuses.

**Close-when:** (1) a negated/prohibited user mention of a critical-arg
value does not satisfy `required_trust=USER` via the refinement --
e.g. the binding discounts matches inside negation scope, or the
refinement requires an affirmative authorization signal rather than
mere mention; (2) the benign controls still hold (genuine user
authorization ALLOWS; affirmative user-supplied args still bind at
USER -- no over-blocking regression); (3) adjacent batteries stay
green.

**CLOSED 2026-10-03** (wave-316 lane 1: F398 closure, `to-spec` ->
TDD red-before-green at the `check()`/`provenance_gate()` seams).
`gov/provenance_sink.py` gains deterministic negation scoping for the
critical-arg refinement: `_affirmative_mention(content, text)` judges
each occurrence of the arg value in its own clause; a clause is
negated iff it carries a negation-cue token (the `never`/`not`/`n't`
family, `without`, and the prohibition verbs
refuse/prohibit/forbid/block/avoid/exclude/disallow/stop/deny/reject/halt).
Clause boundaries are sentence terminators, a period followed by
whitespace (so `mallory@evil.com` is never torn apart), and the
contrastive conjunctions but/however/yet/although/though (per-mention:
"you may email X but never cc Y" binds X, not Y). `_bind_arg` now
requires an affirmative mention in BOTH precedence rules -- a negated
occurrence contributes no trust anywhere, so a negated-only mention
falls through to the context min, never to USER via that mention. No
new decision codes: the F398 scenario now refuses with the existing
coded `provenance-critical-arg-refused` (the value binds at TOOL from
the attacker segment, below required USER). Refusal reasons stay
generic (no content). stdlib `re` only; no LLM, no new crypto.
Close-when evidence: (1) the break-first probe
`P2-refinement-negation-indirection` BREAKs on the open tree (negated
mention + attacker send -> `ALLOW`) and, re-pinned per the wave-306
lesson, asserts `REFUSE provenance-critical-arg-refused` on the
closed tree (HELD); a sensitivity neuter (`_clause_negated` ->
`False`) re-BREAKs it, proving the check is load-bearing; (2) benign
controls hold -- `P2-refinement-benign-no-fp` and
`P2-user-segment-allows` HELD, plus 7 new `NegationTests` unit tests
(affirmative still ALLOWS, per-mention contrast, contraction
negation, email-period clause integrity, contrastive affirmation,
double-negation fail-closed) -- `tests/test_provenance_sink.py` 42/42;
(3) adjacent green -- `w315_redteam` 1 BREAK / 38 HELD / 0 ERROR (the
remaining BREAK is the still-OPEN F399 probe), `w314_provsink`
0/23/0, `w315_vsa` 20/20, `w280_redteam` 0/24/0, `w313_f397` 0/14/0,
`w314_rekor` 0/15/0, the 4 sink-adjacent unit suites
(test_witness_rekor, test_approval_tokens, test_plan_policy,
test_trajectory_risk) OK, and the HMAC chokepoint audit OK. Pin
unchanged 1888 (no new codes). Deliberate residual: the cue list is a
conservative floor -- evasion-shaped phrasings outside the vocabulary
(e.g. "email X is off the table") are not recognized as negated and
fall to the context min, never to USER; cross-sentence anaphora
("Never email X. Actually, go ahead") is out of scope and fails
closed.

## F399: provenance_gate constructs a fresh ProvenanceSink per call -- the REPLAN_BUDGET escalate-terminal ratchet, quarantine set, and consumed-declassification set are dead state at the executor seam (LOW, CLOSED 2026-10-03 wave-316 lane 1)

**Cells:** wave-315 independent red-team (lane 3, this lane), claim 2026-10-03T21:21:00Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w315_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`P2-fresh-sink-per-call-defeats-budget`, `P2-replan-budget-terminal`,
`P2-budget-reset-fresh-context`).

**Defect:** `provenance_gate()` (`gov/provenance_sink.py:606`) is the
executor seam's only entry point (`gov/executor.py:13058`, called per
approved record), and it constructs a fresh `ProvenanceSink()` on
every call. The sink's cross-call state -- `_refusals` (driving the
`REPLAN_BUDGET=3` escalate-terminal ratchet), `_quarantined`, and
`_consumed` (single-use declassification) -- is therefore discarded
after every call. Verified break-first: 6 consecutive same-context
critical-arg refusals through `provenance_gate` never reach
escalate-terminal (all six return
`provenance-critical-arg-refused`); a single stateful
`ProvenanceSink` under the same sequence escalates terminal at the
4th refusal (control -- the ratchet works when the instance is
reused). The class docstring advertises the bounded re-plan
guarantee; the wiring defeats it. Each individual call still refuses
fail-closed -- what is lost is the pressure ratchet (an agent can
retry refused actions indefinitely without terminal escalation) and
the quarantine/consumed sets at this seam.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. No unsafe execution results -- every
refused call still refuses; the loss is the liveness/pressure
property (bounded re-plan) and cross-call quarantine/consumed
bookkeeping at the executor seam, not a bypass.

**Close-when:** (1) the executor seam reuses one sink per unit of
re-plan context (or `provenance_gate` accepts an injected sink), so
repeated refusals in one context escalate terminal at the
documented budget and quarantine/consumed sets persist across calls
in that context; (2) per-context isolation is preserved (fresh
context still resets the budget -- no cross-context bleed);
(3) adjacent batteries stay green.

**CLOSED 2026-10-03** (wave-316 lane 2: `provenance_gate` accepts an
injected `sink`; the executor owns one run-scoped `ProvenanceSink`
(`Executor._pv_sink`, lazily created at the first gated call, shared
by reference with spawned children so a spawn cannot dodge the
ratchet) and passes it at the sweep seam; per-context isolation is
preserved by the sink's `ctx_key` (tool + influencing segment ids);
the sink is dropped with the executor at run end. Break-first
evidence: 6 same-context refusals through the gate with a retained
sink escalate terminal at the 4th (`provenance-quarantine-terminal`);
harness executor-seam tests
(`tests/test_provenance_sink.py::SweepIntegrationTests::test_seam_reuses_one_sink_across_records`)
show the 4th same-context refused record carrying the terminal code,
and `test_seam_per_context_isolation` shows no cross-context bleed;
`evals/w315_redteam_probes.py` probe `P2-sink-per-seam-context` HELD
(it was BREAK as `P2-fresh-sink-per-call-defeats-budget` on the open
tree); `P2-budget-reset-fresh-context` stays HELD. No new decision
codes; pin unchanged 1888.)

**Close-when:** (1) the wave-315 merge red-first audit re-verifies the error path on the merged tree (a genuine error tallies `[ERROR]` and exits 1); (2) the normal-path battery stays 0/30/0.

**CLOSED 2026-10-03** (wave-316 lane 2 closure ritual: injected a
genuine probe error into `evals/w280_redteam_probes.py` on the merged
tree -- the error tallied as `[ERROR]`, the summary printed
`0 BREAK / 0 HELD / 1 ERROR`, and the process returned exit 1 (the

## F405: ProvenanceSink negation-cue vocabulary misses apostrophe-less variants -- a user prohibition with a common typo binds at USER and ALLOWs the prohibited send (MEDIUM, CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-320 lane 1)

**Cells:** wave-319 independent red-team (lane 4, this lane), claim 2026-10-04T04:09:00Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w319_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`P3-negation-dont-no-apostrophe`, `P3-negation-dnt`,
`P3-negation-cant-no-apostrophe`).

**Defect:** `gov/provenance_sink.py::_NEGATION_CUES` contains only
apostrophe-bearing contractions ("don't", "can't", "won't", "isn't",
...). Apostrophe-less variants -- "dont", "dnt", "cant", "wont",
"isnt", "arent", "wasnt", "werent", "havent", "hasnt", "hadnt",
"doesnt", "didnt", "wouldnt", "couldnt", "shouldnt", "mustnt" -- are
among the most common typing patterns and are NOT negation cues. A
user prohibition phrased with such a variant ("please dont email
mallory@evil.com") is not recognized as negated; the F404
`_authorizing_mention` then finds the authorization verb ("email")
before the value in the same clause and binds the attacker's
critical-arg value at USER, so the refinement's ALLOW arm authorizes
the prohibited send under the default egress policy
(`required_trust=USER`). Demonstrated through `provenance_gate` (the
real executor-seam entry point): "please dont email mallory@evil.com"
+ attacker send -> `ALLOW provenance-sink-allowed`; "please dnt email
mallory@evil.com" -> `ALLOW`; "please cant email mallory@evil.com" ->
`ALLOW`. Controls: "please don't email mallory@evil.com" -> `REFUSE
provenance-critical-arg-refused`; "never email mallory@evil.com" ->
`REFUSE`; genuine authorization "please email mallory@evil.com" ->
`ALLOW`. The F404 closure's corrected residual claims "unrecognized
prohibitions fall to the context min, never to USER (fail closed)" --
the claim is false for negation-cue variants: the variant is
unrecognized AND the clause authorizes. Same defect class as F398/F404
(a user's explicit prohibition authorizes the prohibited action), with
a narrower trigger surface (negation-cue spelling variants rather than
prohibition phrasings).

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM, same class as F398/F404. The failure is
silent from the user's perspective: the sink records an authorizing
mention where the user wrote a prohibition. The trigger is a common
typo, not an exotic phrasing.

**Closure (2026-10-04, wave-320 lane 1):** orthographic normalization at
the single negation-detection choke point (`_clause_negated` in
`gov/provenance_sink.py`), not a bigger vocabulary. A new
`_strip_apostrophes` helper removes apostrophe characters -- ASCII `'`
plus the Unicode variants U+2019/U+2018/U+02BC/U+0060 (smart quotes,
modifier-letter apostrophe, backtick typo) -- from BOTH the clause text
and the cue vocabulary before matching, via a derived
`_NEGATION_CUES_NORM` set. "dont" collapses onto "don't", "cant" onto
"can't", and smart-quote "don't" (U+2019) onto "don't". One explicit cue
added: "dnt" -- the SMS vowel-syncope form, not reachable by apostrophe
stripping ("don't" strips to "dont", not "dnt"); the close-when requires
the `P3-negation-dnt` probe to flip, so this single-word surgical addition
is the minimal honest fix (deviation from the lane brief's "no new cue
words" direction, recorded in the lane SPEC.md). Break-first red loop:
"please dont email mallory@evil.com", "please dnt email mallory@evil.com",
"you cant email mallory@evil.com the report", and "please don\u2019t email
mallory@evil.com" all ALLOWed on the open tree and now REFUSE coded
`provenance-critical-arg-refused` on the closed tree; all 17
apostrophe-omission variants from the defect refuse. Benign controls hold:
"please don't email mallory@evil.com" and "never email mallory@evil.com"
still refuse; genuine "please email mallory@evil.com" still ALLOWs; all 63
`test_provenance_sink` unit tests pass (56 existing + 7 new
F405ApostropheNormalizationTests); w319_redteam 0/24/0 (three P3 probes
flipped BREAK->HELD, two new Unicode/boundary probes HELD); w317_redteam
0/38/0 (F404 probes stay HELD). No new decision codes; pin unchanged 1933.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w319_redteam_probes.py` P3 (three F405
probes now assert the coded refusal HELD; two new probes:
P3-negation-unicode-apostrophe, P3-negation-normalization-boundary) and
`tests/test_provenance_sink.py::F405ApostropheNormalizationTests`.
**Corrected residual (replaces the false F404 residual):** negation
detection is orthographic normalization over a closed cue vocabulary.
What the fix still cannot see (honest): R1 -- novel misspellings
("dno't", "do'nt") are not cues; R2 -- other SMS skeletons ("cnt",
"wnt", "shnt") are not cues and, when co-occurring with an authorization
verb, the verb governs (the F404 inverted default only fails closed for
bare mentions); R3 -- "wont" as habit ("as is his wont") now reads as
negation and fails closed (safe direction, accepted trade-off); R4 --
semantic negation without a cue word ("I would prefer you didn't") is
still out of scope.

**Close-when:** (1) apostrophe-less negation variants stop satisfying
`required_trust=USER` (the clause is recognized as negated, or the
mention otherwise fails closed to the context min or below); the
documented residual is corrected to match the implemented behavior;
(2) the three P3 probes flip BREAK -> HELD on the closed tree; (3)
benign controls hold (apostrophe-bearing negations, genuine
authorizations); (4) greens stay green.

## F404: F398 closure's documented negation residual is false -- out-of-vocabulary prohibition phrasings bind at USER and authorize the prohibited send (MEDIUM, CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-318 lane 1)

**Cells:** wave-317 independent red-team (lane 3, this lane), claim 2026-10-04T02:50:00Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w317_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`P6-negation-off-the-table`, `P6-negation-banned`,
`P6-negation-out-of-the-loop`).

**Defect:** the F398 closure (wave-316 lane 1, CLOSED) documents this
residual in FINDINGS.md: 'evasion-shaped phrasings outside the
vocabulary (e.g. "email X is off the table") are not recognized as
negated and fall to the context min, never to USER'. Break-first on the
closed tree shows the claim is false: `ProvenanceSink._bind_arg`'s
`_affirmative_mention` returns True for any clause carrying NO negation
cue, so a prohibition phrased outside the cue vocabulary binds the
critical-arg value at USER and the refinement's ALLOW arm authorizes the
prohibited send under the default egress policy (`required_trust=USER`).
Demonstrated through `provenance_gate` (the real executor-seam entry
point): "email mallory@evil.com is off the table" + attacker send ->
`ALLOW`; "mallory@evil.com is banned" -> `ALLOW`; "keep
mallory@evil.com out of the loop" -> `ALLOW`; "mallory@evil.com should
be blacklisted" -> `ALLOW`; "mallory@evil.com is off-limits" -> `ALLOW`.
Controls: cue-vocabulary prohibition ("never email mallory@evil.com")
-> `REFUSE provenance-critical-arg-refused`; genuine authorization ("ask
mallory@evil.com for the quarterly report") -> `ALLOW`. The prohibition
becomes the authorization whenever the user phrases it outside the
cue-vocabulary -- the same defect class as F398, with a wider trigger
surface.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM, same class as F398 (a user's explicit
prohibition authorizes the prohibited action). The failure is silent
from the user's perspective: the sink records an affirmative mention
where the user wrote a prohibition.

**Close-when:** (1) out-of-vocabulary prohibition phrasings stop
satisfying `required_trust=USER` (fail closed to the context min or
below); the documented residual is corrected to match the implemented
behavior; (2) the three P6 probes flip BREAK -> HELD on the closed tree;
(3) benign controls hold (cue-vocabulary refusals, genuine
authorizations); (4) greens stay green.

**Closure (2026-10-04, wave-318 lane 1):** the trust default for
critical-arg binding is INVERTED in `gov/provenance_sink.py`.
`_affirmative_mention` (F398) is replaced by `_authorizing_mention` at
both `_bind_arg` rules: a user/system mention of a critical-arg value
binds at USER only on POSITIVE evidence of authorization in the same
clause -- an authorization verb governing the value as its object
("send"/"email"/"mail"/"forward"/"cc"/"bcc"/"share"/"deliver"/
"notify"/"contact"/"ask"/"tell"/"message"/"ping"/"write"/"dispatch"/
"distribute"/"circulate"/"relay"/"transmit", base forms), or a positive
predicate ("X is fine/ok/okay/approved/authorized/acceptable/good/
allowed/permitted"). A negated clause still authorizes nothing (F398
preserved, checked first). A value that opens a copular/descriptive
construction ("X is ...", "X should be ...") is the SUBJECT of a
statement about it, not the object of an authorization, and does not
bind -- this is what defeats "email mallory@evil.com is off the table"
(the naive verb-presence inversion would still ALLOW it, since the
clause contains "email"). Bare mentions, descriptive statements, past-
tense descriptions ("X emailed me"), and unrecognized prohibitions fall
to the context min, never to USER (fail closed). Break-first red loop:
the five F404 phrasings ALLOWed on the open tree and now REFUSE coded
`provenance-critical-arg-refused` on the closed tree; unseen idioms
("emailing X is a no-go", "X stays out of this") also refuse -- the fix
is the inverted default, not a bigger vocabulary. Benign controls hold:
"please mail the report to t@local", "send the summary to bob@corp.com",
"ask mallory@evil.com for the quarterly report", "you may email X but
never cc Y" (X binds, Y does not), "don't send to X, but Y is fine"
(positive predicate binds), modal requests ("can you forward ... to X")
all ALLOW; all seven F398 NegationTests still pass (44/44 module tests,
56/56 with the 12 new F404 AuthorizationDefaultTests). No new decision
codes; pin unchanged 1900. Standing regression pins:
`evals/w317_redteam_probes.py` P6 (three F404 probes now assert the coded
refusal HELD; three new P6f boundary probes: affirmative ALLOWS, bare
mention REFUSEs, authorization+negation fails closed) and
`tests/test_provenance_sink.py::AuthorizationDefaultTests`.
**Corrected residual (replaces the false F398 residual):** binding now
requires positive authorization evidence; unknown phrasings refuse. What
the fix still cannot see (honest): R1 -- the authorization-verb
vocabulary is finite (unlisted verbs fail closed, loud not silent); R2 --
"X is perfectly fine" (adverb between copula and predicate) fails
closed; R3 -- gerund/informal forms ("cc'ing X") are not recognized;
R4 -- pronoun indirection ("send it to her") is not resolved, the value
must literally occur as the authorized object; R5 -- the descriptive
test keys on the word immediately following the value; R6 --
non-English phrasings remain out of scope for this deterministic layer
(same standing boundary as F398).

## F406: ProvenanceSink negation-cue vocabulary misses orthographic near-misses -- a user prohibition with a transposed-letter or vowel-syncope typo binds at USER and ALLOWs the prohibited send (MEDIUM, CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-322 lane 1)

**Cells:** wave-321 independent red-team (lane 3, this lane), claim 2026-10-04T06:22:00Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w321_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`P3-near-miss-dnot-transposed`, `P3-near-miss-odnt-transposed`,
`P3-near-miss-cannt-doubled`, `P3-near-miss-cnt-syncope`,
`P3-near-miss-wnt-syncope`).

**Defect:** the F405 closure normalized apostrophes at the
`_clause_negated` choke point (`gov/provenance_sink.py`), so a variant
is recognized as negation only if it collapses onto the closed
`_NEGATION_CUES` list after apostrophe-stripping. Single-edit
near-misses that do NOT collapse -- transposed letters ("dno't" ->
"dnot", "odn't" -> "odnt", "d'not" -> "dnot"), doubled letters
("cann't" -> "cannt", "shoudn't" -> "shoudnt"), and vowel syncopes
beyond the single explicit "dnt" cue ("cnt", "wnt", "shdnt") -- are not
negation cues. A user prohibition phrased with such a near-miss
("please dno't email mallory@evil.com") is not detected as negated;
the F404 `_authorizing_mention` finds "email" before the value, binds
the critical value at USER, and the prohibited send ALLOWs end-to-end
(`provenance-sink-allowed`). Same harm as F398/F404/F405. This
promotes the F405 residuals R1/R2 prose to a tracked finding, with one
correction to that prose: R1 claimed "do'nt" is uncovered -- it IS
covered (apostrophe-stripping collapses it onto "dont" and it refuses
coded `provenance-critical-arg-refused`).

**Close-when:** (1) the five standing probes refuse coded
`provenance-critical-arg-refused` on the closed tree; (2) benign
controls hold -- "please email mallory@evil.com" still ALLOWs, and
"please don't email mallory@evil.com" / "please do'nt email
mallory@evil.com" still refuse; (3) no new decision codes (the refusal
reuses `provenance-critical-arg-refused`); pin unchanged 1946.

**Residuals / explicit non-goals:** semantic negation without a cue
word (F405 R4) remains out of scope; any edit-tolerant fix must not
widen the vocabulary's meaning -- the R3 "wont"-as-habit fail-closed
trade-off stands.

**Closure (2026-10-04, wave-322 lane 1):** bounded orthographic-nearness
rule at the same `_clause_negated` choke point (`gov/provenance_sink.py`).
A token is a near-miss cue iff it is at insert/delete/transpose-only edit
distance exactly 1 from a normalized contraction cue (`dont doesnt didnt
cant wont shouldnt wouldnt couldnt mustnt isnt arent wasnt werent havent
hasnt hadnt cannot dnt`), excluding the anti-negation modals `want`
(d1 from `wasnt`) and `can` (d1 from `cant`) -- treating them as negation
would invert the language's canonical authorization phrasings. Substitution
is excluded by design (the finding's typo classes are
transpose/double/syncope; admitting substitution is where `want`~`wont`
lives). The near-miss set (3013 strings) is precomputed at import;
per-clause matching stays O(tokens) set membership, exactly like the
exact-cue path; the cue list's closed
semantics are unchanged. All five standing probes refuse coded
`provenance-critical-arg-refused`; benign controls hold (`please email
mallory@evil.com` ALLOWs, `please don't ...` / `please do'nt ...` refuse,
`I want/can to email ...` ALLOW). No new decision codes; pin unchanged
1964 (the close-when's "1946" was written pre-wave-321-merge -- the
invariant is "no new codes"). Residuals: substitution typos (`dond` for
`dont`) not caught; known fail-closed collisions documented at the
`_NEAR_MISS_CUES_NORM` definition in `gov/provenance_sink.py` (`don` as
name Don, `won`, `ant`, `cat`,
`dot`, `rent`, `dent`, `cannon`) -- each refuses a genuine send rather
than allowing a prohibited one, the safe direction (F404/F405
precedent); multi-edit misspellings are the next ceiling.

## F407: OCI referrers discovery crashes uncoded on malformed registry JSON -- a 200 response with a non-object body escapes as AttributeError/TypeError instead of a coded oci-* refusal (LOW, CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-323 lane 1)

**Cells:** wave-322 independent red-team (lane 4), claim 2026-10-04T07:14:14Z.
Standing regression pins: `evals/w322_redteam_probes.py` (probes
`P2-malformed-referrers-array`, `P2-malformed-referrers-string`,
`P2-malformed-referrers-subject`, `P2-malformed-entry-digest`,
`P2-malformed-referrers-null`).

**Close-when (met 2026-10-04, wave-323 lane 1):**
(1) All five standing probes refuse coded with the new
`oci-referrers-malformed` code (domain `oci`, severity `low`) --
`w322_redteam` battery green with green checks enabled.
(2) `discover_referrers` validates the response shape BEFORE any field
is dereferenced: non-dict bodies (array/string/null), non-dict
`subject`, and present-but-non-string entry digests each refuse with
`oci-referrers-malformed`; no uncoded exception escapes
`discover_referrers` / `pull_and_verify` for any registry-controlled
bytes.
(3) Benign controls hold: `P2-happy-path` honest referrers/pull
roundtrip still works; subject-mismatch ignore semantics unchanged
(non-dict subject is now a refusal, falsy/absent subject still
ignored); entry filtering for missing/None digests and non-dict
entries unchanged (fail-closed, no new ACCEPT paths -- the registry
remains untrusted storage).

**Fix:** `gov/oci_distribution.py` `discover_referrers` -- shape gate
before dereference (array/string/null body -> refusal; `subject`
falsy-or-dict preserved, truthy non-dict -> refusal; entry digest
present-but-non-string -> refusal, missing/None -> filtered as
before). Spec-review hardening (same defect class, same close-when
clause): the tag-schema fallback refuses coded on a non-list tag
document, and `parse_manifest` validates digest fields are strings
before the regex sees them (non-string subject/layer digests refuse
coded `oci-manifest-malformed` instead of raising TypeError). +1 code
(`oci-referrers-malformed`), pin 1976 -> 1977.

**Defect:** `OCIRegistryClient.discover_referrers` (`gov/oci_distribution.py`)
parses the referrers endpoint body with `json.loads` inside try/except but
dereferences the result OUTSIDE it: a 200 response whose body is a JSON
array (`["not","an","object"]`), a JSON string (`"just a string"`), or an
object with a non-dict `subject` (`{"subject": "not-a-dict"}`) raises an
uncaught `AttributeError` on `.get`; a referrers entry whose `digest` is a
truthy non-string (`{"digest": 12345}`) raises an uncaught `TypeError` from
the regex match. Both escape `pull_and_verify` (verified end-to-end) as
uncoded exceptions instead of a coded `OCIRefusal`. The module's contract
is explicit -- "Refusals are policy/integrity violations, never a silent
None", and every trust verdict on the untrusted-registry path is coded.
Fail-closed (no wrong evidence is ever returned; the caller sees an
exception), so availability-only: a malicious registry can already 404,
but the uncoded crash breaks callers that catch only `OCIRefusal` /
`OCIError` and violates the coded-refusal taxonomy. Same class as the
F371 precedent (uncoded crash on untrusted input), lower harm (no
integrity impact).

**Close-when:** (1) the four standing probes refuse coded (a new
`oci-referrers-malformed` code or the existing `oci-referrers-unavailable`
/ `oci-manifest-malformed`, at the fixer's choice -- the taxonomy, not
the probe, decides); (2) no uncoded exception escapes
`discover_referrers` / `pull_and_verify` for any registry-controlled
bytes (array/string/null bodies, non-dict subject, non-string digests);
(3) benign controls hold -- honest referrers/pull roundtrip still works
(`P2-happy-path`).


## F408: monitor state deleted mid-outage silently re-baselines the wrapper's failure count (MEDIUM, CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-324 lane 1)

**Cells:** wave-324 independent re-verification (spec re-check of lane 1), claim 2026-10-04T09:31:33Z.

Deleting the monitor state file mid-outage when the alert-state mirror has no head (monitor never healthy -- e.g. perpetual fetch failures) silently re-baselined the outage counter: the monitor treats a missing state file + `last_seen=None` as a first run, persists count 1, and refuses with `consecutive_failures=1`; the wrapper treated the exception-carried count as authoritative and overwrote its mirror (4 -> 1) with no alert. When the counter climbed back to 3, the re-fired alert id collided with the first outage's `witmon-alert/<id>/failure/i1/3` and the file sink's id-dedupe dropped it -- the operator never saw the re-alert. Same class as the spec-review Finding 1 (unknown/surprising counts alert LOUD, never silent); the lane's earlier fix guarded only the head-present case.

**Close-when (met 2026-10-04, wave-324 lane 1):**
(1) On the failure path, when the mirror is positive and the monitor-reported count is strictly less than the mirror, `run_monitor_once` alerts LOUD with `witness-alert-wrapper-error` and raises `AlertWrapperError` instead of overwriting the mirror (no legitimate flow has the monitor's count move backwards on the failure path: counts only increase there, and the healthy path is the only legitimate reset, which also resets the mirror).
(2) New standing probe `P17-monitor-state-deleted-no-head-loud` in `evals/w324_alert_probes.py`: 4 fetch failures, delete monitor state, next tick raises coded `witness-alert-wrapper-error` with exactly 1 wrapper-error alert and the mirror preserved at 4; battery 0 BREAK with green checks on.
(3) Benign controls hold -- P1/P2/P3/P4/P5 (threshold, every-run-while-down, recovery, crash-safety) unaffected; the two pre-run refuses (state-mismatch, policy-version-rollback) still report the pre-run count, which equals the mirror, so the `<` guard does not fire on them.


## F409: alert-state deletion during a healthy window reuses incident_seq, dropping the next outage's early failure alerts (LOW, CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-326 lane 1)

**Cells:** wave-325 independent red team (lane 4), claim 2026-10-04T10:20:00Z.

Deleting the alert-state file during a healthy window resets `incident_seq` to 1 for the next outage. The previous outage's 3rd-failure alert (`witmon-alert/<monitor>/failure/i1/3`) is already recorded in the alert sink, so when the new outage's counter reaches 3 the re-fired alert id is byte-identical and the sink's id-dedupe drops it silently. The outage still alerts from failures=4 on (i1/4, i1/5 are fresh ids), so this is delayed alerting -- never fully silent -- but the dedupe invariant ("a later outage's alerts never dedupe against an earlier outage's") is violated. Same class as F408 (alerting-state trust across incidents): the F408 fix guards monitor-state deletion and backwards counts, not alert-state loss between incidents. Related accepted boundary: deleting BOTH state files mid-outage re-baselines silently (the attacker who owns the wrapper's alert-state file can also delete the alert queue and suppress everything); deleting only the alert state mid-outage is noisy (count continues from the monitor's own state).

**Reproduction:** 3 fetch failures (alert i1/3 emitted) -> one healthy tick with a valid checkpoint -> delete `<dir>/alert_state.json` -> 3 more fetch failures: the tick with `consecutive_failures=3` emits no new alert record (sink count unchanged); ticks 4-5 alert as i1/4, i1/5. Standing probe `P1a-f409-alert-state-deleted-healthy-window` in `evals/w325_redteam_probes.py` (expected BREAK on the wave-324 tree).

**Close-when:** after alert-state loss, the next outage's failure alerts must not dedupe-collide with any earlier outage's alerts. Candidate fixes: (a) on a fresh alert state, scan the alert queue/file for this monitor_id's maximum emitted incident_seq and start above it; (b) bind the outage's first-failure timestamp into the alert id; (c) persist incident_seq outside the alert-state file. The standing P1a probe must flip to HELD, the full w325 battery must go 0 BREAK / 45 HELD / 0 ERROR, and the F408 guards (P1d/P1h/P4a) must stay HELD.

**Severity: LOW** -- requires local alert-state file deletion during a healthy window (an attacker with that write access can already delete the alert queue and suppress everything outright); impact is bounded delay (alerts resume once `consecutive_failures` exceeds the previous outage's maximum), never silence.

**Closure (wave-326 lane 1, 2026-10-04):** close-when candidate (b) implemented, plus LOUD loss detection. The outage's incident identity is now `(incident_seq, incident_first_failure_ts)`: the alert id is `witmon-alert/<monitor>/failure/i<seq>-<first_failure_ts>/<failures>`, with the timestamp bound at the healthy->failing transition and persisted before emit (crash-retry within an outage reuses the id, preserving the exactly-once dedupe). Two outages can share an `incident_seq` only if the alert state was lost between them, and then their first-failure timestamps differ -- so the next outage's alerts can never byte-collide with an earlier outage's. Additionally, a missing alert-state file against a monitor with prior history (head or nonzero failure count) emits a LOUD coded `witness-alert-state-lost` alert and continues with the timestamp-bound identity (fires once per loss; the fresh state is persisted by the normal paths). A missing alert state with no monitor history is still a silent fresh install; deleting BOTH state files stays the accepted silent re-baseline boundary (P1b). New code registered: `witness-alert-state-lost` (witness/medium); pin 2020 -> 2021. Verification: P1a flips to HELD ("new outage's 3rd-failure alert emitted"), w325 battery 0 BREAK / 50 HELD / 0 ERROR, w324 alert battery 0 BREAK / 20 HELD / 0 ERROR, F408 guards (P1d/P1h/P4a) stay HELD, 49/49 monitor_alert unit tests pass (7 new F409ClosureTests).


## F410 — LOW — Post-rotation timestamp bootstrap requires contiguous versions from v1; a pruned repository wedges the client permanently (Wave 326, CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-327 lane 2)

**Cells:** wave-326 TUF section-5 audit battery (`evals/w326_tufaudit_probes.py::T4c-post-rotation-pruned-v1-wedges`, `T4d-post-rotation-gap-wedges`), 2026-10-04. Filed by the wave-326 lane-4 audit.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-327 lane 2.**

**Closure:** close-when candidate (b) implemented in `gov/bundle_refresh.py::_bootstrap_timestamp_post_rotation` -- clean timestamp-slot misses no longer end the scan; the bootstrap tolerates a bounded run of `POST_ROTATION_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_MISSES = 32` consecutive clean misses instead of breaking on the first one. Transport failures still stop the scan immediately (unreliable view: keep the best version seen so far). The scan deliberately still starts at v1 rather than at the floor: candidate (a) (start at `max(1, floor)`) would skip the planted sub-floor slot and break the T4b probe, which the close-when requires to stay HELD -- a below-floor version that verifies under the new root remains a loud rollback refusal, and slots below the floor can never contribute to `best`. The bound keeps a hostile repository from forcing unbounded miss-driven fetching: past the bound the client suspends fail-closed, exactly as if the repository withheld everything. No new decision codes; pin unchanged 2035. Honest residual: prune windows wider than 32 consecutive slots still suspend (fail-closed, no regression -- the same as the old behavior), and the warned-skip path for non-verifying slots remains unbounded (pre-existing; a malicious repository serving infinite old-key-signed versions was already an infinite loop before this change).

**Verification:** T4c/T4d flip to HELD (bootstrap recovers to timestamp v5 on pruned/gapped repositories; a second cycle stays trusted), T4a/T4b stay HELD (contiguous recovery; planted sub-floor new-key-signed v1 still refused coded pre-rotation rollback), full w326 battery 18/0/0 held/break/error, `tests/test_bundle_refresh_audit.py` 14/14 OK (`F410KnownIssueTest` rewritten as `F410RegressionTest` pinning recovery + a miss-bound suspension test), `tests/test_bundle_refresh` 29/29 OK, adjacent supply-chain batteries zero-delta (w267 20/0/0, w326_standing 0/14/0, w326_sched 0/18/0).

**Reproduction** (both probes in `evals/w326_tufaudit_probes.py`): establish a trusted chain (root v1, timestamp v1..v3 under the old key). Publish a trust-changing root rotation (root v2: root key a->rk3, timestamp key ts->tk2, dual-signed old 2-of-2 AND new 2-of-2). Publish timestamp v4, v5 under the NEW key and remove the old v1..v3 slots (T4c), or remove just the v3 slot leaving v1, v2 (old key), v4, v5 (new key) (T4d). `refresh()` adopts root v2, drops the chain, and enters `_bootstrap_timestamp_post_rotation`, which scans timestamp slots from v1 and `break`s on the first `FetchNotFound`. T4c: slot v1 is gone -> break with `best=None` -> `_ChainBreak("post-rotation: no timestamp version verifies under the new root; cannot complete the chain")` -> state `suspended`. T4d: slots v1, v2 fail the new-root signature check (skipped), slot v3 is gone -> break before v4/v5 are ever fetched -> same `_ChainBreak` -> `suspended`. A second `refresh()` repeats the identical scan and suspends again: the client can never recover on its own.

**Why this matters:** the scan's `break`-on-first-miss assumes the repository serves a contiguous version sequence starting at v1. Nothing in the TUF model requires a repository to retain old versions — and after a key compromise (the exact Mercury-style scenario fast-forward recovery exists for), an operator pruning compromised-key metadata is plausible. The pre-rotation rollback floor already rejects anything below the old version, so slots v1..floor-1 are useless to the scan anyway; requiring their existence is pure liveness cost. The failure is fail-closed (suspended, serves nothing) but it is permanent and fleet-wide: every client that held the pre-rotation chain wedges at the same rotation.

**Close-when:** the post-rotation bootstrap finds the highest version >= the pre-rotation floor that verifies under the new root without requiring v1 (or any contiguous prefix) to exist. Candidate fixes: (a) start the scan at `max(1, floor)` instead of 1; (b) continue past `FetchNotFound` with a bounded consecutive-miss limit instead of breaking on the first miss. After the fix, T4c/T4d must flip to HELD (bootstrap recovers to timestamp v5), T4a/T4b must stay HELD (contiguous recovery and floor enforcement), and the full w326 battery must go 0 BREAK / 18 HELD / 0 ERROR.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Availability-only and fail-closed — no trust is compromised, the client suspends loudly rather than accepting bad metadata. Requires a trust-changing root rotation (rare, operator-driven) plus a repository that does not retain a contiguous timestamp history from v1. MEDIUM was rejected because there is no bypass, no silent acceptance, and no data exposure; HIGH was never in play.

## F411: Federated-mode mint_identity accepts an unverified dict token_claims, bypassing token authentication (MEDIUM, CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-327 lane 1) [renumbered F410->F411 at the wave-326 merge per the wave-272 earliest-filed rule: lane 4 filed F410 at 11:19:59 UTC, lane 5 at 11:29:45 UTC]

**Cells:** wave-326 independent red team (lane 5), claim 2026-10-04T12:00:00Z.

`ToolExecutor.mint_identity` with `token_verifier` configured (wave-325 federated identity, dex pattern) refuses tokenless mints (`identity-token-required`) and verifies string tokens against the deployment's pinned issuers -- but a `dict` `token_claims` takes "the legacy path unchanged" (`gov/executor.py`: "A dict token_claims takes the legacy path unchanged"): it is trusted as pre-verified and only shape-checked by `decision_packet.check_token_claims`, which explicitly does NOT verify signatures ("It does NOT check the JWT signature -- the caller presents the VERIFIED claim set"). `TokenVerifier.verify_token` returns a plain dict with no authenticity marker, so the executor cannot distinguish a verified dict from a forged one. Any in-process caller can therefore mint any identity -- arbitrary agent_id/role/principal, arbitrary agent_scope -- without holding a valid token. The wave-325 lane-2 battery probed only the string path and tokenless refusal, never the dict path in federated mode. The sibling seam is sound: `verify_decision_packet`'s token-consistency check binds presented claims to the packet's signed identity_token section (iss/aud/exp/jti), so a forged dict cannot pass packet verification -- but the minted identity itself, and the forged claims stored in `_mcp_token_claims` that feed the MCP required-scope check (`authority_proof.check_against_boundary`), are fully attacker-controlled.

**Reproduction:** configure `ToolExecutor(..., token_verifier=v)` with a pinned issuer; call `mint_identity("attacker-agent", "admin", "victim-principal", token_claims={"iss": <pinned>, "sub": "attacker-agent", "aud": "sasanam-policy-engine", "iat": now, "exp": now+300, "jti": "x", "principal": "victim-principal", "role": "admin", "agent_scope": "all"})` -- no signature anywhere: the mint succeeds (break-first verified 2026-10-04 on the wave-325 tree). A forged *string* token is correctly refused coded `identity-token-tampered`. Standing probe `P3a-f411-dict-token-claims-bypass` in `evals/w326_redteam_probes.py` (expected BREAK).

**Close-when:** in federated mode (`token_verifier` set), `mint_identity` must not honor an unverified dict: either refuse dict `token_claims` with a coded error directing the caller to pass the token string (so the executor verifies it), or accept only a non-forgeable verified-claims type produced by the executor's own verifier. The standing P3a probe must flip to HELD (forged dict raises `IdentityTokenError`, identity not minted); the string-token end-to-end mint (P3l) and tokenless refusal (P3m) must stay HELD; non-federated mode byte-identical. No new decision codes from this lane.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Authentication bypass in a security feature: the deployment configures `token_verifier` believing issuance is token-gated, but any in-process caller defeats the gate with a forged dict. Requires in-process code execution (the executor hosts partially-trusted components such as bridges); not remotely exploitable; no direct data exfiltration.

## F412 — LOW — Standing-verdict conflict resolution is not atomic: a crash between the two journal appends permanently wedges the store (Wave 327)

**Cells:** wave-327 independent red team (lane 4), claim 2026-10-04T12:45:00Z.

`StandingStore._resolve_conflict` (`gov/standing_verdicts.py`) journals a conflict in TWO appends: first the `conflict` record, then the winner's `knowledge` record. A crash between them leaves the `conflict` entry as the journal tip. On reload, `_replay` sets `_tips[digest]` to the conflict seq -- and a `conflict` entry has no `asserted_standing` field. Both `standing_of` and `attach_knowledge` then raise an UNCODED `KeyError: 'asserted_standing'` (direct dict indexing, no coded fail-closed path). The store is permanently wedged: every reload replays the same poisoned tip, no advisory can ever be attached again, and the journaled "resolution" never took effect (the winner's knowledge was lost). Recovery requires manual journal surgery.

**Reproduction:** register an artifact; attach trusted knowledge (seq 1), then quarantined knowledge superseding it (seq 2); append a `conflict` entry directly (simulating the crash between `_resolve_conflict`'s two `_append` calls); reload the store from the journal. `standing_of(digest)` raises `KeyError: 'asserted_standing'`; `attach_knowledge` with a legitimate justified flip raises the same. Standing probe `P1f-f412-conflict-crash-wedges-store` in `evals/w327_redteam_probes.py` (expected BREAK).

**Why this matters:** the standing-verdict store is the trust-standing authority for the supply-chain layer. A wedged store cannot record new knowledge -- including the revocation that a conflict was trying to apply. The failure is fail-loud (no silent acceptance, no trust bypass) but it is permanent until an operator hand-edits the journal, and the crash window sits exactly on the concurrent-advisory path (the normal operating mode of a live feed, where races are most likely).

**Close-when:** the conflict resolution becomes atomic -- either journal the conflict record and the winner's knowledge as a SINGLE journal entry, or add load-time recovery (if the tip is a `conflict` entry, complete the resolution from its journaled winner fields), and both `standing_of` and `attach_knowledge` must fail with a CODED error (never a bare `KeyError`) on any unexpected journal shape. After the fix, P1f must flip to HELD (crash-window recovers or refuses coded), the full w327 battery must go 0 BREAK / 32 HELD / 0 ERROR, and the conflict/journal unit tests must cover the crash-window.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Availability-only: no trust is compromised, no silent acceptance, the failure is loud. Requires a process crash (power loss, OOM kill, SIGKILL) landing in the microsecond window between two adjacent appends -- narrow, though the window sits on the contended path. Recovery is manual but possible.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-328 lane 1.** `_resolve_conflict` now journals the conflict record and the winner's knowledge as a SINGLE journal entry (one `_append`: one write + fsync) -- there is no crash window between two appends. The entry carries the winner's full knowledge fields (`asserted_standing`, `origin`, `collector`, `known_since`, `supersedes`) alongside the conflict metadata (`winner_*`/`loser_*`), so it is a valid tip and the chain stays linear. `_replay` validates the knowledge payload of single-entry conflict records via `_check_knowledge`; legacy two-append conflict records (pre-F412 journals) deliberately do NOT move the tip -- if the crash landed between the two appends, the tip stays at the pre-conflict knowledge and the store recovers instead of wedging (the conflict remains in the audit trail). Both `standing_of` and `attach_knowledge` refuse coded `supplychain-standing-journal-corrupt` (never a bare `KeyError`) if a tip entry is ever not a valid knowledge record. P1f flips to HELD (crash-window recovers cleanly). +1 code (`supplychain-standing-journal-corrupt`), pin 2044 -> 2045.

## F413 — LOW — Policy-channel feed iteration orders by filename, not version: an in-window update is skipped when a higher multi-digit version is refused, and an intermediate version's revocations are silently dropped (Wave 328)

**Cells:** wave-328 independent red team (lane 4), claim 2026-10-04T14:05:00Z.

`_feed_files()` in `gov/policy_channel.py` (new in wave-327) iterates `sorted(os.listdir(...))` -- lexicographic FILENAME order -- while its own docstring promises "`(version, name)` pairs for this policy, **sorted by version**". Observed on the base tree: a feed holding `pol.v1.json`, `pol.v10.json`, `pol.v2.json` returns `[(1, 'pol.v1.json'), (10, 'pol.v10.json'), (2, 'pol.v2.json')]`. Two integrity-relevant manifestations, one root cause:

(a) Delayed update (fail-closed, loud). Feed `{v1, v2, v10}`, agent floor at v1, `max_skip=4`: the poll tries v10 first, refuses it coded `policy-channel-version-skip`, and STOPS the poll -- the valid in-window v2 is never applied and the agent stays on v1 even though an applicable, properly-signed update sat in the feed. Reproduced: `poll report: applied=False version=None code=policy-channel-version-skip current=1`.

(b) Silently dropped revocation. Feed `{v9 (revokes=[12]), v10}`, floor at v8: v10 applies first, v9 is skipped with a bare `continue` (no report note, no warning), `revoked_versions` stays `[]` -- and a later validly-signed v12 APPLIES even though the publisher revoked it in v9. Reproduced: after poll `current=10 revoked=[]`, then `v12 APPLIED -- v9's revocation was silently dropped`. The `continue` makes the skip invisible in the poll report (the report names only the applied version).

The failure is never a trust bypass of the signature itself (unsigned, non-canonical, and replayed versions are all refused coded -- P1a/P1e/P1f HELD), but the version-application policy is not what its docstring says: publication order by filename is not semantic order by version.

**Reproduction:** standing probes `P1b-f413-feed-version-ordering` and `P1c-f413-intermediate-revocation-recorded` in `evals/w328_redteam_probes.py` (both expected BREAK on the base tree).

**Why this matters:** the policy channel is the remote governance-update path. A publisher that jumps versions (pruned feed, late-arriving publisher -- the same conditions as F410) can leave the fleet on a stale policy while the update sits unread in the feed, or worse, leave a revocation unenforced while the revoked policy later installs cleanly. Both outcomes are invisible in normal operation: (a) looks like a routine version-skip refusal, (b) is entirely silent.

**Close-when:** `_feed_files` returns `(version, name)` pairs sorted numerically by VERSION (matching its docstring); P1b flips to HELD (feed `{v1, v2, v10}`, floor v1: v2 applied, then v10 refused coded `policy-channel-version-skip`); P1c flips to HELD (feed `{v9 (revokes=[12]), v10}`, floor v8: `revoked_versions` contains 12 after the poll, and a later v12 refuses coded `policy-channel-revoked`); existing single-digit-feed behavior is unchanged (w327_polchan battery stays 0/18/0).

**Severity rationale:** LOW. The primary manifestation is fail-closed and loud (a coded refusal, no trust compromise); the revocation case requires the publisher to publish with version jumps and an intermediate revocation -- the pruned-feed conditions of F410 -- and the channel's signature checks are intact throughout. No new decision codes needed.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-329 lane 1.**

## F414 — LOW — Shamir distribute() pre-flight is defeated by path aliases: a symlink-aliasing assignment pair passes the distinct-paths check, the write loop refuses LOUD on the second write, but the first shard is already on disk (Wave 329)

**Cells:** wave-329 independent red team (lane 3), claim 2026-10-04T16:20:00Z.

`distribute()` in `gov/shamir_custody.py` (new in wave-328) promises: "an existing file at any target refuses the whole distribution before anything is written." The pre-flight compares `os.path.abspath()` spellings, which do not resolve symlinks. Two assignment paths that name the same file through a symlink (`/real/shard` and `/link/shard` where `/link` -> `/real`) are abspath-distinct, so the pre-flight passes; the write loop then refuses the second write coded `custody-shamir-distribute-refused` -- but the first shard has already been written 0600 to the shared file. Reproduced: after the coded refusal, the real directory contains `['shard']` -- a partial distribution.

The failure is fail-closed and loud (the refusal is coded, the shard is 0600, no manifest is returned, no silent state), and the trust model is unaffected: a partial distribution still needs t custodians to reconstruct. What breaks is the documented atomicity guarantee: the operator is told nothing was written when one shard was. The same alias class (hard links, bind mounts, case-insensitive filesystems) is not covered either.

**Reproduction:** standing probe `P1h-shamir-distribute-symlink-alias-partial-write` in `evals/w329_redteam_probes.py` (expected BREAK on the base tree).

**Close-when:** `distribute` resolves assignment paths with `os.path.realpath` (or equivalent) before the distinctness and existence pre-flight, so an aliased pair refuses before anything is written; P1h flips to HELD; `w328_shamir` battery stays 0/36/0. No new decision codes needed.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed and loud throughout; the only casualty is the documented all-or-nothing distribution guarantee. An operator who retries after the loud refusal must clean up the stray shard first, and the stray shard is visible in the target directory.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-330 lane 1:** `distribute` resolves assignment paths with `os.path.realpath` before the distinctness and existence pre-flight (unresolvable paths refuse coded); a (device, inode, basename) check on parent directories covers directory-level aliases realpath cannot see (bind mounts). An aliased pair now refuses coded `custody-shamir-distribute-refused` before anything is written; P1h flips to HELD; the case-insensitive-filesystem residual is documented LOUD in the docstring. No new codes, pin unchanged 2058.

## F415 — LOW — Policy-channel _feed_files crashes uncoded on unicode-digit version filenames (Wave 330)

**Cells:** wave-330 independent red team (lane 3), claim 2026-10-04T19:05:00Z.

`_feed_files()` in `gov/policy_channel.py` gates the version fragment with `str.isdigit()` and then calls `int()` directly. `isdigit()` admits Unicode digits that `int()` rejects (e.g. U+00B2 SUPERSCRIPT TWO: `"²".isdigit()` is True, `int("²")` raises `ValueError`). A feed file named `pol.v².json` passes the gate; `int(mid)` then raises a BARE `ValueError` that escapes `poll()` -- which catches only `PolicyChannelError`. Any feed-dir writer (no signing key needed) can crash every poll: loud and fail-closed, but UNCODED, violating the coded-refusal discipline (F412-class). Reproduced: standing probe `P1g-policy-channel-unicode-version-uncoded` in `evals/w330_redteam_probes.py` (expected BREAK on the base tree). The >4300-digit variant of the same class is not reachable through this seam (NAME_MAX caps the fragment well below the int() digit limit).

**Reproduction:** place `pol.v².json` (any bytes) in the feed dir alongside a valid `pol.v1.json`; `poll()` raises bare `ValueError: invalid literal for int()`.

**Close-when:** the version-fragment parse is made total -- ASCII-digit check (or try/except around `int()`) refusing coded `policy-channel-malformed`; P1g flips to HELD; `w327_polchan` stays 0/18/0. No new decision codes needed.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed and loud (exception, never an acceptance); no integrity violation. The impact is a poll DoS by anyone able to write a file into the feed directory.

**Status: OPEN.**

## F416 — LOW — Sigstore-bundle witness time/index parsing crashes uncoded on over-long digit strings (Wave 330)

**Cells:** wave-330 independent red team (lane 3), claim 2026-10-04T19:06:00Z.

`_check_witness()` in `gov/evidence_sigstore.py` gates `integratedTime` and `logIndex` on `str.isdigit()` and then calls `int()` directly. A >4300-digit string passes the gate; `int()` raises the digit-limit `ValueError` -- bare, uncoded, escaping `open_sigstore_bundle()`. The `integratedTime` conversion happens BEFORE the witness SET is verified, so ANY bundle presenter triggers it -- and the offline verifier's threat model explicitly includes hostile bundles. The `logIndex` conversion (at the inclusionProof branch) crashes the same way behind a valid SET/checkpoint. Reproduced: standing probes `P1a-evidence-sigstore-integratedtime-digitlimit-uncoded` and `P1b-evidence-sigstore-logindex-digitlimit-uncoded` in `evals/w330_redteam_probes.py` (expected BREAK on the base tree). Same defect class as F415, different emission site.

**Close-when:** both conversions are made total (length-bounded digit check or try/except) refusing coded `evidence-bundle-malformed`; P1a/P1b flip to HELD; `w329_sigb` stays 0/22/0 and `test_evidence_sigstore` stays green. No new decision codes needed.

**Severity rationale:** LOW. Fail-closed and loud (exception, never a false 'Verified OK'); no signature or witness binding is bypassed. The impact is a verify-path DoS: a hostile bundle crashes the verifier instead of being refused coded.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-04 wave-331 lane 2.** `_check_witness()` now verifies the witness SET (logId binding, canonicalizedBody binding, SET signature) BEFORE `integratedTime`/`logIndex` are converted or trusted, and both conversions go through the TOTAL `_parse_int64_as_string()` (ASCII digits only, length-bounded to 20 chars before `int()`, coded `evidence-bundle-malformed` on anything else); a bare `ValueError` can never escape. P1a/P1b flip to HELD (coded refusal); `w329_sigb` 0/22/0 and `test_evidence_sigstore` green. No new codes, pin unchanged 2058.

## F417 — LOW — gov/mcp_oauth_binding._normalize_url escapes a non-numeric URL port as a bare ValueError (Wave 333)

**Cells:** wave-333 independent red-team (lane 5), claim 2026-10-05.

`gov/mcp_oauth_binding._normalize_url` crashes uncoded on a non-numeric URL port: `port = parts.port` raises `ValueError` before the `isinstance(port, (int, type(None)))` guard below it ever runs (dead code). Attacker-influenced inputs all funnel through it -- rogue-AS authorization-response `iss`, presented token `aud`/`resource` claims, `issuer_hint` -- so a rogue AS can crash the client with a bare `ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as 'badport'` instead of the coded `mcp-oauth-metadata-malformed` refusal the module promises ("Fail closed on shape").

## F418 — MEDIUM — Revocation is decision-time-only; in-flight sessions have no kill channel (Wave 333)

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-05 wave-333 lane 4.** New `gov/revocation_push.py`: CAEP/SSF-shaped revocation-event intake (typed envelope: event_id / event_type URIs / subject / issued_at, HMAC-signed by default); subject->session index with EXACT (kind,id) matching; synchronous fan-out that calls each bound session's kill callback and then confirms via an optional liveness probe -- a raising callback or a still-alive liveness report SUSPENDS the session fail-closed (never silently continued); `require_live()` is the per-step gate (unknown sessions refuse); replays are idempotent (original receipt, `revocation-push-event-replayed`, callbacks fire once); +8 `revocation-push-*` codes centrally registered, pin 2062 -> 2070. ## F419 — LOW — No server-side per-request bearer-token guard; token-passthrough ban unenforced on the serving side (Wave 334)

**Cells:** wave-334 MCP server-authz lane (lane 2), claim 2026-10-05.

The wave-332 MCP OAuth hardening is client-side only: `gov/mcp_oauth_binding.check_token_resource` refuses `mcp-oauth-resource-misbound` when *the client* is about to present a token at the wrong server, and its authenticity boundary explicitly requires the caller to have verified the token signature. A deployment serving MCP tools over HTTP therefore has no gov-provided gate to call: a token minted for resource A presented at a server guarding resource B is never refused server-side (accept-by-absence), and no 401 challenge path exists. This is the server-side half of the wave-332 client work (w333 prospectus STEAL #1; MCP Authorization spec: servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience, RFC 8707 Section 2, and MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens).

**Reproduction:** `/tmp/red_mcpsrv.py` on base `a40c2ef4` → `F419-RED: ACCEPT-BY-ABSENCE -- token minted for resource A presented at resource B is never refused server-side; no 401 path exists in gov/.`

**Severity rationale:** LOW. No in-tree server accepts bearer tokens today (the in-tree MCP surface is client/executor-side -- `gov/adapters/mcp_adapter.py` calls out to a real MCP server, never serves), so there is no live in-tree exploit path; the exposure is at deployment wiring, where any MCP server built on the stack inherits the accept-by-absence. Same "missing enforcement point" class as F418 (filed+closed same lane).

**Status: CLOSED 2026-10-05 wave-334 lane 2.** New `gov/mcp_server_authz.py`: per-request bearer-token guard -- `validate_bearer_request(resource_server, authorization_header, verify_fn, *, expected_issuer, ...)` enforces, in order: token-in-query refusal, Authorization header shape, deployment verifier acceptance, time window (exp/nbf), issuer (exact match), resource binding (RFC 8707, wired through `check_token_resource` and remapped into the `mcp-server-auth-*` domain), scope; every failure raises coded `McpServerAuthzError` mapped to HTTP 401 (403 only for `mcp-server-auth-insufficient-scope`); `www_authenticate_challenge` builds the RFC 6750 challenge (error_description carries the machine code, never token bytes; header-injection characters stripped); `refusal_response` returns the (status, challenge) pair. +11 `mcp-server-auth-*` codes centrally registered, pin 2077 -> 2088.
